Benefits: Constant cable tension throughout the squat; Builds quad-dominant squatting; No barbell needed — useful in some commercial gyms; Front-loaded position forces upright torso; Easy to load progressively via cable stack; Provides unique stimulus
Muscles Worked (Raw): Quadriceps (heavy emphasis); Gluteus maximus; Anterior deltoid (handle support); Core (bracing); Hamstrings; Calves

Description: Attach a low cable to a belt around your waist (or hold a handle at your chest). Stand facing away from the cable in front of a sturdy box. Step forward to add tension to the cable. Place one foot fully on the box. Lean your torso forward over the working leg. Drive through the heel of the working foot to step up onto the box. Squeeze the glute hard at the top. Step back down with control. Complete reps on one side before switching.
Benefits: Glute-focused step up; Constant cable tension; Builds single-leg glute strength; Reduces quad dominance; Useful for glute hypertrophy; Improves hip extension power
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus maximus; Hamstrings; Quadriceps

Description: Attach a rope handle to a low cable pulley. Stand facing the cable. Grip both ends of the rope and hold it at your chest like a goblet. Step back to create cable tension. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart. Brace your core hard. The cable will pull you forward — resist this throughout. Sit back and down into a squat. Keep your torso upright. Descend until thighs are parallel or deeper. Drive through your feet to stand back up. The cable resistance peaks at the standing position. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Benefits: Constant cable tension throughout the squat; Resistance peaks at standing (opposite of free weights); Trains anti-tip core stability; Useful when no dumbbells or kettlebells are available; Easy to load progressively; Beginner-friendly squat variation
Muscles Worked (Raw): Quadriceps; Gluteus maximus; Hamstrings (secondary); Core (anti-extension, stabilizer); Upper back (isometric)

Description: Set a cable to chest height with a single handle. Half kneel with your right knee on the floor and left foot planted in front. Position yourself perpendicular to the cable with the cable on your right side. Grip the handle with both hands at chest level. Brace your core hard against the lateral pull. Press the handle straight out from your chest until your arms are extended. Hold the press while resisting the cable pull. Bring the handle back to your chest with control. Complete reps, switch sides and stance.
Benefits: Combines anti-rotation core with hip stability; Builds core stability under lateral force; Strong oblique engagement; Half kneeling challenges hip control; Useful for athletes who need core stability; Constant cable tension through the range
Muscles Worked (Raw): Obliques (internal and external); Rectus abdominis; Quadratus lumborum; Gluteus medius

Exercise Name: Cable Half Kneeling Adductor Pallof Press
Description: Set a cable to chest height and stand to one side of the machine. Get into a half kneeling position with the inside knee down. Squeeze a small ball or pad between your knees. Hold the handle at chest level with both hands. Brace your core hard. Press the handle straight out from your chest to full extension. Resist the cable pulling you toward the machine. Pause briefly, then bring the handle slowly back to your chest.
Benefits: Trains anti-rotation core; Adds adductor activation; Builds inner thigh strength; Improves trunk stability; Useful for athletes; Strengthens hip stabilizers
Muscles Worked (Raw): Obliques; Adductors; Rectus abdominis; Transverse abdominis

Description: Attach a rope handle to a low cable pulley. Stand facing the cable machine with feet hip-width apart. Grip both ends of the rope with a neutral grip — palms facing each other. Step back slightly so the cable is under tension at the start position. Stand tall with the rope ends hanging at your thighs. Pull your shoulders back, brace your core, and pin your elbows against your sides. Curl the rope up by bending only at the elbows. Keep your wrists in the neutral position throughout. Continue until your hands are at shoulder height. Squeeze hard for one second at the top. Lower the rope under control over two to three seconds back to the start position. Maintain constant tension on the cable — do not let the weight stack touch down between reps.
Benefits: Constant cable tension throughout the entire range of motion; Heavily targets the brachialis and brachioradialis; Easier on the wrists than supinated cable curls; Easier to load progressively with small increments than dumbbells; Excellent for high-rep bicep and forearm finishing work; Trains grip strength through the rope hold
Muscles Worked (Raw): Brachialis; Brachioradialis; Biceps brachii; Forearm flexors; Anterior deltoid (minor stabilizer)

Description: Set two cables at chest height with single handles. Drop into a half kneeling position between the cables. Grip one handle behind in one hand and the other in front. Brace your core hard with the torso upright. Press the front handle forward to extension. At the same time pull the back handle to the body. Squeeze the chest forward and back at end range. Reverse to the start with control. Complete reps and switch.
Benefits: Combo press and row move; Trains anti-rotation core; Builds chest and back together; Strong functional pattern; Useful upper body move; Builds core stability
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Latissimus dorsi; Core; Anterior deltoid

Description: Set a cable to the lowest setting and attach a single handle. Drop into a half kneeling position perpendicular to the cable. Grip the handle with the outside hand. Tuck the elbow tight against the side at 90 degrees. Brace your core and keep the torso upright. Externally rotate the forearm out to the side. Squeeze the rotator cuff at the end range. Rotate back to the start with control. Complete reps and switch sides.
Benefits: Strong rotator cuff builder; Trains shoulder health; Half kneeling stance braces the body; Useful pre-pressing move; Builds shoulder stability; Strong rehab move
Muscles Worked (Raw): Posterior deltoid; Rotator cuff; Rhomboids

Exercise Name: Cable High Pulley Overhead Tricep Extension
Description: Attach a rope handle to a high cable pulley. Grip both ends of the rope with a neutral grip (palms facing each other). Step forward and turn around so you are facing away from the cable. Bring the rope up and behind your head, with your elbows pointing forward and bent at roughly 90 degrees. Stagger your stance for stability — one foot slightly forward. Lean your torso forward slightly. Brace your core. Pin your upper arms in place — they should not move during the rep, only your forearms. Extend at the elbows to push the rope up and forward overhead. As you reach lockout, separate your hands slightly to spread the rope ends. Squeeze your triceps hard for one second at lockout. Slowly let the rope travel back down behind your head over two to three seconds. Feel a deep stretch in your triceps.
Benefits: Targets the long head of the triceps under deep stretch; Constant cable tension throughout the entire range of motion; Loaded stretching drives effective muscle growth; Easier on the elbows than barbell overhead extensions; Excellent finisher for tricep workouts; Easy to load progressively in small increments
Muscles Worked (Raw): Triceps brachii (especially the long head); Anconeus; Anterior deltoid (isometric); Core (stabilizer)

Description: Attach an ankle strap to a low cable. Strap it around your right ankle. Stand sideways to the cable with the working leg closest to the cable. Hold the frame for balance. Pull your right leg across your body to the left against the cable tension. Continue until your right leg crosses past your left. Squeeze your inner thigh at the end position. Slowly return to start. Complete reps, then switch legs. Aim for 12 to 15 reps per side.
Benefits: Isolates the adductors with constant cable tension; Easy to load progressively; Helps prevent groin strains; Builds hip strength balance; Adjustable cable resistance; Useful for athletic training
Muscles Worked (Raw): Adductor magnus, longus, brevis; Gracilis; Pectineus

Description: Set an incline bench facing away from a low cable station. Attach a single handle or short bar to a low cable pulley. Lie back on the incline bench with the cable behind you. Grip the handle with an underhand grip and let your arm hang behind you. Pin your shoulder back against the bench. Curl the handle up by bending only at the elbow. Continue until your forearm is roughly vertical. Squeeze your bicep at the top, then lower with control to the stretched position.
Benefits: Constant cable tension through the range; Strong stretch on the bicep at the bottom; Eliminates body english; Builds bicep size at the long head; Different stimulus than standard incline curls; Useful for hypertrophy training
Muscles Worked (Raw): Biceps brachii (long head); Brachialis; Brachioradialis

Description: Set a cable to the highest pulley with a rope or bar attachment. Stand facing away from the cable station. Grip the attachment behind your head with both hands. Step forward and bend slightly at the hips. Position your elbows pointing forward and tucked next to your head. Brace your core. Extend your elbows to push the attachment forward and away. Squeeze the triceps at the top, then return to the starting position.
Benefits: Strong stretch on triceps long head; Constant cable tension through the range; Different angle than tricep pushdowns; Builds tricep size; Useful for hypertrophy training; Strong peak contraction
Muscles Worked (Raw): Triceps brachii (long head); Triceps brachii (medial and lateral heads); Anconeus

Description: Position an incline bench at about 30 to 45 degrees in front of a low cable pulley. Lie face down on the bench with chest supported and arms hanging over the top. Grip a single bar or two single handles attached to the low cable. Allow your arms to fully extend toward the cable with tension active. Brace your core and pull your shoulders back. Row the cable handle up by driving your elbows back. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top. Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position with control.
Benefits: Strict rowing with no body english; Chest support eliminates lower back stress; Constant cable tension through the range; Builds back size and thickness; Strong lat and rhomboid engagement; Useful for hypertrophy training
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi; Rhomboids; Trapezius (middle and lower); Biceps brachii; Posterior deltoid

Description: Set an incline bench facing away from a low cable station. Attach a short bar or rope to a low cable pulley. Lie back on the incline bench with the cable behind you. Grip the attachment with a close underhand grip. Allow your arms to hang behind your body in a fully stretched position. Pin your shoulders back against the bench. Curl the attachment up by bending only at the elbows. Squeeze your biceps at the top, then lower with control to the stretched position.
Benefits: Targets long head of biceps; Strong stretch from incline angle; Close grip emphasizes outer arm; Constant cable tension; Useful for hypertrophy training; Builds bicep peak
Muscles Worked (Raw): Biceps brachii (long head); Brachialis; Brachioradialis

Description: Set an adjustable bench to roughly 30 to 45 degrees and place it between two cable stations with low pulleys. Attach a single-handle (D-handle) to each low pulley. Sit on the bench, grab one handle in each hand, and lie back. The cables should run upward from the floor to your hands. Plant both feet firmly on the floor. Pull your shoulders down and back, lift your chest. Start with the handles held out to your sides at roughly chest height, with arms slightly bent. The cables should be under tension at the start. Brace your core. Bring both handles together in a wide arc up over your upper chest, ending with the handles touching above your sternum. Squeeze your chest hard for one second at the top. Maintain the slight elbow bend throughout. Lower the handles under control over two to three seconds back to the starting position. Feel the stretch in your upper chest.
Benefits: Targets the upper (clavicular) chest with constant cable tension; Long range of motion with a deep stretch at the bottom; Excellent for building upper-chest size when added to incline pressing; Easier on the shoulders than dumbbell incline flys for many lifters; Constant tension drives effective hypertrophy; Easy to load in small increments
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major (especially the clavicular/upper head); Anterior deltoid (secondary); Biceps brachii (stabilizer); Serratus anterior

Description: Set an incline bench between two low cable pulleys. Lie face-down on the bench with feet on the floor. Reach down and grab the right cable with your left hand and the left cable with your right hand. Start with the cables crossed under your chest. Brace your core and pin your chest to the bench. Sweep your arms out and back to your sides. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end range. Return slowly to the crossed position.
Benefits: Strict rear delt isolation; Constant cable tension; No momentum or torso swing; Bench-supported for strict form; Builds rear delt detail; Useful for shoulder balance
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rear deltoid; Rhomboids; Traps

Description: Set an incline bench in front of a low cable pulley. Attach a rope handle to the low pulley. Sit on the bench facing away from the cable and lie back. Reach overhead and grab the rope with both hands. Start with arms extended over your forehead. Bend at the elbows to lower the rope behind your head. Keep your upper arms still and only the elbows moving. Extend the elbows to return to the start position.
Benefits: Constant cable tension on the triceps; Stretches the long head of the triceps; Builds mass in the triceps long head; Reduces wrist strain compared to barbell; Improves elbow extension strength; Excellent triceps isolation
Muscles Worked (Raw): Triceps brachii (long head); Triceps brachii (lateral head); Triceps brachii (medial head)

Description: Set an incline bench (30 to 45 degrees) facing away from a high cable. Attach a straight bar or rope. Lie face up on the incline bench. Grip the bar overhead. Start with elbows bent, bar behind your head. Push the bar forward and down by extending at the elbows. Lock out in front of your chest. Squeeze your triceps. Slowly let the bar return behind your head. Keep upper arms still. Aim for 12 to 15 reps per set.
Benefits: Different resistance angle than standing pushdowns; Emphasizes the tricep long head; Constant cable tension; Incline position prevents cheating; Easy to load progressively; Useful for tricep hypertrophy
Muscles Worked (Raw): Triceps brachii (long head emphasis); Anconeus

Description: Set a cable pulley to chest height. Attach a D-handle. Stand sideways to the cable. Grip the handle with both hands at your chest. Step away from the cable until there is tension. Brace your core hard. Maintain square hips and shoulders. Press the handle straight forward by extending your arms. The cable pulls you to rotate — resist and maintain square position. Hold at full extension for 2 to 3 seconds. Pull the handle back to your chest. Repeat 10 to 12 reps per side.
Benefits: Gold-standard anti-rotation core exercise; Builds deep core stability; Develops oblique and TVA strength; Easy to load progressively; Functional core training; Carries over to all rotational sports
Muscles Worked (Raw): Obliques (anti-rotation); Transverse abdominis; Rectus abdominis; Erector spinae; Gluteus medius (hip stabilizer)

Description: Set a cable to a high position. Attach a rope handle. Kneel facing away from the cable. Hold the rope behind your head near your ears. Start upright (tall kneeling). Core braced. Crunch downward by flexing your spine — drive your elbows toward your knees. Squeeze your abs hard at the bottom. Slowly return to the upright position. The movement comes from spinal flexion, not hip flexion. Use moderate to heavy weight. Aim for 12 to 15 reps.
Benefits: Classic heavy loaded ab exercise; Allows progressive overload for ab thickness; Constant cable tension; Excellent for ab hypertrophy; Simple setup; Gym staple exercise
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Obliques; Hip flexors (slight)

Description: Set a cable to the lowest pulley with a single handle. Stand facing the cable station with feet shoulder-width apart. Bend forward at the hips with a flat back. Grip the handle in your right hand with palm facing your body. Pin your right upper arm against your side, parallel to the floor. Brace your core and pull your shoulders back. Extend your right elbow back to straighten the arm fully. Squeeze the tricep at the top, then return to the starting position. Switch arms.
Benefits: Constant cable tension through the range; Strict tricep isolation; Different angle than standard kickback; Builds tricep size; Strong peak contraction; Useful for hypertrophy training
Muscles Worked (Raw): Triceps brachii (long head); Triceps brachii (lateral head); Anconeus

Description: Attach an ankle strap to the low cable pulley and to one ankle. Get on all fours with the cable to your working side. Position your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips. Brace your core to keep a flat back. Lift the working leg out to the side, keeping the knee bent at 90 degrees. Raise the leg until the thigh is parallel to the floor. Squeeze the side glute at the top. Lower slowly to the start. Complete reps on one side before switching.
Benefits: Isolates the gluteus medius; Improves hip stability; Sculpts the side glutes; Constant cable tension throughout; Useful for hip strengthening; Reduces lower back loading
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus medius; Gluteus maximus; Hips

Description: Set an incline bench at 45 to 60 degrees facing away from a low cable pulley. Attach a straight bar or rope. Sit on the bench. Reach back and grip the attachment. Press it overhead. Pin your upper arms next to your head. Elbows point straight up. Lower the attachment behind your head by bending at the elbows. Feel the deep stretch. Extend back to lockout by contracting your triceps. Keep upper arms still. Maintain cable tension throughout — do not let slack develop. Repeat for the desired number of reps. The incline position increases the stretch vs flat or standing versions.
Benefits: Deep long-head stretch with constant cable tension; Incline position increases stretch vs standing/flat versions; Excellent for tricep hypertrophy; Easy to load progressively; Combines the best of incline position and cable tension; Back-supported position allows focus on the triceps
Muscles Worked (Raw): Triceps brachii (especially the long head); Anconeus

Description: Set a cable pulley to a high position. Attach a rope or single handle. Stand sideways to the cable with feet shoulder-width apart. Grip the handle with both hands. Start with arms extended above your head toward the cable. Pull the cable diagonally across your body from high to low — like a judo throw. Rotate your torso, drive through your hips, and finish with the handle near your opposite knee. Control the cable back to the starting position over two seconds. Complete reps on one side, then switch sides. Use moderate weight. Aim for 10 to 12 reps per side.
Benefits: Builds explosive rotational power; Targets the obliques heavily; Carries over to martial arts and rotational sports; Constant cable tension throughout; Easy to load progressively; Trains hip-to-shoulder force transfer
Muscles Worked (Raw): Obliques (heavy involvement); Rectus abdominis; Latissimus dorsi; Anterior deltoid; Hip rotators; Gluteus maximus

Description: Set two cable pulleys to their lowest position. Place an incline bench (30 to 45 degrees) between them. Lie on the incline bench. Grip a D-handle in each hand. Start with handles at your chest, elbows at 45 degrees. Press both handles up and together, converging at the top above your upper chest. Squeeze your upper chest hard at the top — constant cable tension here. Lower under control back to your chest. Maintain cable tension throughout — never let the weight stack rest. Use moderate weight. Aim for 10 to 15 reps per set.
Benefits: Constant cable tension throughout the press; Excellent for upper chest hypertrophy; Joint-friendly; Easy to load progressively; Different tension curve than barbell pressing; Converging press path for peak contraction
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major (clavicular head); Anterior deltoid; Triceps brachii; Serratus anterior

Exercise Name: Cable Kneeling Leaning Forward One Arm Row
Description: Set a cable to the lowest setting with a single handle. Kneel on one knee in front of the cable stack. Grip the handle with the hand opposite the kneeling leg. Lean forward and let the cable pull the arm extended. Brace your core and keep the chest tall. Pinch the shoulder blade down. Pull the handle back driving the elbow past the body. Squeeze the lat hard. Lower with control. Switch sides.
Benefits: Strong unilateral lat builder; Constant cable tension; Trains the rhomboids; Builds back size; Useful back move; Strong cable move
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi; Rhomboids; Posterior deltoid; Biceps brachii

Exercise Name: Cable Kneeling One Arm Lat Pulldown
Description: Set a high cable pulley with a D-handle attachment. Kneel directly under the cable on your right knee, left foot flat in front for stability. Reach up and grip the handle with your right hand using an overhand grip. Lean slightly forward. Brace your core. Pull the handle down toward your right shoulder by driving your elbow down and back. Continue pulling until your right hand reaches your shoulder. Squeeze your right lat hard at the bottom. Slowly extend your arm back overhead under control. Complete reps, then switch sides.
Benefits: Isolates each lat individually; Eliminates body english; Reveals left-right imbalances; Constant cable tension throughout; Builds lat width; Easy to load progressively
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi (single side); Teres major; Posterior deltoid; Biceps brachii; Rhomboids

Description: Set a cable to a low pulley with a single handle. Kneel on the floor facing away from the cable, with the handle in your right hand. Position the handle at shoulder level with elbow tucked. Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to lock the hips. Press the handle straight up overhead until your arm is fully extended. Squeeze your shoulder at the top. Lower the handle back to shoulder level with control. Complete reps on one side, then switch arms.
Benefits: Removes leg drive for strict shoulder work; Constant cable tension through the range; Strong glute and core engagement; Builds shoulder strength unilaterally; Tall kneeling challenges hip stability; Useful for shoulder hypertrophy
Muscles Worked (Raw): Anterior deltoid; Lateral deltoid; Triceps brachii; Core stabilizers

Description: Set a cable pulley to the lowest position. Attach a rope handle. Kneel facing away from the cable. Pass the rope between your legs from behind. Grip both ends. Kneel tall. The cable should be taut. Hinge at the hips, pushing your butt back. Let the cable pull your hands back between your legs. Drive your hips forward by squeezing your glutes. Return to tall kneeling with hips fully extended. Squeeze your glutes hard at the top. Aim for 12 to 15 reps per set.
Benefits: Isolates the glutes without quad involvement; Kneeling removes leg drive; Constant cable tension throughout; Teaches proper hip hinge mechanics; Easy to load progressively; Excellent glute activation exercise
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus maximus (primary); Hamstrings; Erector spinae; Core (stabilizer)

Description: Set a cable to the lowest pulley with a single handle. Kneel on one knee facing the cable, opposite knee bent at 90 degrees. Grip the handle with the same-side arm as the kneeling leg. Extend the arm forward toward the pulley. Brace your core and keep your back flat. Pull the handle to your hip by driving the elbow back. Squeeze your lat hard at the back of the row. Slowly extend the arm forward to the starting position. Switch sides.
Benefits: Strict single-arm rowing; Corrects lat strength imbalances; Constant cable tension through the range; Eliminates leg drive; Builds back thickness; Strong core anti-rotation challenge
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi; Rhomboids; Trapezius (middle); Biceps brachii

Description: Set a preacher bench in front of a low cable pulley. Attach a straight bar or rope to the low pulley. Kneel behind the preacher bench with your chest pressed to the pad. Drape your arms over the preacher pad with the cable attachment in your hands. Allow your arms to fully extend with the cable below. Brace your core and pin your chest to the pad. Curl the attachment up by bending only at the elbows. Squeeze the biceps at the top, then lower with control to full extension.
Benefits: Strict bicep isolation; Constant cable tension; Strong stretch at the bottom; Eliminates body english; Builds bicep size with peak contraction; Useful for hypertrophy training
Muscles Worked (Raw): Biceps brachii; Brachialis; Brachioradialis

Description: Set a cable pulley to a low position. Attach a D-handle. Stand sideways to the cable. Grip the handle with the hand closest to the cable, then bring it to your chest. Step away from the cable until you feel tension. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Take a wide step to the side away from the cable with your far leg. Sit your far hip back and bend your far knee, lowering into a lateral squat on that side. Keep your near (close to cable) leg straight, foot flat on the floor. Drive through your far foot to push back to standing. Repeat for the desired reps, then switch sides. Use moderate weight.
Benefits: Builds frontal-plane hip strength; Constant cable tension throughout; Targets the adductors and glutes; Trains lateral stability; Carries over to athletic cutting movements; Easy to load progressively
Muscles Worked (Raw): Quadriceps (working leg); Gluteus maximus and medius; Adductors (extended leg, stretched); Hamstrings; Core (stabilizer)

Description: Set a cable to chest height with a single handle. Kneel sideways to the cable station with both knees on the floor. Grip the handle with both hands at chest level. Step away from the anchor to create cable tension. Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to lock the hips. Rotate your torso away from the cable, pulling the handle across your body. Continue rotating until your arms are extended on the far side. Slowly return to the starting position with control. Complete reps, switch sides.
Benefits: Trains rotational core strength; Constant cable tension through the rotation; Kneeling position eliminates leg drive; Strong oblique engagement; Useful for athletes needing rotational power; Easy to scale by changing cable resistance
Muscles Worked (Raw): Obliques (internal and external); Rectus abdominis; Transverse abdominis

Description: Set a cable to the lowest position. Attach a D-handle. Stand next to the cable. Grip the handle with your far hand (cable crosses behind or in front of your body). Stand tall. Arm at your side with slight elbow bend. Raise your arm out to the side to shoulder height. Squeeze your lateral delt at the top. Lower under control. Complete reps, then switch sides. Use light to moderate weight. Aim for 12 to 15 reps.
Benefits: Constant tension throughout full range; Superior to dumbbells for bottom-range tension; Builds the lateral delt cap; Easy to load progressively; Strict isolation; Joint-friendly
Muscles Worked (Raw): Lateral deltoid (primary); Anterior deltoid (slight); Upper trapezius (slight)

Description: Attach a single-handle (D-handle) to a low cable pulley. Stand sideways to the cable machine. Grip the handle in your far hand (the hand away from the machine). Grip the upright of the cable machine with your near hand and lean your body away from the pulley until your near arm is fully extended. Your body should now be at a roughly 30-degree angle from vertical, leaning away from the cable. Let the working arm hang across your body. Brace your core and keep a slight bend in the working elbow. Lift the handle out to your side by raising your elbow up and out. Continue until your upper arm is roughly parallel to the floor. Pause briefly at the top, then lower under control over two to three seconds back to the start position. Keep tension on the cable throughout. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
Benefits: Loads the lateral deltoid through its longest possible range of motion; Constant cable tension throughout the entire rep; Heavily targets the bottom portion of the raise that dumbbells cannot effectively load; Excellent for breaking through side-delt size plateaus; Trains one side at a time, exposing imbalances; Easy to load progressively in small increments
Muscles Worked (Raw): Lateral deltoid; Anterior deltoid (secondary); Posterior deltoid (secondary); Supraspinatus (rotator cuff, initial range); Core (anti-rotation)

Description: Set two cable pulleys to the lowest position. Attach D-handles. Stand between the cables. Grip both handles at your sides (low). Step forward into a staggered stance. Arc both handles upward and together in front of your upper chest or face. Squeeze your upper chest when hands meet. Slowly lower back to the sides under control. Maintain slight elbow bend throughout. Aim for 12 to 15 reps per set.
Benefits: Emphasizes the upper (clavicular) chest; Low-to-high arc targets different fibers than horizontal flies; Constant cable tension throughout; Easy to load progressively; Excellent for upper chest development; Joint-friendly
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major (clavicular head); Anterior deltoid; Serratus anterior

Exercise Name: Cable Low Row with Rope Attachment
Description: Attach a rope to a low cable pulley. Sit on the floor or a low bench facing the machine. Grip both ends of the rope with palms facing each other. Sit tall with chest up and core braced. Row the rope toward your lower chest by driving the elbows back. Pull the rope ends apart at the end of the motion. Squeeze the upper back and rear delts hard. Lower the rope back to the start with control.
Benefits: Allows extra rear delt squeeze; Builds upper back detail; Constant cable tension; Improves rowing strength; Useful back day move; Easy to scale loading
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi; Rhomboids; Posterior deltoid; Biceps brachii

Description: Set both cable pulleys to the lowest position with single handles. Stand facing away from the cable stack with one handle in each hand. Position the handles at hip level with arms back behind your body. Step forward to create cable tension. Brace your core and pull your shoulders back. Press both handles up and forward at an upward angle until your arms meet at chest level. Squeeze your chest at the top with arms extended. Lower the handles back to the starting position with control.
Benefits: Targets lower chest with cable tension; No decline bench required; Constant tension through the range; Builds chest size and lower pec definition; Useful for chest specialization; Strong tricep engagement
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major (lower fibers); Triceps brachii; Anterior deltoid

Description: Set a cable to the lowest position. Sit on a bench or the floor facing the cable. Grip a V-bar, rope, or straight bar handle. Sit upright with feet on footplates or flat on the floor. Row the handle toward your lower abdomen by driving your elbows back. The low cable angle creates a slightly upward pulling path. Squeeze your lats and lower back at the end of the row. Slowly extend forward. Aim for 10 to 12 reps per set.
Benefits: Low angle emphasizes the lower lats; Builds back thickness; Constant cable tension; Easy to load progressively; Different angle than standard seated row; Comfortable seated position
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi (lower fibers); Trapezius (middle); Rhomboids; Biceps brachii; Erector spinae

Description: Set a cable pulley to a low position. Attach a straight bar or D-handle. Grip the handle and bring it to your chest, or hold it overhead. Face away from the cable. Step away from the cable to create tension. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Brace your core. Step your right foot forward into a lunge stance. Lower your back (left) knee toward the floor by bending both knees. Drive through your front foot to push back to standing. Step back. Repeat or alternate sides for the desired reps.
Benefits: Constant cable tension throughout the lunge; Loads both eccentric and concentric phases; Builds quad and glute strength; Easy to load progressively; Useful when no dumbbells are available; Excellent for unilateral leg work
Muscles Worked (Raw): Quadriceps; Gluteus maximus; Hamstrings; Adductors; Core (stabilizer); Calves

Exercise Name: Cable Low Seated Row with V Bar
Description: Sit at a cable row station with feet on the platform. Grip the V bar with both hands palms facing each other. Sit tall with the back straight and chest up. Brace your core and pinch the shoulder blades. Pull the V bar toward the lower ribs. Drive the elbows back close to the sides. Squeeze the lats hard at the back. Extend the arms with control to the start.
Benefits: Builds the lats; Trains the mid back; Strong neutral grip row; Builds back size; Useful classic move; Builds the biceps
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi; Biceps brachii; Rhomboids; Trapezius

Description: Set a cable to the lowest pulley with a short bar attachment. Lie on your back on the floor with feet near the cable station. Grip the bar with a close underhand grip. Extend your arms straight up over your chest with the cable creating tension. Brace your core and press your back to the floor. Lower the bar back toward your forehead by bending only at the elbows. Continue down until the bar is near your forehead. Curl back up to the starting position by extending the elbows.
Benefits: Strict bicep isolation; Lying position eliminates body english; Constant cable tension through the range; Close grip targets long head; Useful for breaking through curl plateaus; Strong peak contraction
Muscles Worked (Raw): Biceps brachii (long head); Brachialis; Brachioradialis

Description: Attach a rope to a high cable pulley. Kneel facing away from the cable machine. Grip both ends of the rope. Pull them behind your head with elbows bent. Pin your upper arms next to your head. Elbows point forward. Brace your core. Keep your torso upright. Extend at the elbows to push the rope forward and up. Split the rope at lockout. Squeeze your triceps hard. Hold one second. Slowly let the rope return behind your head over two seconds. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Benefits: Kneeling position eliminates leg drive and lower-back involvement; Constant cable tension throughout; Strict tricep isolation; Deep stretch on the long head; Easy to load progressively; Useful variation for high-rep tricep work
Muscles Worked (Raw): Triceps brachii (especially the long head); Anconeus; Core (stabilizer)

Description: Position a flat bench in front of a low cable pulley. Attach a straight bar or EZ bar. Lie on the bench on your back, head closest to the cable machine. Reach back and grip the bar. Start with arms extended toward the cable. The cable should be under tension. Pin your upper arms at your sides or slightly forward. Brace your core. Curl the bar up by bending at the elbows. Squeeze your biceps at the top. Lower under control over two seconds. Maintain cable tension throughout. Keep your upper arms still — only forearms move. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Benefits: Eliminates all body english — strict bicep isolation; Constant cable tension throughout the full range; Lying position prevents swinging or leaning; Excellent for feeling the target muscle; Useful for high-rep finishing work; Easy to load progressively
Muscles Worked (Raw): Biceps brachii; Brachialis; Brachioradialis; Forearm flexors

Description: Position a flat bench (or floor space) in front of a low cable pulley. Attach a straight bar. Lie on your back on the bench (or floor) with your head closest to the cable. Reach back overhead and grip the bar with an underhand grip. Pull the bar down so your arms are extended straight back overhead, palms up. The cable should be under tension. Pin your upper arms — they will angle slightly back overhead. Keep them still. Curl the bar by bending at the elbows. Squeeze your biceps as the bar moves toward your forehead. Lower under control. Maintain cable tension and upper arm position. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Benefits: Constant cable tension throughout the range; Lying position eliminates all body english; Slight bicep stretch loaded throughout; Excellent strict isolation exercise; Useful for high-rep bicep finishing; Easy to load progressively
Muscles Worked (Raw): Biceps brachii (stretched position); Brachialis; Forearm flexors

Description: Set a cable to the lowest pulley with a single handle. Lie on your right side on the floor perpendicular to the cable station. Grip the handle with your left hand from across your body. Position yourself so the cable runs across your chest. Brace your core to keep your trunk stable. Raise the handle up and across your body to shoulder height. Squeeze your left medial delt at the top. Lower the handle back down with control. Switch sides.
Benefits: Strict medial delt isolation; Lying position eliminates body english; Constant cable tension through the range; Builds shoulder width; Useful for hypertrophy training; Strong peak contraction
Muscles Worked (Raw): Lateral deltoid; Anterior deltoid; Trapezius (upper)

Description: Set both cable pulleys to the lowest position with single handles. Position a flat bench between the two cable stations. Lie back on the bench with handles in each hand. Hold the handles together over your chest with arms extended, palms facing each other. Plant your feet flat and brace your core. Lower the handles to your chest while keeping them close together. Allow your elbows to tuck close to your sides as you lower. Press the handles back up by extending the elbows. Squeeze the triceps at the top.
Benefits: Constant cable tension through the range; Targets triceps with close grip; Builds inner chest as well as triceps; Useful tricep variation for cable users; Strong lockout strength development; Different stimulus than barbell close grip press
Muscles Worked (Raw): Triceps brachii; Pectoralis major (inner fibers); Anterior deltoid

Description: Set two cable pulleys to their lowest position. Place a flat bench between them. Lie on the bench. Grip a D-handle in each hand. Start with arms extended above your chest, slight elbow bend, palms facing each other. Lower both arms out to the sides in a wide arc, maintaining the slight elbow bend. Lower until you feel a deep stretch across your chest. Pull the handles back together above your chest by squeezing your pecs. Squeeze at the top — the cables maintain tension here unlike dumbbells. Use moderate weight. Aim for 10 to 15 reps per set.
Benefits: Constant cable tension throughout — even at the top; Superior to dumbbell fly for constant tension; Deep chest stretch at the bottom; Easy to load progressively; Excellent for chest hypertrophy; Joint-friendly with controlled loading
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Anterior deltoid; Biceps brachii (slight stabilizer); Serratus anterior

Description: Set a cable to the lowest pulley with a bar attachment. Lie on your back on the floor with feet near the cable station. Grip the bar with an underhand grip at shoulder-width. Extend your arms straight up over your chest with cable tension active. Brace your core and press your back to the floor. Lower the bar back toward your forehead by bending only at the elbows. Continue down until the bar is near your forehead. Curl back up to the starting position by extending the elbows.
Benefits: Strict bicep isolation; Lying position eliminates body english; Constant cable tension through the range; Balanced shoulder-width grip; Useful for hypertrophy training; Strong peak contraction
Muscles Worked (Raw): Biceps brachii; Brachialis; Brachioradialis

Description: Set up a flat or incline bench between two cable stations. Attach D-handles to low pulleys on each side. Lie face down on the bench with arms hanging off the sides. Grip a handle in each hand with palms facing each other. Allow your arms to hang down with cable tension active. Brace your core and pull your shoulders back. Shrug your shoulder blades back and together as if pinning them to your spine. Hold the squeeze for one count, then lower with control.
Benefits: Constant cable tension through the range; Targets middle and lower trap fibers; Different stimulus than standing shrugs; Improves scapular control; Helps with posture; Strong for full trap development
Muscles Worked (Raw): Trapezius (middle and lower fibers); Rhomboids; Posterior deltoid

Description: Position a flat bench in front of a low cable pulley so your head is closest to the machine. Attach a straight bar or EZ bar. Lie on the bench, reach back, and grip the bar. Press it up over your chest with arms extended. Plant your feet. Pull your shoulders down and back. Brace your core. Pin your upper arms pointing straight up. Lower the bar toward your forehead by bending only at the elbows. Lower until you feel a strong stretch in your triceps. The cable maintains tension throughout. Extend your arms back up to lockout by contracting your triceps. Maintain the upper arm position throughout. Do not let elbows flare. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Benefits: Constant cable tension throughout the entire range of motion; Loads the bottom stretch position better than free weights; Builds all three heads of the triceps; Easier on the elbows than heavy barbell skull crushers; Excellent for high-rep hypertrophy work; Easy to load progressively
Muscles Worked (Raw): Triceps brachii (all three heads); Anconeus; Forearm extensors (grip)

Description: Set a cable to the lowest pulley with a single bar or rope attachment. Lie on your back on the floor with feet toward the cable. Grip the bar with both hands at thigh level with arms extended. Brace your core and press your back to the floor. Pull the bar up toward your chin by leading with the elbows. Lift your elbows out to the sides as the bar travels up. Continue until the bar reaches chest level. Slowly lower the bar back down with control.
Benefits: Shoulder-friendlier than standing upright rows; Constant cable tension through the range; Lying position eliminates body english; Builds shoulder and trap strength; Different angle than standing variations; Useful for breaking through shoulder plateaus
Muscles Worked (Raw): Lateral deltoid; Anterior deltoid; Trapezius (upper); Brachialis

Description: Set a flat bench in front of a low cable pulley. Attach a rope or straight bar to the cable. Lie back on the bench with your head near the cable. Reach overhead and grab the attachment. Start with arms extended above your forehead. Bend at the elbows to lower the attachment behind your head. Keep your upper arms still and only the elbows moving. Extend the elbows to return to the start position.
Benefits: Constant cable tension; Stretches the long head of the triceps; Builds triceps mass; Smoother resistance than barbell; Reduces wrist strain; Strong triceps isolation
Muscles Worked (Raw): Triceps brachii (long head); Triceps brachii (lateral head); Triceps brachii (medial head)

Description: Attach a single D-handle to the low cable pulley. Stand to the side of the cable, holding the handle in one hand with palm facing your body. Hinge forward at the hips so your torso is nearly parallel to the floor. Place the non-working hand on your knee for support. Pin your working elbow against your ribs with the upper arm parallel to your torso. Extend the elbow to straighten the arm behind you. Squeeze the triceps hard at full extension. Return slowly to the start. Complete reps on one side before switching.
Benefits: Wrist-friendly neutral grip; Constant cable tension on the triceps; Strong peak contraction; Builds triceps definition; Allows unilateral focus; Useful for triceps shape and detail
Muscles Worked (Raw): Triceps brachii (long head); Triceps brachii (lateral head); Triceps brachii (medial head)

Description: Attach an ankle strap to a low cable pulley. Wrap the strap around your right ankle. Stand sideways to the cable machine with the cable on your left side. Your right leg (with the strap) is the working leg. Grip the cable machine upright with your left hand for balance. Stand tall with feet together. Brace your core and pull your shoulders back. Keep your right leg slightly forward and lifted off the floor. Lift your right leg out to the side by abducting at the hip. Keep your knee straight and your toes pointing forward. Continue lifting until your leg is at roughly 30 to 45 degrees from your body. Squeeze your right glute hard. Lower the leg under control back to the start position. Maintain cable tension throughout. Complete all reps on the right side, then switch the strap to the left ankle and stand on the opposite side of the machine.
Benefits: Direct gluteus medius isolation; Constant cable tension throughout the range of motion; Improves hip stability and balance; Builds the upper outer glute “shelf”; Carries over to better squat and deadlift mechanics; Excellent finisher for glute workouts
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus medius; Gluteus minimus; Tensor fasciae latae; Gluteus maximus (upper fibers, secondary); Core (stabilizer)

Exercise Name: Cable One Arm Bent Over Row
Description: Set a cable pulley to the lowest position. Attach a D-handle. Stand facing the pulley with feet hip-width apart. Grip the handle with your right hand. Hinge forward at the hips until your torso is roughly parallel to the floor. Place your left hand on your left thigh for support. Allow your right arm to hang straight down with the handle. Brace your core. Maintain a flat back. Row the handle up toward your hip by driving your right elbow back and along your side. Squeeze your right lat at the top of the row. Lower under control. Complete reps on one side, then switch.
Benefits: Isolates each lat individually; Constant cable tension throughout; Exposes left-right imbalances; Allows full range of motion; Builds back thickness; Easy to load progressively
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi; Trapezius (middle and lower); Rhomboids; Posterior deltoid; Biceps brachii; Forearms; Erector spinae (postural)

Description: Set two cable pulleys at chest height. Attach D-handles to each. Stand between the cables. Grip both handles. Step forward into a staggered stance for stability. Start with arms extended to the sides at chest height, slight elbow bend. Pull both handles together in front of your chest in a wide arc. Squeeze your chest hard when your hands meet in front. Slowly let the handles return to the sides under control. Maintain constant tension on the cables throughout.
Benefits: Constant cable tension through the full arc; Targets the middle/sternal pec; Easy to load progressively; Joint-friendly; Excellent chest isolation; Adjustable cable height for different angles
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major (sternal fibers); Anterior deltoid; Biceps brachii (slight stabilizer); Serratus anterior

Description: Set a cable to the lowest pulley with a single handle. Lie on your back on the floor with the cable behind your head. Grip the handle and extend your arm overhead behind you. Brace your core and press your back to the floor. Raise the handle in an arc up and over your chest. Continue until your arm is roughly perpendicular to the floor. Squeeze your front delt at the top. Slowly lower the handle back to the starting position behind you.
Benefits: Strict front delt isolation; Constant cable tension through the range; Lying position eliminates body english; Builds front delt size and definition; Strong stretch on the front delt at the bottom; Useful for hypertrophy training
Muscles Worked (Raw): Anterior deltoid; Pectoralis major (clavicular head); Trapezius (upper)

Description: Attach a single-handle (D-handle) to a low cable pulley. Stand facing away from the cable machine with the cable running between your legs. Grip the handle in your right hand with palm facing your body. Step forward enough that the cable is under tension at the start position. Stand tall. Brace your core and pull your shoulders back. Set a slight bend in your right elbow and lock it in. Lift the handle straight forward and up by raising your right arm. Rotate your wrist so your palm faces the floor at the top. Continue until your arm is roughly parallel to the floor (at shoulder height). Pause briefly at the top. Lower under control over two to three seconds back to the start position. Maintain constant tension on the cable. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
Benefits: Constant cable tension throughout the entire range of motion; Loads the front delt at the top, where dumbbells lose tension; Exposes and corrects left-right imbalances; Easier to feel the target muscle than during bilateral work; Easy to load progressively in small increments; Trains core anti-rotation through the asymmetric loading
Muscles Worked (Raw): Anterior deltoid; Lateral deltoid (secondary); Pectoralis major (clavicular head, secondary); Serratus anterior (stabilizer); Core (anti-rotation)

Exercise Name: Cable One Arm Incline Fly on Exercise Ball
Description: Set a cable handle at low height. Sit on a stability ball with feet flat on the floor. Walk the feet out and bridge the upper back onto the ball. Grab the handle with one arm extended out to the side. Brace the core and keep the hips lifted. Pull the handle up and across the body in a fly arc. Squeeze the chest at the top centerline. Return with control and continue for all reps then switch.
Benefits: Isolates the upper chest.; Cable provides constant tension.; Ball adds core challenge.; Useful chest accessory.; Builds upper pec.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Anterior deltoid; Biceps brachii; Core

Exercise Name: Cable One Arm Decline Chest Fly
Description: Set a cable to the highest setting and attach a single handle. Stand sideways to the cable and grip the handle in the far hand. Step away to take tension on the cable. Set a staggered stance for stability. Brace your core and keep the chest tall. Start with the arm out to the side at shoulder height. Sweep the arm down and across the body to the opposite hip. Squeeze the chest hard at the bottom. Lower back with control. Switch sides and repeat.
Benefits: Strong lower chest builder; Trains unilateral chest control; Builds chest size; Strong cable move; Useful chest finisher; Trains the sternal head
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Anterior deltoid; Serratus anterior

Exercise Name: Cable One Arm Fly on Exercise Ball
Description: Set a cable to chest height with a single handle attached. Lie face up on a stability ball with upper back supported. Plant the feet flat and lift the hips. Grip the handle with one hand at chest height. Brace your core and keep the body straight. Press the handle out and across the body in a fly arc. Squeeze the chest hard at the top. Return with control. Finish all reps then switch sides.
Benefits: Trains the chest; Adds core challenge; Strong fly variation; Builds chest size; Useful unstable surface
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Anterior deltoid; Core

Description: Set a cable to a low pulley with a single handle. Stand facing away from the cable station with feet shoulder-width apart. Grip the handle with your right hand at chest level, palm forward. Step forward to create cable tension. Brace your core hard against the asymmetric load. Press the handle up and forward at an incline angle until your arm is extended. Resist any rotation in your trunk. Bring the handle back to chest level with control. Switch sides.
Benefits: Targets upper chest with single-arm work; Strong anti-rotation core demand; Constant cable tension through the range; Corrects left-right imbalances; Builds unilateral chest strength; Useful for hypertrophy training
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major (clavicular head); Triceps brachii; Anterior deltoid; Obliques

Exercise Name: Cable One Arm High Pulley Overhead Tricep Extension
Description: Set a cable pulley to the highest setting and attach a single handle. Face away from the cable and grab the handle with one hand. Step forward and bring the elbow up next to the head. Plant the feet in a split stance for stability. Brace the core and keep the elbow pointing forward. Extend the elbow by pressing the hand up overhead. Squeeze the triceps at the top. Lower with control and repeat for all reps then switch sides.
Benefits: Biases the triceps long head through overhead position.; Cable provides constant tension throughout.; Trains one arm at a time for symmetry.; Carryover to pressing strength.; Easy to scale by adjusting cable weight.; Develops triceps size and lockout strength.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Triceps brachii; Anconeus; Posterior deltoid

Exercise Name: Cable One Arm Incline Press on Exercise Ball
Description: Set a cable to low pulley and grip a handle in one hand. Lie back on a stability ball with the upper back supported and head off the ball. Lift the hips into a strong bridge position. Press the ball into your back for stability. Bring the cable handle to chest level with elbow bent. Brace the core and press the cable up and slightly inward. Lock out the arm fully overhead at the top of the press. Lower the cable back to chest level with control and complete all reps then switch.
Benefits: Hits the upper chest with the incline angle.; Trains anti rotation and core stability.; Single arm work exposes imbalances.; Cable tension stays constant throughout.; Builds shoulder stability with the unstable ball.; Adds variety to standard cable presses.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Anterior deltoid; Triceps brachii; Core; Obliques

Exercise Name: Cable One Arm Lateral Bent Over
Description: Set a cable to a low position with a single handle attached. Stand sideways to the cable in a hinged position. Grip the handle with the arm that crosses the body. Brace your core and keep the back flat. Raise the arm out to the side away from the body. Keep a slight bend in the elbow throughout. Squeeze the rear delt hard at the top. Lower with control. Finish all reps then switch sides.
Benefits: Targets the rear delts; Constant cable tension; Strong unilateral move; Builds shoulder shape; Useful rear delt builder
Muscles Worked (Raw): Posterior deltoid; Rhomboids; Trapezius

Description: Set a cable to the lowest position. Attach a D-handle. Stand sideways to the cable. Grip the handle with your far hand (cable crosses behind your body). Stand tall. Arm at your side, slight elbow bend. Raise your arm out to the side to shoulder height. Squeeze your lateral delt at the top. Lower under control. Complete reps, then switch sides. Use light to moderate weight. Aim for 12 to 15 reps per side.
Benefits: Constant cable tension even at the bottom; Superior to dumbbells for constant tension; Strict unilateral isolation; Easy to load progressively; Builds the lateral delt cap; Reveals left-right imbalances
Muscles Worked (Raw): Lateral deltoid (primary); Anterior deltoid (slight); Upper trapezius (slight)

Description: Attach a D-handle to a high cable pulley. Sit or kneel below the pulley. Reach up with one hand and grip the handle. Use your free hand for balance or place it on your hip. Sit tall with chest up. Brace your core. Pull your shoulder blades down and back. Pull the handle down toward your shoulder by driving your elbow down and back. Continue until the handle is at shoulder height. Squeeze your lat hard at the bottom. Slowly let the handle travel back up to a full stretch overhead. Complete all reps on one side, then switch. The longer range of motion is the key advantage — let the lat fully stretch at the top.
Benefits: Trains each lat independently; Longer range of motion than two-handed pulldowns; Exposes and corrects left-right lat imbalances; Easier to feel the target muscle; Easy to load progressively; Builds lat width effectively
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi; Teres major; Trapezius (middle and lower); Rhomboids; Biceps brachii; Core (anti-rotation)

Exercise Name: Cable One Arm Press on Exercise Ball
Description: Set a cable to chest height behind the ball position. Sit on a stability ball and walk the feet out so the upper back rests on the ball. Grip a single handle in one hand at the chest. Brace your core hard and keep the hips lifted. Press the handle straight up to lockout. Squeeze the chest at full extension. Lower with control to the start. Complete reps and switch hands.
Benefits: Strong unilateral chest move; Adds core challenge; Trains the obliques; Constant cable tension; Strong cable move; Builds chest size
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Anterior deltoid; Triceps brachii; Core

Description: Attach a single-handle (D-handle) to a high cable pulley. Stand facing the cable machine with feet shoulder-width apart. Grip the handle with your right hand using an overhand or neutral grip. Pin your right elbow against your right side. Your forearm should start parallel to the floor or slightly higher. Brace your core and pull your shoulders back. Your free hand can rest on your hip for stability. Push the handle straight down by extending only at the elbow. Keep your upper arm completely still. Continue pushing until your arm is fully extended. Squeeze your tricep hard for one second at the bottom. Slowly let the handle travel back up under control until your forearm is parallel to the floor again. Complete all reps on the right side, then switch.

Muscles Worked (Raw): Triceps brachii (especially the lateral head); Anconeus; Forearm extensors (stabilizer); Core (anti-rotation)

Description: Attach a single-handle (D-handle) to a high cable pulley. Sit on the lat pulldown seat with the thigh pad locked over your legs. Reach up with your right hand and grip the handle with a neutral or overhand grip. Place your left hand on your knee or hip for stability. Sit upright with your chest tall. Brace your core and pull your shoulder blade down and back to set the start position. Pull the handle down by driving your elbow down and toward your right hip. Lead with the elbow. Bring your hand to roughly chest height. Squeeze your lat hard at the bottom. Slowly let the handle travel back up to a fully extended overhead position. Feel the stretch in your lat. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
Benefits: Exposes and corrects left-right back strength imbalances; Allows a longer range of motion than the two-arm version; Focuses entirely on contracting one lat at a time; Easier to feel the target muscle than during bilateral work; Trains core anti-rotation through the asymmetric loading; Great accessory after heavier compound back work

Description: Set a cable pulley to roughly waist or mid-torso height. Attach a D-handle. Stand sideways to the cable. Reach across your body with the far hand and grip the handle. Step back slightly. Set a slight bend in your working elbow and lock it in. Brace your core. Stand tall or lean slightly forward. Pull the handle out and back in a wide arc away from the cable, squeezing your rear delt. Continue until your arm is roughly in line with your shoulder. Squeeze hard at the peak. Slowly return under control. Maintain cable tension throughout. Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
Benefits: Constant cable tension throughout the full range; Trains one rear delt at a time for focus and balance; Exposes left-right imbalances; Easy to load progressively; Excellent finisher for shoulder or back days; Trains core anti-rotation as a secondary benefit
Muscles Worked (Raw): Posterior deltoid; Trapezius (middle fibers); Rhomboids; Infraspinatus; Core (anti-rotation)

Description: Set a cable to the lowest pulley with a single handle. Kneel beside a flat bench with the cable in front of you. Drape your right forearm over the bench top with palm facing up. Grip the cable handle with your right hand and let your wrist hang off the bench. Brace your core. Lower your wrist by extending it down toward the floor. Curl the cable up by flexing your wrist. Squeeze your forearm at the top, then lower with control. Switch arms.

Muscles Worked (Raw): Forearm flexors; Wrist flexors; Brachioradialis

Description: Set two cable pulleys to high positions (above head height). Attach D-handles to each. Stand between the cables. Grip both handles with arms extended out to the sides at shoulder height (T position), palms facing up. Stand tall. Brace your core. Keep your upper arms parallel to the floor. Curl both handles toward your head by bending at the elbows. Keep your upper arms still. Continue until your forearms are vertical (or the handles approach your ears). Squeeze your biceps hard at the top — focus on the peak contraction. Slowly extend your arms back to the start over two seconds. Maintain cable tension throughout. Use moderate weight.
Benefits: Targets the biceps in their most stretched position; Constant cable tension throughout; Excellent for bicep peak development; Strict isolation — no body english possible; Easy to load progressively; Builds the bicep peak
Muscles Worked (Raw): Biceps brachii (especially the long head); Brachialis; Brachioradialis; Forearm flexors

Exercise Name: Cable One Arm Twisting Seated Row
Description: Sit at a cable row machine with feet on the platform. Attach a single D-handle to the low cable. Grab the handle with one hand. Sit upright with a tall back. Brace your core and keep your chest up. Pull the handle back toward your hip while rotating your torso away from the cable. Squeeze the lat and oblique at the end of the rep. Return slowly to the start. Complete reps on one side before switching.
Benefits: Builds rotational core strength; Trains the obliques; Strong unilateral back work; Useful for athletes; Builds back thickness; Strong functional move
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi; Obliques; Rear deltoid; Rhomboids

Exercise Name: Cable One Arm Inner Biceps Curl
Description: Attach a single D-handle to a low cable pulley. Stand facing the cable, holding the handle in one hand with palm up. Step back slightly to add tension. Brace your core and keep your chest up. Pin your elbow against your ribs. Curl the handle up toward your shoulder. Squeeze the biceps hard at the top. Lower the handle slowly to the start. Complete reps on one side before switching.
Benefits: Targets the inner biceps; Constant cable tension; Strict, swing-free curl; Allows unilateral focus; Helps fix arm imbalances; Builds biceps thickness
Muscles Worked (Raw): Biceps brachii; Brachialis; Forearms

Exercise Name: Cable Pallof Press With Glute Bridge
Description: Set a cable to chest height when lying down with a single handle. Lie on your back perpendicular to the cable station. Grip the handle with both hands at your chest. Plant your feet flat on the floor with knees bent. Drive your hips up into a glute bridge. Brace your core hard against the lateral pull of the cable. While holding the glute bridge, press the handle straight up over your chest. Bring the handle back to your chest. Continue pressing while holding the bridge. Switch sides.

Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus maximus; Obliques; Rectus abdominis; Hamstrings; Quadratus lumborum

Description: Set a cable pulley to chest height. Attach a single D-handle. Stand facing the cable. Grip the handle with your right hand, palm facing down. Step back so the cable is taut with your arm extended forward. Brace your core. Stand tall. Row the handle toward your torso by driving your elbow back. As you row, rotate your wrist so your palm ends facing up at the end of the rep. Squeeze your back at the peak of the row. Slowly extend your arm forward, rotating your wrist back to palm-down by the end. Complete reps on one side, then switch.

Description: Attach a rope to a low cable pulley. Stand facing away from the machine, straddling the cable. Reach between your legs and grip the rope with both hands. Step forward until the rope is taut. Stand with feet slightly wider than hip-width apart. Hinge forward at the hips, letting the rope pull your hands back between your legs. Keep your back flat. Feel a stretch in your hamstrings. Brace your core. Knees stay slightly bent throughout. Snap your hips forward by squeezing your glutes hard. Stand fully tall at lockout. The cable tension peaks at lockout, loading the glutes maximally at full hip extension. Lower under control. Repeat for 12 to 20 reps per set.
Benefits: Constant cable tension peaks at glute lockout; Excellent glute and hamstring developer; Teaches the hip-hinge pattern effectively; Easier on the lower back than barbell hip hinges; Easy to load progressively; Useful for learning the hip hinge before deadlifts
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus maximus; Hamstrings; Erector spinae; Adductors; Core (stabilizer)

Description: Sit at a lat pulldown station. Secure thighs under the pads. Grip the wide bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width. Arms extended overhead to start. Pull the bar down to your upper chest by driving your elbows down and back. Lean back slightly. Squeeze your lats at the bottom. Slowly extend back overhead under control. Maintain upright torso. Aim for 10 to 12 reps per set.
Benefits: Most popular cable back exercise; Primary pull-up alternative; Builds lat width and back thickness; Easy to load progressively; Accessible for all fitness levels; Constant cable tension
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi; Biceps brachii; Trapezius (lower); Rhomboids; Posterior deltoid

Description: Set a cable to a high position. Attach a straight bar, V-bar, or rope. Grip the bar with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart. Pin your elbows tight against your sides. Push the bar down by extending at the elbows until arms are straight. Squeeze your triceps at the bottom. Hold briefly. Slowly let the bar rise back up to about 90 degrees at the elbow. Keep your upper arms completely still throughout. Aim for 10 to 15 reps per set.

Muscles Worked (Raw): Triceps brachii (all heads); Anconeus

Exercise Name: Cable Parallel Grip Lat Pulldown on Floor
Description: Set a cable to a high position with a parallel grip handle. Kneel directly under the cable on both knees. Grip the handle with palms facing each other. Set the arms straight up at the start. Brace your core and pinch the shoulder blades. Pull the handle down to the chest by driving the elbows down. Squeeze the lats hard at the bottom. Return with control to arms extended overhead.

Description: Set both cable pulleys to chest height with single handles. Position a stability ball between the two cable stations. Lie back on the ball with your upper back supported. Grip a handle in each hand at chest level with palms forward. Plant your feet flat for stability. Brace your core hard. Press both handles forward until your arms are fully extended. Lower the handles back to chest level with control while maintaining ball stability.

Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Triceps brachii; Anterior deltoid; Core stabilizers

Exercise Name: Cable Overhead Tricep Extension Straight Bar
Description: Set the cable to a low position with a straight bar attachment. Stand facing away from the cable stack. Grip the bar overhead with both hands at shoulder width. Step forward to take tension on the cable. Brace your core and keep the chest tall. Keep the upper arms vertical pointing at the ceiling. Extend the elbows pressing the bar straight up overhead. Lower the bar back behind the head with control.

Muscles Worked (Raw): Triceps brachii; Anconeus; Forearm flexors

Description: Position a preacher bench in front of a low cable pulley. Attach a straight bar or EZ bar. Sit on the bench with upper arms draped over the pad. Grip the cable attachment with an underhand grip. Start with arms nearly extended. The cable should be under tension. Curl the bar up by bending at the elbows. Keep upper arms pressed into the pad. Continue until forearms are roughly vertical. Squeeze your biceps hard. Lower under control. Maintain cable tension throughout — do not let slack develop. Stop just before full elbow extension to maintain tension. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Benefits: Constant cable tension throughout the full range; Preacher bench eliminates all body english; Loads the bottom stretch better than dumbbell preacher curls; Excellent for high-rep bicep isolation; Easy to load progressively; Builds bicep strength at the lengthened position
Muscles Worked (Raw): Biceps brachii; Brachialis; Brachioradialis; Forearm flexors

Description: Sit at a lat pulldown station with thighs locked under the pad. Grip the bar with an overhand grip, hands wider than shoulder-width. Pull the bar down toward your upper chest in a strict lat pulldown. At the bottom of the pulldown, hold the bar at chest level with elbows down. Curl the bar up toward your face by bending only at the elbows. Keep elbows pinned to your sides. At the top of the curl, slowly extend your arms back down to the chest position. Then let the bar travel back up to the starting overhead position. Repeat the combined pulldown-then-curl for the desired number of reps. Use moderate weight — both muscle groups need to be challenged.
Benefits: Combines back and bicep work in one movement; Time-efficient for full upper-body pulling; Useful as a finisher or for limited training time; Builds the lats and biceps simultaneously; Trains the muscles together as they function in sport; Easy to load and progress
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi (pulldown); Biceps brachii (curl); Brachialis; Trapezius and rhomboids; Forearms and grip

Description: Attach a straight bar to a low cable pulley. Stand facing the machine with feet hip-width apart. Grip the bar with an overhand (palms-down) grip, hands shoulder-width apart. Stand tall. Pin your elbows against your sides. Brace your core. Curl the bar up by bending at the elbows. Keep the overhand grip throughout. Continue until the bar reaches shoulder height. Squeeze hard at the top. Lower under control. Maintain cable tension. Use lighter weight than standard curls — the overhand position is harder. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Benefits: Targets the brachialis and forearm extensors with constant tension; Builds arm thickness and forearm size; Balances out bicep-dominant training; Helps prevent tennis elbow by strengthening forearm extensors; Easy to load progressively; Complements standard curls for complete arm development
Muscles Worked (Raw): Brachialis; Brachioradialis; Forearm extensors; Biceps brachii (reduced)

Description: Sit at a lat pulldown machine. Grip the bar with hands shoulder-width apart using an underhand (supinated) grip — palms facing you. Adjust the thigh pad to lock your legs in place. Lean back slightly (about 15 degrees). Brace your core. Pull your shoulders back and down. Pull the bar down to your upper chest by driving your elbows down and back along your sides. Continue until the bar touches your upper chest or just below your collarbone. Squeeze your lats and lower back hard at the bottom. Slowly let the bar travel back up to fully extended arms over two to three seconds. Use moderate weight — the underhand grip can stress the wrists and biceps.
Benefits: Emphasizes the lower lats; Increases bicep involvement; Different stimulus than overhand pulldowns; Easier on the shoulders for some lifters; Builds lat thickness; Useful variation for back day
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi (especially lower fibers); Biceps brachii (heavy involvement); Trapezius (lower); Rhomboids; Posterior deltoid; Brachialis

Description: Set a cable to a high position. Attach a straight bar or EZ bar. Grip the bar with a supinated (underhand) grip, hands shoulder-width apart. Pin your elbows at your sides. Push the bar down by extending at the elbows. Lock out at the bottom. Squeeze your triceps. Slowly let the bar rise back up over two seconds. Keep upper arms still — only forearms move. Use moderate weight. Aim for 12 to 15 reps.
Benefits: Targets the medial tricep head; Underhand grip provides different stimulus; Constant cable tension; Easy to load progressively; Useful for complete tricep development; Joint-friendly
Muscles Worked (Raw): Triceps brachii (medial head emphasis); Anconeus

Description: Set a preacher bench in front of a low cable pulley. Attach a straight bar to the low pulley. Sit at the preacher bench with your chest pressed to the pad. Drape your arms over the preacher pad with the cable bar in your hands. Use an overhand grip with palms facing down. Allow your arms to fully extend with the cable below. Curl the bar up by bending only at the elbows, maintaining the overhand grip. Squeeze the forearms at the top, then lower with control to full extension.
Benefits: Targets forearm extensors and brachioradialis; Strict isolation with the preacher pad; Constant cable tension; Builds forearm size and grip; Useful for thicker arms; Pairs well with regular preacher curls
Muscles Worked (Raw): Brachioradialis; Forearm extensors; Biceps brachii; Brachialis

Description: Set a cable pulley to the lowest position. Attach a straight bar handle. Place a flat bench in front of the cable. Sit on the end of the bench facing the pulley. Grip the bar with both hands using an overhand (pronated) grip — palms facing down. Rest your forearms on your thighs. Let your hands hang off your knees with the bar. Allow your wrists to extend down toward the floor — the bar lowers and your knuckles point down. Curl the bar upward by extending your wrists toward your forearms. Continue until your wrists are fully extended. Squeeze your forearm extensors hard. Lower under control over two seconds. Use light weight — the wrist extensors are small.
Benefits: Isolates the forearm extensors; Critical for forearm balance; Helps prevent tennis elbow; Constant cable tension throughout; Builds forearm size and strength; Useful complement to wrist curls
Muscles Worked (Raw): Extensor carpi radialis longus and brevis; Extensor carpi ulnaris; Extensor digitorum; Brachioradialis

Exercise Name: Cable Reverse Grip Straight Back Seated High Row
Description: Set a cable to high pulley with a straight bar attachment. Sit on a bench facing the cable with knees soft and back straight. Grip the bar with an underhand shoulder width grip. Lean back slightly to set a strong straight back position. Brace the core and pull the bar down and back to the lower chest. Keep the elbows tucked and drive them back and down. Squeeze the lats hard at the bottom of the pull. Slowly release the bar back up to the start and repeat.
Benefits: Hits the lats from a high to low angle with reverse grip.; Recruits the biceps strongly through the supinated grip.; Builds back thickness and overall pulling strength.; Cable tension stays constant for time under tension.; Easier on the lower back than bent over rows.; Carryover to chin ups and reverse grip pulls.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi; Biceps brachii; Rhomboids; Trapezius; Posterior deltoid

Description: Attach a straight bar or rope handle to a low cable pulley. Stand facing the cable machine with feet hip-width apart, roughly an arm’s length away. Grip the attachment with an overhand grip. Stand tall with the attachment held at your thighs. The cable should be under tension at the start. Set a soft, fixed bend in your knees. Pull your shoulders back, lift your chest, and brace your core. Begin the descent by pushing your hips straight back. Let the attachment travel down close to your legs. Maintain a flat back throughout. The cable will pull you slightly forward — resist by bracing. Lower until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings, typically when the attachment is at mid-shin level. Drive your hips forward to stand back up, contracting your glutes and hamstrings. Maintain cable tension throughout.
Benefits: Constant cable tension throughout the entire range of motion; Loads the bottom stretch position more effectively than free weights; Excellent for hamstring hypertrophy; Easy to load progressively in small increments; Trains grip and core stability; Allows safe high-rep work near failure
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings (semitendinosus, semimembranosus, biceps femoris); Gluteus maximus; Erector spinae; Adductor magnus; Trapezius (isometric); Forearms and grip; Core (stabilizer)

Description: Sit at a low cable row station with a rope attachment on the cable. Brace your feet on the platform with knees slightly bent. Grip the rope with both hands, palms facing each other. Sit tall with chest up and arms extended forward. Brace your core. Pull the rope to your face level by leading with the elbows out wide. Pull the rope ends apart at the top. Squeeze the upper back hard, then extend the arms forward with control.
Benefits: Targets rear delts and upper back; Rope split allows full contraction; Strong rhomboid engagement; Builds posture and shoulder health; Constant cable tension through the pull; Useful for upper back specialization
Muscles Worked (Raw): Posterior deltoid; Rhomboids; Trapezius (middle); Biceps brachii

Exercise Name: Cable Rope Extension Incline Bench Row
Description: Set an incline bench (30 to 45 degrees) facing a low cable pulley. Attach a rope handle. Lie face down on the bench. Grip the rope with both hands. Start with arms extended toward the cable, chest on the bench. Row the rope toward your lower chest by driving your elbows back and flaring the rope ends. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top. Lower under control. The chest support eliminates all momentum. Aim for 10 to 12 reps per set.
Benefits: Strict back isolation from chest support; Rope allows neutral grip and wider motion; Easy on the lower back; Constant cable tension throughout; Easy to load progressively; Excellent for back hypertrophy
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi; Trapezius (middle); Rhomboids; Posterior deltoid; Biceps brachii

Exercise Name: Cable Rope High Pulley Overhead Tricep Extension
Description: Attach a rope handle to a high cable pulley. Grip both ends of the rope. Face away from the cable machine. Step forward and lean slightly. The rope should be behind your head with elbows bent. Stagger your stance for stability. Brace your core. Pin your upper arms in place. Extend at the elbows to push the rope forward and overhead. As you reach lockout, split the rope ends apart. Squeeze your triceps hard for one second at lockout. Slowly let the rope travel back behind your head over two to three seconds. Feel the deep stretch. Keep your upper arms still throughout — only the forearms move. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Benefits: Rope allows extra range of motion and hand splitting at lockout; Deep stretch on the long head of the triceps; Constant cable tension throughout the range; Easier on the elbows than barbell overhead extensions; Excellent finisher for tricep workouts; Easy to load progressively
