Benefits: Trains the biceps with no weights needed.; Self regulating resistance from your own legs.; Joint friendly with smooth manual tension.; Excellent travel friendly biceps option.; Engages forearms through the towel grip.; Builds biceps endurance with high rep work.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Biceps brachii; Brachialis; Forearm flexors; Brachioradialis

Description: Lie on your back with hands behind your head, elbows out wide. Lift your shoulders off the floor and bring both knees up to 90 degrees. Brace your abs hard. Crunch up and twist to bring your right elbow toward your left knee. At the same time, extend your right leg straight out. Reverse the motion, twisting to bring the left elbow toward the right knee. Extend the left leg as the right knee comes up. Continue alternating in a smooth pedaling pattern.
Benefits: Hits abs and obliques together; No equipment required; Builds rotational core strength; Strong rectus abdominis activation; Trains hip flexors; Classic ab exercise
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Obliques (internal and external); Hip flexors

Exercise Name: Lying Double Legs Hammer Curl with Towel
Description: Lie flat on your back on the floor with knees bent. Loop a towel under both feet with each end held in your hands. Hold the towel with a neutral hammer grip and elbows close to the body. Press both legs gently against the towel to create tension. Curl your hands up toward the shoulders with palms facing in. Increase or decrease leg pressure to scale the load. Squeeze the brachialis and biceps at the top. Lower the towel slowly back to full arm extension and repeat.
Benefits: Hits the brachialis and brachioradialis with the hammer grip.; Self regulating resistance from your own legs.; Joint and wrist friendly neutral grip.; Builds forearm size and grip strength.; No weights needed.; Excellent option for travel and home training.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Biceps brachii; Brachialis; Brachioradialis; Forearm flexors

Description: Lie on the back with the legs straight. Place the hands at the sides palms down. Brace your core and lift the legs slightly off the floor. Cross one leg over the other. Reverse the cross with the opposite leg on top. Continue the criss cross pattern. Keep both legs straight and elevated throughout. Continue for the working set.
Benefits: Loads the lower abs; Trains the hip flexors; Strong core drill; No equipment needed; Builds the abs
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Hip Flexors; Core

Description: Lie on your back. Hands behind your head. Knees bent, feet flat. Crunch up and rotate — bring your right elbow toward your left knee. Simultaneously lift your left knee toward your right elbow. Touch or bring them as close as possible. Lower back to start. Repeat on the other side — left elbow to right knee. Continue alternating. Aim for 10 to 15 reps per side.

Description: Lie on your back on the floor. Lift the legs straight up to vertical with feet pointing at the ceiling. Place the hands at the sides for support. Brace your core hard. Press the feet up toward the ceiling lifting the hips off the floor. Continue lifting until the hips are clear of the floor. Squeeze the lower abs hard at the top. Lower the hips back down with control.
Benefits: Strong lower abs builder; No equipment needed; Trains the glutes; Builds the rectus abdominis; Useful core builder; Easy to do anywhere
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Gluteus maximus; Hip flexors

Description: Lie flat on the floor with knees bent and feet planted. Hold a dumbbell in each hand over your chest with palms facing each other. Keep a slight bend in the elbows. Brace your core and pin your back to the floor. Lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc. Stop when your upper arms touch the floor. Squeeze the chest to bring the dumbbells back together over your chest. Pause briefly at the top.

Description: Lie face down. Hands behind your head or at your sides. Legs on the floor. Lift your chest and upper body off the floor by contracting your lower back. Rise as high as comfortable. Hold for 1 to 2 seconds. Squeeze your lower back. Lower under control. Move with control — no jerking. Aim for 12 to 20 reps.
Benefits: Strengthens the erector spinae from the floor; No equipment needed; Builds lower back endurance; Beginner-friendly; Useful for back health; Accessible anywhere
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae; Gluteus maximus (slight); Multifidus

Exercise Name: Lying Floor Row with Bent Knee
Description: Find a sturdy fixed object low to the ground like a heavy bed or couch base. Lie face up on the floor with the head and shoulders just past the object. Reach back and grip the underside or edge with both hands. Bend your knees and place your feet flat on the floor. Brace the core and keep the body relatively straight. Pull the chest up by driving the elbows back along the sides. Squeeze the upper back at the top of the pull. Lower yourself slowly back to the floor and repeat.

Description: Place a folded towel on the floor. Lie face down with the towel under the hips and pelvis. Extend the arms out in front or place the hands at the temples. Brace the core and squeeze the glutes. Raise the chest and shoulders off the floor by extending the spine. Hold the top position briefly. Lower the chest back to the floor with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Benefits: Builds lower back and glute strength.; Towel support increases range of motion.; No equipment needed beyond a towel.; Excellent home alternative to a hyper bench.; Improves spinal extension.; Carryover to deadlifts and back squats.; Reduces lower back stiffness.

Description: Lie on your back on the floor. Place the hands at the sides for support. Set the legs straight on the floor. Brace your core hard. Lift both straight legs up off the floor. Continue lifting all the way up to vertical. Squeeze the lower abs at the top. Lower the legs back down with control to just above the floor.
Benefits: Strong lower abs builder; No equipment needed; Full range of motion; Builds the rectus abdominis; Useful core builder; Trains hip flexors
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Hip flexors; Quadriceps

Description: Lie face down on a mat. Bend the knees and let them fall out wide to the sides. Press the soles of the feet together in a frog position. Rest your forehead on your hands. Brace your core and keep the upper body still. Squeeze the glutes to lift the bent legs off the floor. Hold the squeeze briefly at the top. Lower the legs back down with control.
Benefits: Strong glute activator; No equipment needed; Easy to add to a warm-up; Builds glute mind-muscle connection; Useful prone glute move; Trains hip extension
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus maximus; Hamstrings; Lower back

Description: Lie face down on the floor with arms at your sides or under your forehead. Extend your legs straight. Keep your feet hip-width apart. Brace your core gently to protect your lower back. Squeeze your glutes as hard as possible. Imagine cracking a walnut between your butt cheeks. Hold the squeeze for 3 to 5 seconds. Breathe normally. Release for 1 to 2 seconds. Repeat for 10 to 20 reps as a warm-up. This is purely a contraction drill — no movement, no equipment, no excuses.
Benefits: Activates the glutes and builds mind-muscle connection; Excellent warm-up before squats and hip thrusts; Helps lifters who struggle to feel their glutes; No equipment needed — works anywhere; Useful for rehabilitation; Takes less than two minutes

Description: Lie flat on your back with the legs extended. Place the hands at your sides for support. Brace the core and press the lower back to the floor. Keeping the legs straight, lift them up toward the ceiling. Stop when the legs are roughly vertical. Squeeze the abs at the top. Lower the legs back down with control without touching the floor. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
Benefits: Hammers the lower abs and hip flexors.; Builds core strength with a long lever.; No equipment needed.; Excellent foundation for hanging leg raises.; Trains the abs through a full range of motion.; Develops anterior core endurance.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Hip flexors; Obliques; Quadriceps

Description: Lie face down on the floor with legs extended and arms in front. Rest your forehead lightly on the ground. Brace your core and squeeze your glutes. Lift your chest, arms, and legs off the floor at the same time. Hold this top position for time. Keep your neck neutral by looking at the floor. Breathe steadily throughout the hold. Lower back down with control when the hold time is complete.
Benefits: Builds isometric posterior chain endurance; Strengthens the spinal erectors; Improves postural strength; No equipment required; Useful as a back-day finisher; Builds glute and hamstring endurance

Description: Set a decline bench with the head lower than the feet. Lie on the bench with the head at the lower end. Reach overhead and grip the top of the bench with both hands. Brace your core hard. Lift the legs up and curl the hips up off the bench. Continue until the hips are lifted high and legs are vertical. Squeeze the lower abs at the top. Lower the legs and hips back down with control.
Benefits: Strong lower abs builder; Decline angle adds load; Builds the rectus abdominis; Useful core builder; Strong bench move; Trains hip flexors
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Hip flexors; Obliques

Description: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat. Bend your elbows to 90 degrees. Position them at your sides on the floor. Drive your elbows hard into the floor, pressing down. This should lift your upper back slightly off the floor using your lats. Hold the lifted position for 2 to 3 seconds. Relax and lower. Focus on squeezing your lats to create the lift. Aim for 10 to 15 reps.
Benefits: Teaches lat engagement with zero equipment; Useful for developing pull-up mind-muscle connection; Beginner-friendly lat activation; Can be done anywhere; Develops lat awareness; Useful warm-up before pulling exercises
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi; Triceps brachii (elbow drive); Posterior deltoid; Rhomboids

Description: Lie face down on the lying leg curl machine. Adjust the ankle pad so it sits across the back of your lower legs, just above your heels. Position your knees just past the edge of the bench so they can pivot freely. Grip the handles in front of the bench and brace your core. Keep your hips pressed firmly against the pad. Curl your heels up toward your butt by bending only at the knees. Continue until your knees are fully bent. Squeeze your hamstrings hard for one second at the top. Lower the pad under control over two to three seconds back to the starting position with legs nearly straight. Stop just before the weight stack touches down to maintain tension on the hamstrings. Avoid lifting your hips off the pad to use body english — strict form is critical.
Benefits: Direct hamstring isolation with peak contraction at the top; Allows safe, comfortable training to muscular failure; Easy to load progressively in small increments; Builds the biceps femoris (knee-flexion specialist) heavily; Excellent accessory after squats or deadlifts; Trains the hamstrings without spinal load
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings (biceps femoris, semitendinosus, semimembranosus); Gastrocnemius (calf, secondary); Popliteus

Description: Lie on your back. Extend both legs straight, lifted a few inches off the floor. Press your lower back into the floor. Cross your right leg over your left leg. Open them and cross your left leg over your right. Continue alternating in a scissor-cross pattern. Keep both legs straight and off the floor. Move with control. Aim for 15 to 20 crosses per set.

Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis (lower); Hip adductors (crossing); Hip flexors; Obliques (slight)

Description: Lie on the back with the legs straight. Place the hands at the sides palms down. Brace your core and lift the legs slightly off the floor. Trace a figure eight pattern with both legs together. Move the legs up and to one side. Continue the figure eight curve down and across. Repeat the pattern continuously. Continue for the working set.
Benefits: Loads the lower abs; Trains multiple planes; Strong core drill; Builds the hip flexors; Useful core move
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Hip Flexors; Core

Description: Lie on your back, arms at your sides. Legs extended on the floor. Raise both legs up to vertical (90 degrees). At the top, curl your hips up — push your feet toward the ceiling. This lifts your hips off the floor. Lower your hips back down. Lower your legs back to the floor under control. That is one rep. The hip curl at the top is the key portion. Maintain lower back contact with the floor during the leg raise phase. Aim for 10 to 15 reps.

Exercise Name: Lying Leg Hip Raise on Floor
Description: Lie on the back with the legs extended. Place the arms at the sides palms down. Brace the core and press the lower back into the floor. Lift the legs straight up to vertical. Continue lifting by curling the hips off the floor. Drive the toes toward the ceiling at the top. Squeeze the abs hard at the peak. Lower with control to the start.
Benefits: Loads the lower abs hard.; Trains the hip flexors.; Bodyweight move requires no equipment.; Builds the rectus abdominis.; Useful core finisher.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Hip flexors; Obliques

Exercise Name: Lying Leg Hip Side Raise on Floor
Description: Lie on the back with the legs extended. Place the arms at the sides palms down. Brace the core and press the lower back into the floor. Lift the legs straight up to vertical. Curl the hips off the floor and angle them to one side. Drive the hips diagonally toward one shoulder. Squeeze the obliques hard at the top. Lower with control and alternate sides each rep.
Benefits: Hammers the obliques.; Trains the lower abs.; Bodyweight move.; Builds the side core.; Useful core variation.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Obliques; Rectus abdominis; Hip flexors

Description: Lie flat on your back on the floor with your legs straight and arms extended at your sides, palms down. Place your hands flat under your glutes for added lower-back support if needed. Brace your core hard. Press your lower back firmly into the floor and keep it there throughout the entire set. Lift both straight legs off the floor by contracting your abs and hip flexors. Keep your legs straight or with a slight bend in the knees. Continue lifting until your legs reach vertical (90 degrees) or as high as your range allows while keeping your lower back pressed into the floor. Pause briefly at the top, then lower the legs back down slowly under control over a count of two to three seconds. Stop just before your heels touch the floor — keep tension on the abs throughout the set. If your lower back lifts off the floor, you have lowered too far. Reduce the range until you can maintain back contact.

Description: Lie flat on your back with the legs extended. Place the hands at your sides for support. Brace the core and press the lower back to the floor. Keeping the legs straight, lift them up toward the ceiling. Stop when the legs are roughly vertical. Hold the top position for several seconds while squeezing the abs. Lower the legs back down with control to just above the floor. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Description: Lie on a flat bench with the hips near the end. Grip the sides of the bench above your head for support. Extend the legs straight out so they hang slightly off the end. Brace the core and press the lower back to the bench. Lift the legs up toward the ceiling keeping them straight. Stop when the legs are roughly vertical. Lower the legs back down past the bench line for a stretch. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Description: Lie face down on the floor or a bench. Extend the arms straight out to the sides forming a T. Set the palms facing down. Brace your core and keep the head neutral. Lift the arms up off the floor by squeezing the upper back. Hold the T position briefly at the top. Lower the arms back down with control. Keep the neck relaxed throughout.

Description: Lie flat on your back with the legs extended. Place the hands at your sides for support. Brace the core and press the lower back to the floor. Lift the legs up toward the ceiling keeping them straight. At the top, lower the legs to one side with control. Stop just above the floor on the side. Bring the legs back to center and lower them to the start. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.

Description: Lie face down on the floor or a bench. Bend the elbows and bring the upper arms close to the sides. Set the forearms angled out forming a W shape. Brace your core and keep the head neutral. Lift the arms off the floor by pulling the elbows back. Squeeze the upper back hard at the top. Hold the W position briefly. Lower the arms back down with control.

Description: Lie face down on the floor with the legs extended. Lift the chest slightly off the floor. Bring the arms into a W shape with elbows bent at the sides. Squeeze the shoulder blades to hold the W position. Slowly straighten the arms overhead into a Y position with thumbs up. Squeeze the lower traps at the Y position. Return to the W shape with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Description: Lie face down on the floor with the legs extended. Lift the chest slightly off the floor. Bring the arms into a W shape with elbows bent at the sides. Squeeze the shoulder blades to hold the W position. Slowly straighten the arms out to the sides into a T position. Squeeze the rear delts and traps at the T position. Return to the W shape with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Description: Lie face down on the floor. Arms extended out to the sides at shoulder height. Thumbs pointing up. Lift both arms as high as possible off the floor. Squeeze your shoulder blades together and your rear delts at the top. Hold for 1 to 2 seconds. Lower under control. The weight of your arms provides the resistance. Aim for 15 to 20 reps.

Description: Lie on the back with the knees bent and feet flat. Place the hands lightly on the lower abs. Brace your core and inhale to set the position. Exhale and curl the head and shoulders up. Focus on contracting the abs hard. Hold the contracted position for a beat. Lower with control to the start. Continue for the working set.

Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Obliques; Core

Description: Lie on your back with arms at your sides and legs extended. Lift both legs a few inches off the floor. Brace your abs hard. Crunch your shoulders off the floor. At the same time, raise your right leg up while lowering the left. In the next rep, switch the leg positions in a scissor kick. Maintain the elevated shoulders and continuous scissor kicks. Keep your lower back pressed to the floor throughout.

Description: Lie on your back. Press your lower back into the floor. Arms at your sides. Lift both legs 6 to 12 inches off the floor. Alternately raise one leg up (about 45 degrees) while the other stays low. Switch in a scissor pattern. Move with control — not speed. Keep both legs off the floor throughout. If your lower back arches, raise legs higher. Aim for 15 to 25 kicks per leg or work for time.

Description: Lie flat on your back on the floor. Place your hands at your sides or under your hips. Lift both legs off the floor a few inches. Keep the legs straight and brace your core hard. Cross one leg over the other in a scissor motion. Uncross and cross the other leg over. Continue alternating crosses with control. Keep the lower back pressed into the floor.

Description: Lie flat on your back with the arms out to the sides. Lift the legs and bend the knees at ninety degrees. Brace the core and press the upper back into the floor. Lower the bent knees to one side with control. Stop just before the knees touch the floor. Use the obliques to bring the knees back to the center. Lower the knees to the other side. Continue alternating for the desired number of repetitions.

Description: Lie flat on your back with the legs extended. Place the hands at your sides for support. Brace the core and press the lower back to the floor. Lift one leg up toward the ceiling keeping it straight. As the first leg lowers, lift the other leg up. Pass the legs at the midline of the body. Continue the scissor motion smoothly. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions per leg.

Simultaneously lower the other leg toward the floor. Switch the leg positions in a continuous motion. Keep the legs straight throughout. Continue the alternating raises for the working set.

Description: Position yourself face down on the lying leg curl machine. Place the back of your right calf against the roller pad. Grip the handles or the bench for stability. Brace your core and press your hips into the bench. Curl your right heel up toward your glute by bending the knee. Squeeze your right hamstring hard at the top. Lower the leg back down with control to a fully extended starting position. Complete reps on one leg, then switch.

Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings; Gluteus maximus; Gastrocnemius

Description: Lie flat on your back with both legs extended. Place your hands under your glutes or at your sides. Press your lower back into the floor. Brace your core. Lift your right leg straight up toward the ceiling, keeping it straight. Continue until your right leg is vertical (or as high as your range allows). Lower your right leg under control over two to three seconds. Stop just before your heel touches the floor. Keep your left leg flat on the floor throughout. Complete all reps on the right, then switch to the left. If your lower back lifts off the floor, reduce the range of the descent.

Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis (especially lower portion); Hip flexors (iliopsoas); Quadriceps (keeping leg straight); Transverse abdominis

Exercise Name: Lying Single Leg Reverse Biceps Curl with Towel
Description: Lie on your back with the legs extended. Loop a towel under the arch of one foot. Grip both ends of the towel with one hand using an overhand grip. Lift the leg slightly off the floor for tension. Brace the core and keep the upper arm fixed. Curl the hand toward the shoulder by bending the elbow. Squeeze the biceps and forearms at the top. Lower with control and repeat for all reps then switch sides.

Description: Lie on the back with the legs straight. Place the hands at the sides palms down. Brace your core and keep the lower back on the floor. Lift one straight leg up toward ninety degrees. Lower the leg with control to the floor. Lift the other leg up to ninety degrees. Continue alternating in a marching pattern. Keep the motion controlled throughout.

Description: Lie on your back with both legs raised, knees bent at 90 degrees (tabletop position). Press your lower back into the floor. Arms at your sides. Slowly lower your right foot toward the floor, keeping the 90-degree knee bend. Lightly tap your right toe on the floor. Return to the tabletop position. Repeat with your left foot. Continue alternating. Maintain lower back contact with the floor. Aim for 10 to 15 taps per side.

Description: Sit on the ab coaster machine with feet on the foot pad. Hold the handles at the top of the machine. Keep your arms straight and your torso slightly leaned back. Brace your core and engage your lower abs. Tuck your knees up and forward toward your chest. Squeeze the lower abs hard at the top. Lower the knees back down with control. Maintain tension in the abs throughout.

Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Hip flexors; Obliques

Description: Lie face down on a lying leg curl machine with both legs under the pad. Adjust the pad to sit just above the heels. Grip the handles for stability. Brace your core and keep your hips pressed into the pad. Curl the weight up using both legs until the heels approach the glutes. Pause briefly at the top. Lift one leg off the pad while leaving the other under it. Slowly lower the weight back to the start with just one leg.

Description: Sit on a hip abduction machine with your back against the pad. Place the pads on the outside of your knees. Adjust the start position to a comfortable narrow stance. Grip the handles for stability. Brace your core and keep your back against the pad. Push your knees outward to spread the pads apart. Squeeze the outer glutes hard at full abduction. Slowly return to the start position with control.

Description: Sit at the leverage curl machine with elbows on the elbow pad. Grip the handles with palms facing up. Brace your core and pin your chest to the support. Curl the right handle up by bending only at the elbow. Squeeze the right bicep hard at the top. Lower the right handle back down with control. Curl the left handle up while the right stays at the bottom. Alternate sides each rep with strict form.

Muscles Worked (Raw): Biceps brachii; Brachialis; Brachioradialis

Description: Set the assisted pull up machine with appropriate counterweight. Stand on the kneeling pad or platform. Grip the chin up handles with palms facing you (underhand grip). Brace your core and pull your shoulders back. Pull your body up by bending at the elbows and driving them down. Continue until your chin clears the bar level. Squeeze your back and biceps at the top. Lower yourself back down with control to a full hang.

Description: Adjust the machine so the pivot point aligns with your hips. Position the resistance pad across your upper back. Brace your core. Start in the hinged-forward position with your torso bent. Extend your torso up by contracting your lower back and glutes. Push against the pad. Continue until your body forms a straight line. Do not hyperextend beyond straight. Squeeze your glutes and lower back at the top for one second. Lower under control back to the starting hinged position. Stop just before the weight stack touches down. Repeat for the desired number of reps.

Description: Set up a lever chest press machine with the desired weight loaded. Anchor resistance bands to the base of the machine. Loop the bands over the press handles or your wrists. Sit on the seat with your back firmly against the pad. Grip the handles at chest level with palms facing forward. Brace your core. Press the handles forward by extending your arms against both the weight and band tension. Lower the handles back to the starting position with control.
Benefits: Accommodating resistance through the press; Overloads the lockout; Builds pressing power; Different stimulus than standard machine press; Combines machine stability with band tension; Useful for strength specialization
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Triceps brachii; Anterior deltoid

Description: Step onto the belt squat machine platform. Attach the loading belt around your hips and clip it to the machine’s weight arm. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart on the platform. Grip the handles for balance. Brace your core and lift your chest. Release the safety mechanism. Squat down by bending at the knees and hips. Keep your torso upright. Descend until your thighs are parallel to the platform or deeper. Drive through your full foot to stand back up. Squeeze your glutes at the top. Repeat for the desired number of reps. Re-engage the safety before stepping off. Adjust foot position and stance width to bias different muscles.
Benefits: Zero spinal compression — the most back-friendly squat variation; Allows heavy quad and glute loading without back stress; Excellent for lifters with lower-back, shoulder, or wrist issues; Allows deeper squatting for many lifters; Trains the legs without upper-body involvement; Useful for high-volume leg work alongside heavy back squats
Muscles Worked (Raw): Quadriceps; Gluteus maximus; Hamstrings (secondary); Adductors; Calves (secondary)

Description: Adjust the seat height so your upper arms rest flat on the arm pad when seated. Sit with your chest against the pad and your upper arms along the angled surface. Grip the handles with an underhand grip. Brace your core. Keep your upper arms pressed firmly against the pad throughout. Curl the handles up by bending only at the elbows. Keep your upper arms still. Continue until your forearms are roughly vertical or the handles are near your shoulders. Squeeze your biceps hard. Lower the handles under control over two to three seconds. Stop just before the weight stack touches down. Maintain tension throughout the set. Repeat for the desired number of reps. Aim for 10 to 15 reps per set.
Benefits: Eliminates all body english — strict bicep isolation; Guided path makes it easy to feel the target muscle; Allows safe training to failure with no spotter needed; Easy to load progressively in small increments; Excellent for beginners learning bicep contraction; Useful for high-rep volume and drop sets
Muscles Worked (Raw): Biceps brachii (long and short heads); Brachialis; Brachioradialis (secondary); Forearm flexors

Description: Sit at the leverage curl machine and adjust the seat to align elbows with the pivot. Place your upper arms on the elbow pad with the chest pressed against the support. Grip the handles with palms facing up. Brace your core and pull your shoulders back. Curl the handles up by bending at the elbows. Continue until your forearms are roughly vertical. Squeeze the biceps hard at the top. Lower the handles back down with control to full extension.
Benefits: Fixed motion path eliminates form errors; Constant tension through the range; Builds bicep size and strength; Allows progressive heavy loading; Beginner-friendly bicep variation; Useful for hypertrophy training
Muscles Worked (Raw): Biceps brachii; Brachialis; Brachioradialis; Forearm flexors

Description: Adjust the leverage chair squat machine to set your starting depth. Step onto the platform. Position the shoulder pads on your upper traps. Grip the handles. Brace your core. Lift your chest. Squat down by bending at the knees and hips. The machine guides the path. Descend until you sit briefly on the chair pad or reach the depth target. Drive through your full foot to stand back up. Do not lock your knees fully at the top. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Benefits: Guided squat path for beginners; Provides support during the lift; Useful for rehabilitation and elderly trainees; Eliminates balance demand of free-weight squats; Easy to load progressively; Safer for those new to squatting
Muscles Worked (Raw): Quadriceps; Gluteus maximus; Hamstrings (secondary); Core (stabilizer)

Description: Sit in the chest press machine. Adjust the seat so the handles are at mid-chest height. Load the desired weight on the plate pegs. Grip the handles with an overhand grip. Pull your shoulder blades back and down. Press the handles forward by extending your arms. Lock out at full extension. Squeeze your chest and triceps. Slowly return the handles to the starting position under control. Maintain chest contact with the back pad throughout. Aim for 10 to 12 reps per set.
Benefits: Guided pressing path removes stabilizer demands; Allows heavier loading for chest isolation; Safe for solo training; Easy to load progressively; Useful for beginners and hypertrophy focus; Comfortable seated position
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Triceps brachii; Anterior deltoid; Serratus anterior

Description: Adjust the seat height so the handles align with your lower chest when seated. Sit with your back firmly against the pad. Grip the handles. Plant your feet flat. Pull your shoulders down and back. Brace your core. Press the handles forward and slightly downward by extending at the elbows. Continue until your arms are nearly fully extended. Do not lock your elbows. Lower the handles under control back to the start position. Maintain tension throughout. Stop just before the weight stack touches down. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Benefits: Targets the lower chest with guided motion; Allows safe training to failure without a spotter; Eliminates stabilizer demand for pure pressing focus; Easy to load progressively; Useful as a finisher after compound pressing; Reduces shoulder involvement vs flat pressing
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major (especially the sternal/lower head); Triceps brachii; Anterior deltoid (reduced); Serratus anterior

Description: Sit at the leverage chest crossover machine. Adjust the seat so your shoulders align with the pivot points. Grip the handles with arms extended out to the sides. Brace your core and pull your shoulders back. Maintain a slight bend in the elbows throughout. Bring the handles together in front of your chest in a wide arc. Squeeze your chest hard at the top. Slowly return to the starting position with control.
Benefits: Fixed motion path eliminates form errors; Constant machine resistance; Builds chest size; Strong peak contraction; Allows progressive heavy loading; Useful for hypertrophy training
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Anterior deltoid; Serratus anterior

Description: Step onto the donkey calf raise machine. Place the balls of your feet on the edge of the foot platform with heels hanging off. Position the padded lever across your lower back (hips, not spine). Grip the handles. Your torso should be bent forward at roughly 90 degrees with your back flat. Let your heels drop as low as possible into a deep calf stretch. Push through the balls of your feet to rise up onto your toes as high as possible. Squeeze your calves hard at the top for one to two seconds. Lower under control back to the deep stretch over two to three seconds. Repeat for 12 to 20+ reps per set.
Benefits: Hip-flexed position stretches the gastrocnemius more than standing raises; Adjustable machine loading for progressive overload; Deep stretch at the bottom drives growth; Guided motion provides consistent form; Excellent calf mass builder; Easier to set up than partner donkey calf raises
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gastrocnemius (medial and lateral heads); Soleus (secondary); Tibialis posterior (stabilizer)

Description: Position yourself in the gripless shrug machine with shoulder pads on top of your shoulders. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart on the platform. Position your hands lightly on the handles or by your sides. Unrack the machine by extending your legs. Brace your core and pull your shoulders back. Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears. Hold the contraction at the top for one count. Lower the load back down slowly with control.
Benefits: No grip required allows extreme loads; Heavy trap loading possible; Strict trap isolation; Builds upper trap mass; Useful for hypertrophy training; Strong peak contraction
Muscles Worked (Raw): Trapezius (upper); Levator scapulae; Rhomboids

Description: Set up the leverage squat machine with the desired plate load. Position yourself under the shoulder pads with feet on the platform. Set your feet shoulder-width apart on the platform. Unrack the machine by rotating the handles or releasing the safety. Brace your core and pull the shoulder pads tight to your body. Squat down as deep as your mobility allows. Drive up through your heels to stand back to the starting position. Re-rack the safety when finished.
Benefits: Fixed motion path provides stability; Builds quad and glute strength; Deep range targets full leg development; Allows heavy loading; Beginner-friendly squat variation; Useful for lifters with balance limitations
Muscles Worked (Raw): Quadriceps; Gluteus maximus; Hamstrings; Adductors

Description: Adjust the seat so the handles align with your upper chest when seated. Sit with your back firmly against the pad. Grip the handles at shoulder-width. Plant your feet flat. Brace your core. Press the handles forward and slightly up by extending your arms. Lock out at the end with arms fully extended. Squeeze your upper chest at the lockout. Slowly return the handles to the start under control. Stop before the weight stack touches down to maintain tension.
Benefits: Targets the upper (clavicular) chest; Guided path with stable loading; Easy to load progressively; Allows focus on pressing strength without stabilization; Safer to fail without a spotter; Excellent for high-volume work
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major (clavicular/upper head); Anterior deltoid; Triceps brachii; Serratus anterior

Description: Adjust the seat height so the handles align with your upper chest when seated. Sit with your back firmly against the pad. Grip the handles with an overhand grip. Plant your feet flat on the floor. Pull your shoulders down and back. Brace your core. Press the handles forward and up by extending at the elbows. Exhale as you press. Continue until your arms are nearly fully extended. Do not lock your elbows. Lower the handles under control back to the start position over two seconds. Stop just before the weight stack touches down. Maintain tension throughout. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Benefits: Direct upper-chest focus with guided motion; Eliminates stabilizer demand — pure pressing focus; Allows safe training to failure with no spotter; Easy to load progressively in small increments; Useful for beginners and for high-volume work; Back support reduces lower-back involvement
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major (especially the clavicular/upper head); Anterior deltoid; Triceps brachii; Serratus anterior

Description: Adjust the seat height so the handles align with your upper chest when seated. Sit with your back firmly against the pad. Grip the handles with arms extended out to your sides. Brace your core, lift your chest, and pull your shoulders down and back into the pad. Bring the handles together in front of your upper chest by squeezing your chest. Keep a slight elbow bend fixed throughout. Continue until the handles meet in front of your upper chest. Squeeze your chest hard for one second. Slowly let the handles travel back out under control. Feel the stretch in your upper chest at the end range. Stop just before the weight stack touches down to maintain tension. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Benefits: Direct upper-chest isolation with guided motion; Eliminates stabilizer demand — pure chest focus; Provides a deep stretch and peak contraction; Allows safe training to muscular failure; Easy to load progressively in small increments; Easier to set up than dumbbell incline flys
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major (especially the clavicular/upper head); Anterior deltoid (secondary); Serratus anterior

Description: Set up a torso rotation machine with desired weight. Kneel on the seat or floor as the machine allows. Position your torso in the pad with arms hooked over the handles. Brace your core and sit tall. Rotate your torso toward one side against the machine resistance. Continue until you reach the end of the rotation range. Squeeze the obliques at the end of the rotation. Slowly return to the starting position. Complete reps then switch sides.
Benefits: Direct loaded oblique work; Eliminates lower body contribution; Builds rotational core strength; Constant resistance through the range; Easy to scale by changing weight; Useful for oblique specialization
Muscles Worked (Raw): Obliques (internal and external); Rectus abdominis; Quadratus lumborum

Description: Adjust the seat so the handles align with your mid-chest when seated. Sit with your back firmly against the pad. Grip the handles. Plant your feet flat. Brace your core. Press the handles forward by extending your arms. As you press, the handles converge toward each other in the middle. Squeeze your inner chest hard at the lockout. Slowly return the handles to the start under control. Stop before the weight stack touches down to maintain tension.
Benefits: Targets the inner pectoral fibers; Converging path mimics a bench-and-fly hybrid; Guided path allows focus on the chest; Easy to load progressively; Excellent for inner chest development; Safer than free-weight variations
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major (inner fibers emphasis); Triceps brachii; Anterior deltoid; Serratus anterior

Description: Sit on the Hammer Strength incline press machine with your back against the pad. Adjust the seat so the handles are at upper chest level. Grip the handles with a neutral or pronated grip. Brace your core and keep your feet flat on the floor. Press the handles forward and upward. Lock out the arms at full extension. Squeeze the upper chest at the top. Lower the handles slowly back to the start.
Benefits: Targets the upper chest; Allows heavy loading; Safe and stable; Fixed press path; Useful for hypertrophy; Reduces shoulder strain
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major (upper); Front deltoid; Triceps brachii

Description: Adjust the seat height so that the arm pads align with the outside of your upper arms. Sit with your back firmly against the pad and place the outsides of your upper arms against the arm pads. Grip the handles if provided. Brace your core and pull your shoulders down. Lift the pads out to your sides by abducting your arms. Keep your torso upright — do not lean. Continue lifting until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor. Pause briefly at the top. Squeeze your side delts. Lower the pads under control over two to three seconds. Stop just before the weight stack touches down. Repeat for the desired number of reps. Aim for 12 to 20 reps per set.
Benefits: Strict side-delt isolation with no cheating possible; Constant resistance throughout the range of motion; Easy to load progressively in small increments; Eliminates the temptation to use momentum or body swing; Excellent for high-rep side-delt finishing work; Easier to feel the target muscle than dumbbell raises
Muscles Worked (Raw): Lateral deltoid; Anterior deltoid (secondary); Supraspinatus (rotator cuff, initial range)

Exercise Name: Machine Lying Banded T Bar Row
Description: Set up on a chest supported T bar machine. Loop a resistance band around the bar handle. Anchor the band low on the machine. Lie face down on the pad with chest supported. Grip the handles with both hands. Brace your core and pinch the shoulder blades. Pull the handles up to the lower ribs. Squeeze the lats hard at the top. Lower with control.
Benefits: Builds the upper back; Adds band tension; Strong T bar variation; Chest supported; Useful for back size; Trains the biceps
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi; Biceps brachii; Rhomboids; Trapezius

Description: Lie face down on the lever T-bar row machine with chest on the pad. Plant your feet on the foot platform and pin your hips down. Grip the handles with palms facing each other. Brace your core and let your arms hang down fully. Row the handles toward your ribs by driving the elbows back. Squeeze the upper back hard at the top of the row. Lower with control until arms are straight again. Keep your chest pinned to the pad throughout.
Benefits: Removes lower back stress; Builds upper back size; Strict chest-supported form; Excellent back hypertrophy move; Easy to load heavy; Strong back day staple
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi; Rhomboids; Middle trapezius; Biceps brachii

Description: Lie on the lying crunch machine with your back flat on the pad. Position the roller pads behind your shoulders or at your chest, depending on the machine. Grip the handles above your head or at your sides. Crunch your torso forward by flexing your spine against the machine resistance. Squeeze your abs hard at the peak of the crunch. Lower under control back to the flat position. Maintain constant tension. Do not let the weight stack rest between reps. Aim for 12 to 15 reps per set.
Benefits: Loaded supine crunch with machine resistance; Easy to load progressively; Mimics floor crunch with added resistance; Simple execution; Comfortable supine position; Excellent for ab hypertrophy
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Obliques (secondary); Hip flexors (slight)

Exercise Name: Machine One Arm Side Chest Press
Description: Sit on a lever chest press machine sideways to one side. Set the seat so the handle is at chest height. Grip the handle with the hand closest to the machine. Brace your core and keep the chest tall. Press the handle forward and across the body. Squeeze the chest hard at full extension. Pause briefly at lockout. Return with control. Complete reps and switch sides.
Benefits: Strong unilateral chest builder; Constant lever resistance; Adds chest stretch; Builds chest size; Strong machine move; Trains the obliques
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Anterior deltoid; Triceps brachii

Exercise Name: Machine One Arm Lateral High Row
Description: Sit on a lever high row machine with the chest pad against the body. Grip a single handle with one hand. Set the arm extended up and out at the start. Brace your core and pinch the shoulder blade. Pull the handle down and back driving the elbow past the body. Squeeze the lat hard at the bottom. Return with control to the start. Complete reps and switch sides.
Benefits: Strong unilateral lat builder; Builds back symmetry; Trains the rhomboids; Builds back size; Useful back move; Strong machine move
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi; Rhomboids; Posterior deltoid; Biceps brachii

Description: Sit on the lever dip machine with the handles set to a comfortable height. Grip the handles with an overhand (palms-down) grip. Keep your back flat against the pad. Brace your core and keep your chest up. Press the handles down by extending the elbows. Continue pressing until your arms are nearly locked out. Squeeze the triceps hard at the bottom. Allow the handles to return to the start with control.
Benefits: Strong triceps isolation; Stable, guided machine path; Reduces stabilization demand; Beginner-friendly dip variation; Easy to load progressively; Builds triceps mass
Muscles Worked (Raw): Triceps brachii (long head); Triceps brachii (lateral head); Triceps brachii (medial head)

Description: Sit at a leverage chest press machine with parallel handles. Adjust the seat so the handles align with your mid chest. Grip the parallel handles with palms facing each other. Pull your shoulders back and brace your core. Press the handles forward until your arms are fully extended. Squeeze your chest at the top. Lower the handles back to chest level with control. Maintain the neutral grip throughout the entire set.
Benefits: Neutral grip is shoulder-friendly; Fixed motion path eliminates balance demands; Builds chest size and strength; Useful for sensitive shoulders; Allows progressive heavy loading; Beginner-friendly chest variation
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Triceps brachii; Anterior deltoid

Description: Set up the leverage squat machine with light or no plate load. Position yourself under the shoulder pads with one foot on the platform. Lift the other leg out in front of you, keeping it extended. Brace your core and grip the handles for stability. Lower into a single-leg squat by bending the working knee. Keep the non-working leg extended forward throughout. Continue down until your working thigh is parallel to the platform or deeper. Drive up through your working heel to stand back to the starting position. Switch legs.
Benefits: Builds single-leg strength with support; Stepping stone to bodyweight pistol squats; Reduces balance and mobility demands; Heavily loads quads and glutes; Corrects left-right imbalances; Useful for beginners working toward pistols
Muscles Worked (Raw): Quadriceps; Gluteus maximus; Hamstrings; Adductors; Core

Description: Set up the vertical row machine with chest pad and foot platform in place. Stand with chest against the pad and feet on the platform. Grip the handles with palms facing up. Let your arms hang straight down with shoulder blades retracted. Brace your core and pin your chest to the pad. Row the handles up toward your sides. Squeeze the lats and biceps at the top of the row. Lower with control until arms are straight again.
Benefits: Biases lower lats and biceps; Chest-supported strict form; Builds back thickness; Easy to load heavy; Excellent back day move; Wrist-friendly grip
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi; Biceps brachii; Rhomboids; Middle trapezius

Description: Lie face down on the lever T-bar row machine. Plant your feet on the platform and pin your chest to the pad. Grip the handles with palms facing up in an underhand grip. Let your arms hang straight down. Brace your core and keep your hips planted. Row the handles up toward your hips by driving the elbows back. Squeeze the lats and biceps at the top of the row. Lower with control until arms are straight.
Benefits: Biases lower lats and biceps; Chest-supported strict form; Builds back thickness; Excellent back day move; Wrist-friendly grip; Easy to load heavy
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi; Biceps brachii; Rhomboids; Middle trapezius

Description: Position yourself in the lever rotary calf machine with feet on the platform. Adjust the load to your appropriate working weight. Place the balls of your feet on the platform with heels off the edge. Position the shoulder pads (if seated) or grips for stability. Brace your core. Lower your heels below the platform level for a stretch. Raise your heels as high as possible against the machine resistance. Squeeze your calves hard at the top, then lower with control.
Benefits: Constant machine resistance through the range; Strong stretch with elevated foot position; Builds calf size and strength; Allows progressive heavy loading; Useful for hypertrophy training; Easy setup and progression
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gastrocnemius; Soleus; Tibialis posterior

Description: Sit in the crunch machine. Adjust the seat so the pad is at your upper chest level. Place your chest or shoulders against the front pad. Grip the handles. Sit up tall against the back pad to start. Crunch forward by flexing your spine — drive the pad forward and down. Squeeze your abs hard at the bottom of the crunch. Slowly return to the starting position under control. Do not use momentum — squeeze and control every rep. Use moderate weight. Aim for 12 to 15 reps per set.
Benefits: Loaded ab flexion with machine guidance; Easy to load progressively; Safe for the lower back; Isolates the abs effectively; Simple setup and execution; Useful for ab hypertrophy
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Obliques (secondary); Hip flexors (slight)

Description: Adjust the seat so the handles or arm pads align with your mid-chest when seated. Sit with your back against the pad. Place your forearms against the arm pads or grip the handles. Set a slight bend in your elbows. Pull your shoulders down and back. Brace your core. Bring the pads or handles together in front of your chest by squeezing your pecs. Continue until the pads meet. Squeeze your chest hard for one second. Slowly let the pads travel back out under control. Feel the stretch at the end range. Stop just before the weight stack touches down. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Benefits: Strict chest isolation with guided motion; Deep stretch and peak contraction; Allows safe training to failure; Easy to load progressively; Excellent finisher after compound pressing; Easier to set up than dumbbell flys
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Anterior deltoid (secondary); Serratus anterior

Description: Sit on a lever ab crunch machine with the resistance set. Position the body so the left side faces the lever. Grip the handles and set the chest pad against the torso. Brace your core and set the feet under the foot pads. Crunch the torso to the left bending sideways. Squeeze the left obliques hard at the bottom. Hold briefly at the contracted position. Return to the start with control. Complete reps.
Benefits: Strong oblique isolation; Constant lever resistance; Easy to scale loading; Builds the obliques; Useful core builder; Strong machine move
Muscles Worked (Raw): Obliques; Quadratus lumborum; Rectus abdominis

Description: Sit on the ab crunch machine with your back against the pad. Grip the handles or place your arms over the chest pad. Adjust the seat height so the pad sits across your chest. Brace your core and keep your hips planted. Crunch your torso forward by contracting the abs. Continue forward until you feel a strong contraction. Squeeze the abs hard at the bottom. Return slowly to the start, controlling the eccentric.
Benefits: Loads the abs with constant resistance; Stable, guided path; Reduces lower back stress; Builds ab thickness; Easy to load progressively; Useful for ab hypertrophy
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Obliques; Hip flexors

Description: Sit on a lever ab crunch machine with the resistance set. Position the body so the right side faces the lever. Grip the handles and set the chest pad against the torso. Brace your core and set the feet under the foot pads. Crunch the torso to the right bending sideways. Squeeze the right obliques hard at the bottom. Hold briefly at the contracted position. Return to the start with control. Complete reps.
Benefits: Strong oblique isolation; Constant lever resistance; Easy to scale loading; Builds the obliques; Useful core builder; Strong machine move
Muscles Worked (Raw): Obliques; Quadratus lumborum; Rectus abdominis

Description: Adjust the seat height and chest-pad position so you can reach the handles with arms fully extended while your chest is pressed against the pad. Sit down and press your chest firmly against the pad. Grip the handles — most machines offer multiple grip options. Brace your core, pull your shoulders down and back, and set your start position. Pull the handles toward your torso by driving your elbows back. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the row. Pause briefly with the handles close to your body. Keep your chest pressed against the pad throughout. Slowly extend your arms back to the start position under control. Feel the stretch in your lats. Stop just before the weight stack touches down to maintain tension. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Benefits: Eliminates lower-back demand — pure mid-back focus; Allows safe, comfortable training to muscular failure; Multiple grip options bias different back muscles; Easy to load progressively in small increments; Excellent for high-rep volume work; Easier to maintain strict form than free-weight rows
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi; Trapezius (middle and lower); Rhomboids; Posterior deltoid; Biceps brachii and brachialis; Forearms and grip

Description: Adjust the seat height so the handles are at roughly shoulder height when seated. Sit with your back firmly against the pad. Grip the handles with an overhand grip. Brace your core, pull your shoulders down and back, and plant your feet flat on the floor. Press the handles straight up by extending at the elbows and shoulders. Exhale as you press. Continue pressing until your arms are fully extended overhead (or nearly so). Do not hyperextend. Lower the handles under control back to shoulder height over two seconds. Stop just before the weight stack touches down to maintain tension on the shoulders. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Benefits: Guided path and back support allow pure shoulder focus; Eliminates core and lower-back demand; Allows safe training to failure with no spotter needed; Easy to load progressively in small increments; Excellent for beginners learning the pressing pattern; Useful for high-volume shoulder training
Muscles Worked (Raw): Anterior deltoid; Lateral deltoid; Triceps brachii; Upper trapezius (secondary); Serratus anterior

Description: Sit on a hip abduction machine with the back flat against the pad. Set the outer thighs against the leg pads. Grip the handles for stability. Brace your core and set the feet on the foot platforms. Press the legs out to the sides spreading the pads apart. Squeeze the glute medius hard at the end range. Hold the contracted position briefly. Return to the start with control.
Benefits: Strong glute medius builder; Constant lever resistance; Easy to scale loading; Builds hip stability; Useful glute isolation; Strong machine move
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus medius; Gluteus maximus; Tensor fasciae latae

Description: Step into a lever standing calf raise machine. Position the shoulder pads firmly on your upper traps. Place the balls of your feet on the raised step with heels hanging off. Stand tall with knees slightly bent. Allow your heels to drop below the platform for a full stretch. Brace your core. Press up through the balls of your feet, lifting your heels as high as possible. Squeeze the calves at the top, then lower the heels back down with control.
Benefits: Heavy loading for calf size; Full range from a step; Builds calf strength and size; Plate-loaded for progressive overload; Strong calf isolation; Useful for calf specialization
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gastrocnemius; Soleus; Tibialis posterior

Description: Stand on the platform of the hip extension machine with your left foot. Position your right leg against the padded lever behind you. Grip the handles for stability. Stand tall with core braced. Press your right leg back and up against the lever by extending at the hip. Keep your torso upright. Continue extending until your right thigh is behind your body. Squeeze your right glute hard. Slowly let the lever return under control. Do not let the weight stack slam. Complete all reps on the right side, then switch. Keep the movement slow and controlled — momentum reduces glute activation. Use moderate weight and higher reps (12 to 20).
Benefits: Direct glute isolation with guided motion; No lower-back involvement; Trains one side at a time, exposing imbalances; Easy to load progressively; Excellent finisher for glute workouts; Useful for rehabilitation and glute activation
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus maximus; Hamstrings (secondary); Core (stabilizer)

Description: Sit on the seat of the lever seated squat machine. Place your back firmly against the back pad. Position your feet on the platform shoulder-width apart. Grip the handles for stability. Unrack the safety and brace your core. Squat the platform away by bending your knees. Continue until your thighs are roughly perpendicular to the platform. Drive through your heels to extend your legs back to the starting position. Re-rack the safety.
Benefits: Heavy quad loading with full back support; Eliminates balance demands; Reduces lower back stress; Allows progressive heavy weight; Useful for lifters with back limitations; Builds quad size and strength
Muscles Worked (Raw): Quadriceps; Gluteus maximus; Adductors

Description: Stand on the lever leg raise machine with one foot on the platform. Position the pad on the front of the working leg thigh. Grip the handles for stability. Stand tall with chest up. Brace your core and keep your standing leg slightly bent. Lift the working leg by driving the knee up against the pad. Continue until the thigh is parallel to the floor or higher. Lower slowly back to the start. Complete reps on one side before switching.
Benefits: Loads hip flexion; Builds hip flexor strength; Trains the lower abs; Functional standing position; Useful for runners; Improves hip drive
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hip flexors; Quadriceps; Rectus abdominis (lower)

Description: Stand at a lever rear kick machine and grip the handles. Set one foot under the lever pad. Brace your core and set the chest tall. Keep the working leg slightly bent. Kick the leg straight back driving the pad up. Squeeze the glute hard at the top. Hold the contracted position briefly. Lower back to the start with control. Complete reps and switch sides.
Benefits: Strong glute isolation; Constant lever resistance; Easy to scale loading; Builds the gluteus maximus; Useful glute builder; Strong machine move
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus maximus; Hamstrings; Spinal erectors

Description: Adjust the seat so your upper arms rest flat on the arm pad when seated, elbows aligned with the pivot point. Sit with your back against the pad. Grip the handles with both hands. Brace your core. Keep your upper arms pressed firmly against the pad throughout. Extend at the elbows to push the handles forward and down until your arms are fully extended. Squeeze your triceps hard at the bottom for one second. Slowly bend at the elbows to return the handles to the start position over two to three seconds. Stop just before the weight stack touches down. Maintain tension throughout. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Benefits: Strict tricep isolation with no body english; Guided path makes it easy to feel the target muscle; Allows safe training to failure; Easy to load progressively; Excellent for beginners and high-rep volume work; Useful for drop sets and giant sets

Description: Stand 3 to 6 feet from a sturdy wall (or partner) with feet shoulder-width apart. Hold a medicine ball at chest height with both hands. Elbows pointing out. Pull yourself up using one arm until your chin clears the bar. Lower under control. This takes years of training to achieve. Progress through: weighted chin-ups → assisted one-arm (band) → negatives → full reps. Even 1 rep is an elite achievement. Requires extreme relative strength.
Benefits: One of the hardest bodyweight exercises; Requires extraordinary pulling strength; Elite calisthenics achievement; Builds elite lat and bicep strength; No equipment beyond a bar; Impressive strength demonstration
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi (extreme); Biceps brachii (extreme); Brachialis; Forearms and grip (extreme); Core (anti-rotation)

Description: Sit on the edge of a bench. Place your right hand on the bench beside your hip. Place your left hand behind your back or at your side. Extend your legs forward. Support your weight on your right arm. Lower your body by bending your right elbow. Descend until your right elbow is at about 90 degrees. Press back up using only your right arm. Complete reps, then switch arms. This is very advanced. Start with two-arm dips first. Aim for 3 to 6 reps.
Benefits: Builds extreme unilateral tricep strength; Advanced pressing exercise; Develops shoulder stability per arm; No equipment beyond a bench; Impressive bodyweight skill; Exposes left-right imbalances
Muscles Worked (Raw): Triceps brachii (heavy); Anterior deltoid; Pectoralis major (lower); Core (anti-rotation)

Description: Begin in a high plank position with hands under the shoulders. Set the body in a straight line from head to heels. Set the feet wider than the hips for stability. Brace your core hard and keep the hips level. Shift the weight slightly to one arm. Lift the other arm off the floor and reach it forward. Hold the one arm position with the body steady. Place the arm back down. Complete time and switch sides.
Benefits: Brutal anti-rotation core move; Builds shoulder stability; Trains the obliques; No equipment needed; Strong unilateral core builder; Useful core finisher
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Obliques; Anterior deltoid; Serratus anterior

Description: Grip a pull-up bar with your right hand only. Overhand grip. Let your body hang freely. Left arm at your side. Engage your shoulder — do not let it passively hang from the joint. Pack your shoulder down. Hold for as long as possible. Switch hands. Start with 10 to 15 seconds and build up. Use chalk if needed for grip. This is significantly harder than a two-arm hang.
Benefits: Builds elite grip strength per hand; Develops shoulder stability and health; Decompresses the spine; Progression toward one-arm pull-ups; Reveals left-right grip imbalances; Builds lat engagement per arm
Muscles Worked (Raw): Forearms and grip (extreme per hand); Latissimus dorsi (stabilizer); Rotator cuff; Biceps brachii; Core (anti-rotation)

Description: Stand on a step with the ball of your right foot on the edge. Bend at the waist and support yourself on a bench or rack. Tuck your left foot behind your right ankle. Lower your right heel as far as possible for a full stretch. Press through the ball of your foot to raise as high as possible. Squeeze your calf at the top. Lower under control. Complete reps, then switch legs. A partner can sit on your lower back for added load. Aim for 15 to 20 reps per leg.
Benefits: Doubles the calf demand per leg; Bent-over position targets the gastrocnemius; Partner can add load by sitting on your back; Exposes left-right calf imbalances; No machine needed; Unique old-school calf exercise
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gastrocnemius (working leg); Soleus; Achilles tendon

Description: Stand on one leg with the other foot lifted. Place a hand on a wall for balance if needed. Brace your core and keep the working leg straight. Press up onto the ball of the foot. Squeeze the calf hard at the top. Lower with control to the floor. Keep the motion smooth. Finish all reps then switch sides.
Benefits: Builds the calves; Trains each side; No equipment needed; Strong calf basic; Useful for travel
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gastrocnemius; Soleus; Calves

Description: Stand on your right leg. Left leg slightly forward or to the side. Bend your right knee to about 45 degrees — roughly one-quarter depth. Drive back up to standing. The limited range makes this manageable even if you cannot do full single-leg squats. Complete reps, then switch legs. Focus on control and balance. Progress by gradually increasing depth over time. Aim for 10 to 15 reps per leg.
Benefits: Accessible single-leg squat regression; Builds initial single-leg strength; Develops balance and control; No equipment needed; Progressive — increase depth over time; Useful for rehabilitation
Muscles Worked (Raw): Quadriceps (working leg); Gluteus maximus; Calves; Core (stabilizer)

Description: Stand on your right leg with arms extended forward for balance. Lift your left leg straight forward, parallel to the floor. Brace your core hard. Slowly squat down on your right leg by bending the knee and sitting your hips back. Keep your left leg extended straight forward, hovering above the floor. Descend until your right hamstring touches your right calf or your butt approaches your right heel. Drive through your right foot to stand back up. Complete reps on one side, then switch. If full depth is too hard, regress: assisted pistol (hold a strap), elevated pistol (foot on bench), or box pistol.
Benefits: Builds elite single-leg strength; Develops balance and stability; Trains ankle and hip mobility; Benchmark calisthenics skill; Exposes left-right strength imbalances; No equipment needed
Muscles Worked (Raw): Quadriceps; Gluteus maximus and medius; Hamstrings; Adductors; Calves and ankle stabilizers; Core (stabilizer); Hip flexors (extended leg)

Description: Stand on one leg with a slight knee bend. Lift the other leg slightly off the floor. Brace your core and keep the chest up. Reach the lifted leg forward and tap the floor. Return to the start position. Reach the leg out to the side and tap the floor. Reach the leg back and tap the floor. Finish all reps then switch sides.
Benefits: Builds balance; Trains the glutes; Strong stability move; Useful for athletes; Builds single leg control
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus maximus; Gluteus medius; Core

Description: Begin in a high plank position with hands wider than shoulders. Set the body in a straight line from head to heels. Brace your core hard. Lower the body to one side by bending only that arm. Keep the other arm straight out to the side. Lower until the chest reaches the bent arm hand. Press back up using the bent arm to lockout. Alternate sides each rep.
Benefits: Brutal unilateral chest builder; Strong push up progression; Builds the chest; Trains shoulder stability; Useful one arm push up prep; Strong calisthenic move
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Triceps brachii; Anterior deltoid; Core

Description: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Place your hands behind your head with elbows wide. Brace your core and engage your abs. Crunch your right elbow toward your left knee while lifting the knee toward the elbow. Twist through the obliques to bring the elbow and knee together. Squeeze your obliques at the top of the crunch. Lower back to the starting position with control. Repeat on the other side, alternating elbows and knees each rep.
Benefits: Targets obliques heavily; Builds rotational core strength; Strong functional movement pattern; Bodyweight ab work; Useful as a finisher; Easy to scale by changing leverage
Muscles Worked (Raw): Obliques (internal and external); Rectus abdominis; Hip flexors

Description: Lie on the floor with knees bent, feet flat. Hold a weight plate or dumbbell at your chest. Sit up by flexing your spine, bringing your chest toward your knees. At the top of the sit-up, press the weight overhead to lockout. Lower the weight back to your chest. Lower your torso back to the floor under control. That is one rep. Continue fluidly. Use moderate weight. Aim for 8 to 12 reps. Keep feet anchored if needed.
Benefits: Combines sit-up with overhead press; Builds abs and shoulders together; Time-efficient compound exercise; No bench needed; Easy to scale by weight selection; Engaging core-to-press combo
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Anterior deltoid; Triceps brachii; Hip flexors; Core

Description: Get into a standard push-up position. Hands shoulder-width apart. Perform a push-up — lower your chest to the floor and press back up. At the top, kick your right leg out to the right side, keeping it straight. Return your right leg to the starting position. Perform another push-up. Kick your left leg out to the left side at the top. Continue alternating sides. Aim for 8 to 12 reps total (4-6 per side).
Benefits: Combines pushing with hip abduction; Builds core anti-rotation under unilateral load; Develops hip flexor and glute medius strength; Engaging push-up variation; No equipment needed; Full-body conditioning
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Triceps brachii; Anterior deltoid; Gluteus medius (kick); Hip flexors (kick); Core (anti-rotation)

Exercise Name: Overhead Triceps Extension with Bed Sheet
Description: Loop a bed sheet around a fixed anchor point at low height. Stand facing away from the anchor. Grab the ends of the sheet behind the head with both hands. Step forward to create tension on the sheet. Brace the core and keep the chest up. Extend the elbows to press the hands overhead. Squeeze the triceps hard at lockout. Lower with control to the start.
Benefits: Trains the triceps at home.; No weights required.; Builds the back of the arms.; Useful for travel.; Joint friendly motion.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Triceps brachii; Anconeus; Anterior deltoid

Description: Adjust the pec deck seat so that when you sit with your back firmly against the pad, the handles or arm pads align with chest height. Sit down with your feet flat on the floor and back pressed against the pad. Grip the handles (or place forearms against the pads) with arms out to your sides, bent slightly at the elbows. Brace your core, pull your shoulders down and back into the pad, and lift your chest. Bring the handles or pads together in front of your body by squeezing your chest. Keep the slight elbow bend fixed throughout — this is a fly, not a press. Continue until the handles or pads meet in front of your chest. Squeeze your chest hard for one second. Slowly let the handles travel back out under control over two to three seconds. Feel a strong stretch in your chest at the end range. Stop just before the weight stack touches down to maintain tension throughout the set.
Benefits: Direct chest isolation with no stabilizer demand; Allows safe, comfortable training to muscular failure; Easy to load progressively in small increments; Provides a deep chest stretch at the end range; Excellent finisher after compound chest pressing; Easier to feel the target muscle than dumbbell flys
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major (sternal head); Anterior deltoid (secondary); Serratus anterior

Description: Start in a push-up position. Walk your feet toward your hands, raising your hips high into an inverted V. Your body should form a sharp angle at the hips. Head between your arms. Bend at the elbows to lower the top of your head toward the floor. Lower until your head nearly touches the floor. Press back up to the pike position by extending your arms. Keep your hips high throughout. The steeper the angle, the more shoulder-dominant the press. Aim for 8 to 12 reps per set.
Benefits: Bodyweight shoulder pressing exercise; Primary progression toward handstand push-ups; Builds overhead pressing strength; No equipment needed; Scalable by foot elevation (higher = harder); Develops shoulder and tricep strength
Muscles Worked (Raw): Anterior deltoid (primary); Lateral deltoid; Triceps brachii; Upper trapezius; Core (stabilizer)

Description: Start in a downward-facing dog pose — hips lifted high, body in an inverted V. Bend your arms and lower your head toward the floor in a pike push-up motion. As you lower, sweep your body forward and down — like a wave motion. Continue until your hips are near the floor and your chest is lifted in a cobra position. From cobra, push your hips up and back, returning to the downward dog pike position. That is one rep. Move smoothly with the breath. Keep your arms working throughout. Aim for 5 to 10 reps with control.
Benefits: Combines pike push-up strength with cobra mobility; Builds shoulder strength and chest flexibility; Develops body control and coordination; No equipment needed; Excellent dynamic warm-up; Trains shoulder mobility under load
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Anterior deltoid; Triceps brachii; Erector spinae; Core (transition control)

Description: Stand on your right leg in front of a box, bench, or chair behind you. Knee-height is a good starting point. Extend your left leg straight in front of you, lifted off the floor. Extend your arms forward for balance. Sit back and down on your right leg, lowering toward the box. Keep your left leg lifted. Lightly touch the box with your butt — do not fully sit and rest. Drive through your right foot to stand back up. Complete all reps on the right, then switch. Lower the box height progressively as you get stronger. Eventually progress to the full pistol squat.
Benefits: Effective progression toward the full pistol squat; Builds single-leg strength and balance; Adjustable difficulty by changing box height; Develops ankle and hip mobility; No equipment needed beyond a box; Trains core stability and coordination
Muscles Worked (Raw): Quadriceps; Gluteus maximus; Hamstrings; Adductors; Calves and ankle stabilizers; Core (stabilizer)

Description: Get into a high plank position with hands shoulder-width apart, body in a straight line. Brace your core hard. Engage your glutes. Slowly lift your right arm straight forward at shoulder height. Reach forward like Superman. Keep your hips perfectly still. Do not let them rotate or bounce. Hold for 1 to 2 seconds at the top. Lower your right arm and place it back on the floor. Lift your left arm in the same way. Continue alternating. Move slowly. Anti-rotation control is the goal.
Benefits: Builds elite anti-rotation core stability; Develops shoulder strength and stability; Trains balance under load; No equipment needed; Easy to scale by adjusting arm height; Useful for athletic core training
Muscles Worked (Raw): Core (heavy anti-rotation); Obliques; Anterior deltoid (lifting arm); Triceps brachii (planted arm); Serratus anterior; Gluteus maximus

Description: Get into a high-plank or forearm plank position with your body in a straight line from heels to head. Set your feet together at the start. Pull your shoulders down and back. Brace your core hard. Keep your hips perfectly level — do not let them sag, pike up, or rotate during the jacks. Jump both feet out wide simultaneously, landing in a wide stance. Maintain the plank position throughout — your upper body does not move. Immediately jump your feet back together to the starting position. Continue alternating wide and narrow foot positions in a controlled rhythm. Land softly on the balls of your feet to minimize impact. Continue for the desired duration (typically 20 to 60 seconds) or rep count.
Benefits: Trains core stability and cardiovascular conditioning together; Builds anti-rotation core strength through the leg movement; Improves hip mobility; Excellent HIIT or finisher exercise; No equipment needed — works anywhere; Time-efficient core-and-cardio combination
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Transverse abdominis; Obliques (anti-rotation); Hip abductors; Hip adductors; Gluteus maximus and medius; Anterior deltoid (isometric); Calves

Description: Begin in a forearm plank position. Set the elbows under the shoulders and the body in a straight line. Brace your core hard and keep the hips level. Hop both feet out wide to the sides at the same time. Land softly with feet wide. Hop both feet back together to the start. Continue the jumping jack feet pattern at speed. Keep the upper body steady throughout.
Benefits: Strong core and cardio combo; Trains the gluteus medius; Builds shoulder stability; No equipment needed; Useful core finisher; Builds cardio capacity
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Gluteus medius; Anterior deltoid

Description: Place towels under both feet on a smooth floor. Set up in a high plank with hands under the shoulders. Set the body in a straight line from head to heels. Brace your core and keep the back flat. Slide both feet out wide to the sides. Then slide both feet back to the center. Continue the slides at a steady tempo. Continue for the working set.
Benefits: Loads the core; Trains the glutes; Strong plank variation; Low impact move; Useful for core size
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Core; Gluteus medius

Description: Get into a high plank. Set feet wide for stability. Shift weight to your left arm. Raise your right arm out to the side at shoulder height. Hold for 1 to 2 seconds. Return to plank. Raise your left arm. Continue alternating. Minimize hip rotation. Aim for 6 to 10 raises per side.
Benefits: Combines plank with lateral raise; Builds shoulder and core together; Anti-rotation core demand; Scalable with or without dumbbells; No equipment needed for bodyweight version; Engaging and challenging
Muscles Worked (Raw): Lateral deltoid (raising arm); Core (anti-rotation); Anterior deltoid (support arm); Obliques

Description: Get into a push-up position with arms fully extended, hands under shoulders. Set your body in a straight line from heels to head. Brace your core. Squeeze your glutes. Hold this position for the desired time. Do not let your hips sag or pike up. Breathe steadily. Start with 20 to 30 seconds and build up to 60 seconds. This is the top position of a push-up.
Benefits: Adds shoulder and tricep demand to the plank; Builds anti-extension core strength; No equipment needed; Same position as top of push-up; Develops shoulder stability; Beginner-friendly
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Transverse abdominis; Anterior deltoid; Triceps brachii; Serratus anterior; Gluteus maximus

Description: Place a pair of hexagonal dumbbells on the floor. Hex dumbbells are essential — round ones will roll. Get into a high-plank position gripping the dumbbells with hands directly under your shoulders. Set feet wider than hip-width for stability. Brace your core hard and form a straight body line from heels to head. Perform a push-up by lowering your chest toward the dumbbells, then pressing back up to the high-plank.
