Cross your arms again, this time with left arm on top. Continue alternating which arm crosses on top. Move at a brisk, rhythmic pace. Use full range of motion. Perform for 30 to 60 seconds as a warm-up.
Benefits: Dynamic shoulder warm-up; Opens the chest through arm swing; Warms up the upper body; No equipment needed; Quick and accessible; Improves shoulder mobility
Muscles Worked (Raw): Anterior, lateral, and posterior deltoid; Pectoralis major; Trapezius; Rhomboids

Description: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart. Extend both arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height. Brace your core and pull your shoulders back. Begin making small forward circles with both arms. Gradually increase the circle size to large sweeping circles. After several large forward circles, reverse direction. Make small backward circles, gradually increasing to large circles. Maintain straight arms and shoulder height throughout.
Benefits: Warms up the shoulders; Improves shoulder mobility; Activates rotator cuff; No equipment required; Useful for warmups before upper body training; Easy and effective shoulder prep
Muscles Worked (Raw): Anterior deltoid; Lateral deltoid; Posterior deltoid; Rotator cuff

Description: Sit or stand tall with shoulders relaxed. Look straight ahead with the head in a neutral position. Place two fingers on the front of your chin. Gently push the chin straight back, not down. Feel a stretch at the back of the neck. Create a double chin position briefly. Hold for a few seconds and release. Repeat the chin tuck several times in a row.
Benefits: Improves forward head posture; Strengthens deep neck flexors; No equipment needed; Easy to do at any time; Useful for desk workers; Strong posture drill
Muscles Worked (Raw): Deep neck flexors; Sternocleidomastoid; Upper trapezius

Description: Lie flat on your back with both legs extended. Hold a yoga strap, towel, or resistance band. Bend your right knee and loop the strap around the ball of your right foot. Hold both ends of the strap with your hands. Extend your right leg straight up toward the ceiling, keeping your knee straight. Use the strap to gently pull your leg closer to your chest. Adjust the depth based on your hamstring flexibility. Stop where you feel a strong but tolerable stretch. Keep your left leg flat on the floor (or bent for less intensity). Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch legs and repeat.
Benefits: Safe and controlled hamstring stretch; Strap allows precise depth control; Excellent for tight hamstrings; Comfortable supine position; Easy on the lower back; Foundational stretch for any flexibility program
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings (biceps femoris, semitendinosus, semimembranosus); Calves (secondary); Lower back (gentle)

Description: Stand tall with feet shoulder width apart and arms reaching out wide. Inhale and reach the arms up and overhead in a wide arc. Begin to hinge forward at the hips while the arms travel wide. Bring the arms down and across as the hands reach toward the toes. Touch the toes or shins at the bottom of the bend. Reverse the path by sweeping the arms back wide and overhead. Stand back up tall with arms reaching wide again. Repeat the circular flow for the full set.
Benefits: Stretches the hamstrings and lower back.; Opens the chest and shoulders through wide arm reach.; Improves spinal mobility through flexion and extension.; Acts as a dynamic warm up before lifting.; No equipment needed.; Loosens up the entire posterior chain.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings; Erector spinae; Pectoralis major; Anterior deltoid

Description: Stand next to a wall or sturdy support for balance. Place a hand on the support. Lift one leg slightly off the floor. Brace your core and keep the chest up. Swing the lifted leg forward to about hip height. Swing the leg back behind you with control. Use momentum but stay in control. Finish all reps then switch sides.
Benefits: Mobilizes the hips; Strong warm-up move; Trains the hamstrings; Useful before training; Activates the glutes
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings; Hip Flexors; Gluteus maximus

Description: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Bring your arms behind your back at hip level. Clasp your hands together with fingers interlaced. Press your palms together if possible. Brace your core and pull your shoulders back. Squeeze your shoulder blades together. Slowly lift your clasped hands away from your body. Hold the stretch with deep breathing.
Benefits: Opens the chest and front delts; Improves shoulder mobility; Useful for desk worker tightness; No equipment required; Recovery stretch for upper body lifters; Easy to do anywhere
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Anterior deltoid; Biceps brachii

Description: Lie on your back on the floor or a mat. Bend your knees and place your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Position your feet so your knees fall comfortably toward each other or stack directly above your feet — whichever is more comfortable. Place your hands on your belly or rest them at your sides with palms up. Close your eyes. Relax your jaw, shoulders, and hips. Allow the floor to support your weight completely. Let go of any muscle tension. Breathe naturally and deeply. Stay in the position for 5 to 20 minutes. To exit, slowly roll to one side and rise gently.
Benefits: Releases back tension naturally; Decompresses the spine; Restorative — useful as a cool-down or recovery practice; Reduces stress; No equipment needed; Easy to integrate into any routine
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae (relaxed); Quadratus lumborum; Hip flexors (relaxed); Diaphragm (deep breathing)

Description: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Place your hands on your lower back for support. Slowly bend forward at the waist, letting your arms hang down. Allow your head and arms to relax. Feel the stretch through your back. Hold for 15 to 20 seconds. Breathe deeply. Slowly roll up to standing, vertebra by vertebra. Hands return to lower back. From standing, lean to one side, sliding your hand down your leg. Hold for 10 to 15 seconds. Return to center and lean to the other side. Repeat the entire sequence two to three times.
Benefits: Relieves general back tension; Improves spinal mobility in multiple planes; Gentle enough for daily use; No equipment needed; Excellent warm-up or cool-down; Suitable for all fitness levels
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae; Latissimus dorsi; Quadratus lumborum; Obliques (side bending); Hamstrings (forward fold)

Description: Lie face down on the floor with both legs straight. Rest your arms folded under your forehead. Brace your core lightly to protect the lower back. Have a partner lift one leg by holding the ankle. Have the partner gently raise the leg up toward your back. Feel a deep stretch in the hamstring of the lifted leg. Hold the stretch and breathe slowly. Lower the leg back down. Repeat on the other side.
Benefits: Deep hamstring stretch; Protects the lower back; Useful for athletes; Easy partner drill; Builds hamstring flexibility; No equipment required
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings; Calves; Gluteus maximus

Description: Stand with the feet hip width apart. Wrap the arms around the body in a self hug. Cross the arms so each hand reaches the opposite shoulder blade. Brace your core and keep the chest up. Bend forward at the hips slightly. Gently slap the back with the hands. Feel the stretch across the upper back. Release and repeat as needed.
Benefits: Stretches the upper back; Releases the rhomboids; Strong recovery move; Useful warm-up; Builds upper back mobility
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rhomboids; Posterior deltoid; Trapezius

Description: Sit on the floor with both legs extended. Bend your right knee and place your right foot flat on the floor outside your left thigh. Bend your left knee and tuck your left foot near your right glute (or keep your left leg extended for an easier version). Sit up tall. Place your right hand on the floor behind your right hip. Reach your left arm up. Then twist to the right and bring your left elbow to the outside of your right knee. Press your left elbow into your right knee to deepen the twist. Look over your right shoulder. Keep both sit bones grounded. Hold for 5 to 10 breaths. Switch sides.
Benefits: Deeply mobilizes the spine through rotation; Stretches the obliques, lower back, and glutes; Aids digestion through abdominal compression; Opens the hip of the bent leg; Calming and detoxifying; Foundational deep twist in yoga
Muscles Worked (Raw): Obliques (deep stretch); Erector spinae; Gluteus maximus (bent leg); Piriformis; Thoracic spine rotators; Latissimus dorsi

Description: Stand tall holding a light resistance band with a wide grip. Set the arms straight in front at chest height. Pull the band apart to take tension. Keep the arms straight as you lift the band overhead. Continue the arc back behind the head. Lower the band behind the back to hip level. Reverse the path to bring the band back to the front. Continue the slow circling motion for the duration.
Benefits: Opens the chest and shoulders; Useful warm-up move; Trains shoulder mobility; Strong band move; Builds shoulder stability; Easy to do anywhere
Muscles Worked (Raw): Anterior deltoid; Pectoralis major; Posterior deltoid

Description: Stand with feet hip-width apart. Extend both arms straight out to the sides. Draw small forward circles with both arms simultaneously. Gradually increase the circle size over 10 to 15 reps. Continue for 15 to 20 seconds forward. Reverse direction — draw backward circles. Again start small and increase. Continue for 15 to 20 seconds backward. Keep arms straight throughout.
Benefits: Warms up the shoulder joints; Increases blood flow to the rotator cuff; Prepares shoulders for upper-body training; No equipment needed; Quick and accessible; Standard warm-up exercise
Muscles Worked (Raw): Deltoids (all three heads); Rotator cuff; Trapezius; Serratus anterior

Description: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Place your hands on your lower back for support. Brace your core slightly to protect the lower back. Pull your shoulders back and lift your chest. Slowly arch backward through the upper spine. Lead the bend with the chest, not the lower back. Continue until you feel a stretch in the abs and front of the body. Hold the stretch briefly, then return to upright.
Benefits: Opens the abs and hip flexors; Improves spinal extension; Counteracts forward-flexed posture; No equipment required; Useful for desk workers; Easy to do anywhere
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Hip flexors; Pectoralis major

Description: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Brace your core lightly. Keep a slight bend in the knees if needed. Hinge at the hips to fold the torso forward over the legs. Reach your hands down toward your toes. Allow the head to hang relaxed. Feel the stretch through the hamstrings and back. Hold for several breaths then come back up slowly.
Benefits: Stretches the hamstrings; Releases lower back tension; No equipment needed; Easy to add to any routine; Useful warm-up move; Strong fundamental stretch
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings; Spinal erectors; Calves

Description: Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width apart. Hinge forward at the hips into a flat-back forward fold. Let your hands hang toward the floor. Reach your right hand toward your left foot, twisting your torso to the left. Extend your left arm up toward the ceiling, opening your chest. Look up at your left hand. Feel the stretch through your right side body, hamstrings, and obliques. Return to center, then twist to the right — left hand toward right foot, right arm toward ceiling. Continue alternating sides for 10 to 15 reps total. Move with control and breath.
Benefits: Combines hamstring stretch with thoracic rotation; Excellent dynamic warm-up; Improves spinal flexibility; No equipment needed; Quick and accessible; Builds coordination and rhythm
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings; Erector spinae; Obliques (rotation); Thoracic spine rotators; Latissimus dorsi

Description: Sit cross legged on the floor with the spine tall. Set the back of one hand on the opposite knee. Place the other hand behind the body on the floor. Brace your core and lengthen the spine up. Inhale to grow taller through the spine. Exhale and rotate the torso to one side using the hands to deepen. Hold the deep twist with steady breath. Slowly unwind back to center. Switch sides and repeat.
Benefits: Strong spinal twist; Stretches the obliques; Releases the lower back; No equipment needed; Useful cool down move; Builds spinal mobility
Muscles Worked (Raw): Obliques; Spinal erectors; Latissimus dorsi

Exercise Name: Bird of Paradise Pose Svarga Dvijasana
Description: Stand with the feet wide and turn the right foot out. Bend the right knee into a side angle pose. Reach the right arm under the right thigh and the left arm behind the back. Clasp the hands together for the bind. Shift weight onto the left foot. Slowly stand up keeping the bind. Extend the right leg out and up to the side. Hold the pose for the desired duration then switch sides.
Benefits: Builds single leg balance.; Stretches the hamstrings and hips.; Opens the chest and shoulders through the bind.; Calms the mind in classical yoga practice.; No equipment needed.; Improves total body coordination.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings; Adductors; Gluteus medius; Pectoralis major; Quadriceps

Description: Sit on the floor with knees bent and feet flat. Lean back slightly so you balance on your sit bones. Lift both feet off the floor. Extend your legs straight at roughly 45 degrees. Extend both arms forward at shoulder height, parallel to your legs. Body forms a V-shape with torso and legs. Brace your core hard. Keep your back as flat as possible — no rounding. Lift your chest. Engage your hip flexors and quads. Hold for 15 to 30 seconds, building up to 60 seconds. Lower with control. Repeat 2 to 4 sets.
Benefits: Builds anterior core strength; Strengthens hip flexors and quads; Develops balance and body control; Foundational yoga and Pilates pose; No equipment needed; Improves digestion through abdominal compression
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Hip flexors (iliopsoas, rectus femoris); Quadriceps; Hamstrings (stretched); Erector spinae (postural)

Description: Sit on the floor with knees bent and feet flat. Lean back slightly to balance on your sit bones. Lift your feet off the floor and bring your shins parallel to the floor. Extend your arms forward at shoulder height with palms facing each other. Brace your core hard to maintain balance. Form a V shape with your body, balancing on your sit bones. Hold the position with steady breathing. For an advanced version, fully extend your legs straight.
Benefits: Builds core endurance; Strong hip flexor engagement; Develops balance and stability; Foundational yoga core pose; No equipment required; Useful for yoga and pilates flow
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Hip flexors; Hamstrings; Quadriceps

Description: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Reach both arms straight up overhead, palms facing forward or each other. Engage your core gently. Squeeze your glutes for low-back support. Lift your chest tall and slowly arch your upper back, reaching your hands back behind you. Look up gently if comfortable. Keep your neck long. Lengthen through the entire spine. Hold for 5 to 15 seconds at the deepest point. Slowly return to upright. Repeat 3 to 5 times.
Benefits: Opens the entire front of the body; Decompresses the spine; Counteracts hunched posture from sitting; Stretches the abs, hip flexors, and chest; No equipment needed; Quick and accessible
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae (engaged); Rectus abdominis (stretched); Pectoralis major (stretched); Hip flexors (stretched); Anterior deltoid; Latissimus dorsi (engaged)

Exercise Name: Bodyweight Front Plank to Downward Dog
Description: Start in a high plank with hands under shoulders and body straight. Brace the core and keep the head in line with the spine. Push the hips up and back into a downward dog position. Press the chest toward the thighs and aim heels toward the floor. Spread the fingers wide and press through the full hand. Hold the downward dog position for a breath. Shift forward back into the plank with hips lowered to neutral. Continue flowing between the two positions for the full set.
Benefits: Stretches the hamstrings and calves through the dog position.; Opens the shoulders and lats with the inverted V shape.; Strengthens the core and shoulders in the plank.; Improves shoulder mobility and overhead control.; Decompresses the spine through the hip hinge.; No equipment needed and travel friendly.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings; Calves; Latissimus dorsi; Anterior deltoid

Description: Stand in an open doorway. Place your right forearm against the doorframe with your elbow at shoulder height (90-degree bend). Step your right foot forward through the doorway. Gently lean your body forward. Your right arm stays against the frame. Feel the stretch across your right chest and front shoulder. Adjust the elbow position higher (lower chest stretch) or lower (upper chest stretch). Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch sides and repeat. Apply only gentle forward pressure — never force the stretch.
Benefits: Targets one side of the chest at a time; Reveals left-right tightness asymmetries; Adjustable depth via elbow height and lean angle; Counteracts forward-hunched posture; No equipment needed beyond a doorway; Excellent for upper body cooldown
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major (one side); Pectoralis minor; Anterior deltoid; Biceps brachii

Description: Stand or sit tall. Clasp your hands behind your head with elbows pointing forward. Gently pull your elbows out and back, opening your chest. Pull your shoulder blades down and together. Lift your chest. Avoid arching your lower back. Feel the stretch across your chest, front shoulders, and triceps. Hold for 15 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. For more intensity, gently arch your upper back while pulling elbows back. Repeat two to three times.
Benefits: Opens the chest, shoulders, and triceps; Counteracts forward-hunched posture; Quick and accessible stretch; No equipment needed; Useful between sets or anytime during the day; Improves overhead pressing position
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major (stretched); Anterior deltoid (stretched); Triceps brachii (stretched); Rhomboids (engaged); Lower trapezius (engaged)

Description: Stand or sit tall. Reach your right arm straight up overhead. Bend your right elbow to drop your right hand down behind your head, between your shoulder blades. Reach your left hand up and grasp your right elbow. Gently pull your right elbow toward the left, deepening the stretch. Feel the stretch through the back of your right upper arm (tricep), right lat, and right shoulder. Keep your chest lifted and core braced. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch sides and repeat.
Benefits: Deeply stretches the triceps and shoulders; Opens the lats; Improves overhead mobility; Quick and accessible; No equipment needed; Excellent post-workout stretch for arm and pressing days
Muscles Worked (Raw): Triceps brachii (especially long head); Latissimus dorsi; Posterior deltoid; Teres major

Exercise Name: Bodyweight Standing Around the World Wall Supported
Description: Stand sideways to a wall with one shoulder close to it. Place the inside hand on the wall at hip height. Brace the core and keep the shoulder relaxed. Slide the hand up the wall toward the ceiling. Continue tracing the arm overhead and back behind you. Bring the hand all the way down behind your hip. Reverse the motion to come back to the start. Repeat for all reps then switch sides.
Benefits: Mobilizes the shoulder through a full circle.; Wall feedback keeps the shoulder blade tracking honestly.; No equipment needed beyond a wall.; Excellent warm up for overhead lifts.; Improves shoulder mobility.; Reduces shoulder stiffness.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Anterior deltoid; Lateral deltoid; Posterior deltoid; Trapezius; Pectoralis major

Description: Stand next to a sturdy support. Place the non working hand on the support. Hinge forward at the hips. Let the working arm hang straight down. Brace your core and keep the back flat. Swing the working arm gently forward and back. Then swing it side to side. Finish with small circles in both directions.
Benefits: Mobilizes the shoulder; Strong rehab drill; Useful warm-up; Builds shoulder range; Trains shoulder mobility
Muscles Worked (Raw): Anterior deltoid; Posterior deltoid; Lateral deltoid

Description: Stand tall with feet hip width apart. Reach the arms straight up overhead. Interlace the fingers and turn the palms up. Brace your core lightly. Press the hands up reaching tall through the spine. Slowly arch the upper back gently backward. Hold the stretch with steady breath. Slowly return to neutral and lower the arms.
Benefits: Releases lower back tension; Stretches the lats; Easy to do anywhere; No equipment needed; Useful posture stretch; Builds spinal mobility
Muscles Worked (Raw): Spinal erectors; Latissimus dorsi; Rectus abdominis

Description: Stand tall holding a weighted bottle in both hands at chest level. Set your feet at hip-width and brace your core. Grip the bottle by the handle and the bottom. Begin circling the bottle around your head in a halo motion. Keep the bottle close to your head as it travels around. Move slowly and control the bottle through the full path. Complete several halos in one direction. Reverse the direction and circle the other way.
Benefits: Mobilizes the shoulders; Builds shoulder strength; No KB or DB required; Useful warm-up move; Easy to scale at home; Travel-friendly setup
Muscles Worked (Raw): Anterior deltoid; Lateral deltoid; Core; Upper back

Description: Lie face down on the floor with arms at your sides. Bend both knees, bringing your heels toward your glutes. Reach back with both hands and grip the outsides of your ankles or feet. Inhale and lift your chest off the floor by pressing your feet back into your hands. Simultaneously lift your thighs off the floor, deepening the back bend. Engage your glutes and core. Look forward, not up (to protect the neck). Hold for 5 to 10 breaths. Breathe into the front body. Release slowly back to the floor.
Benefits: Deeply stretches the chest, abs, hip flexors, and quads; Strengthens the entire back chain; Opens the front of the shoulders; Counteracts forward-hunched posture; Energizing and invigorating; No equipment needed
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major (stretched); Rectus abdominis (stretched); Hip flexors (stretched); Quadriceps (stretched); Erector spinae (strengthened); Gluteus maximus (engaged)

Description: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Bring your arms straight out in front of you at chest height. Hold both palms facing each other. Brace your core and pull your shoulders back. Open both arms out wide to the sides. Continue until you feel a stretch across your chest. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the open position. Bring the arms back together in front of you. Continue.
Benefits: Stretches the chest; Warms up the shoulders; No equipment required; Useful for warmups; Improves chest mobility; Easy to do anywhere
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Anterior deltoid; Posterior deltoid

Description: Lie on the back with the knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Place the heels close to the glutes. Set the arms at the sides palms down. Brace your core and inhale to prepare. Press through the heels to lift the hips up. Roll the shoulders under and clasp the hands beneath. Lift the chest up toward the chin. Hold the pose then release with control.
Benefits: Opens the chest; Stretches the hip flexors; Strong yoga pose; Useful for back health; Builds the glutes
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus maximus; Erector spinae; Hip Flexors

Description: Stand facing a wall about an arm’s length away. Place both hands on the wall at shoulder height. Step your right foot back about two to three feet. Keep your right leg straight with the heel pressed into the floor. Bend your left (front) knee. Lean forward into the wall while keeping your back leg straight. Feel the stretch through your right calf (gastrocnemius). Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. For the soleus, bend your right (back) knee while keeping the heel down. Feel the stretch lower in the calf. Hold for another 20 to 30 seconds. Switch sides and repeat both versions.
Benefits: Stretches both the gastrocnemius (straight leg) and soleus (bent leg); Improves ankle dorsiflexion for better squat depth; Relieves calf tightness from running or high heels; Quick and accessible; No equipment needed beyond a wall; Useful warm-up or cool-down
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gastrocnemius (straight knee variation); Soleus (bent knee variation); Achilles tendon

Description: Sit on the floor with your back tall. Bring the soles of your feet together and let your knees fall out to the sides. Hold your feet or ankles with your hands. Sit up tall through the spine. Gently flap your knees up and down toward the floor. Move at a comfortable rhythm without forcing range of motion. Keep your spine long and your shoulders relaxed. Continue for a comfortable duration.
Benefits: Opens the hips and inner thighs; Improves hip mobility; Loosens tight adductors; Useful as a warm-up or cool-down; Calming and gentle on the body
Muscles Worked (Raw): Adductors; Hips; Hip Flexors

Description: Sit on the floor with legs extended in front. Loop a rope or strap around the ball of one foot. Hold the ends of the rope with both hands. Brace your core and keep the spine tall. Pull the rope ends back toward the body. Let the toes pull back to deepen the calf stretch. Hold the stretch with steady breath. Release. Switch legs and repeat.
Benefits: Strong calf stretch; Useful for runners; Builds ankle mobility; Strong cool down stretch; Easy to do anywhere; Trains the hamstrings
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gastrocnemius; Soleus; Calves

Description: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Set the feet hip width and arms at the sides. Brace your core and squeeze the glutes. Drive through the heels to lift the hips up. Walk the shoulders under and interlace the hands beneath the body. Press the arms down to lift the hips higher. Open the chest and roll the shoulders under. Hold the pose with steady breath. Release with control.
Benefits: Opens the hip flexors; Stretches the chest; Builds glute strength; Strong yoga pose; Trains spinal extension; Useful warm-up
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus maximus; Pectoralis major; Hip flexors; Hamstrings

Description: Sit on the floor with legs extended. Bend both knees and bring the soles of your feet together. Let your knees drop out to the sides. Pull your heels toward your groin as close as comfortable. Hold your feet with both hands. Sit up tall with chest lifted. Press your knees gently toward the floor with your elbows for a deeper stretch. For more depth, fold forward from the hips with a flat back. Reach your forehead toward your feet. Hold for 30 to 90 seconds. Breathe deeply. Avoid forcing your knees down — let gravity do the work over time. Use a folded blanket or block under each knee for support if needed.
Benefits: Opens the inner thighs, groin, and hips; Improves hip flexibility for squats and wide-stance lifts; Calming and restorative pose; No equipment needed; Useful for athletes and lifters with tight adductors; Foundational hip-opening yoga pose
Muscles Worked (Raw): Adductors (inner thighs); Gracilis; Pectineus; Hip rotators; Lower back (forward fold)

Description: Kneel on the floor with knees hip-width apart, tops of feet on the floor. Place your hands on your lower back with fingers pointing down for support. Lift your chest tall. Squeeze your glutes. Slowly arch backward, leading with your chest. Keep your hips pushed forward over your knees. If comfortable, reach back to grasp your heels with both hands. Open your chest fully. Let your head drop back gently if your neck allows. Hold for 5 to 8 breaths. To exit, bring your hands back to your lower back, lift your chest, and rise to upright.
Benefits: Deeply opens the chest, hips, and quads; Counteracts forward-hunched posture; Strengthens the back; Energizing and uplifting; Improves spinal extension mobility; No equipment needed
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae (engaged); Rectus abdominis (deeply stretched); Pectoralis major (stretched); Hip flexors (deeply stretched); Quadriceps (stretched); Anterior deltoid (stretched)

Exercise Name: Calf Stretch with Hands Against Wall
Description: Stand facing a wall about an arm length away. Place both hands on the wall at shoulder height. Step one foot back keeping the leg straight. Plant the back heel firmly on the floor. Bend the front knee and lean toward the wall. Feel the stretch in the back calf and Achilles. Keep the back heel pressed down throughout. Hold the stretch for the desired duration then switch sides.
Benefits: Lengthens the calves and Achilles tendon.; Improves ankle mobility.; No equipment needed beyond a wall.; Easy to perform anywhere.; Carryover to squat depth and running mechanics.; Reduces calf tightness.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Calves; Gastrocnemius; Soleus; Tibialis posterior

Description: Kneel on the floor with knees hip-width apart, shins flat on the mat. Place your hands on your lower back, fingers pointing down. Squeeze your glutes. Inhale, lift your chest, and begin to arch backward. Keep your hips pushing forward over your knees. Reach back with one hand at a time to grip your heels. If your hands cannot reach, keep them on your lower back or place blocks beside your feet. Lift your chest toward the ceiling. Open your throat by gently dropping your head back. Press your shins firmly into the floor. Keep glutes engaged to protect your lower back. Hold for 5 to 8 breaths. Breathe into your chest and belly. To exit, bring hands back to lower back, lift chest, then come up to vertical. Rest in child’s pose.
Benefits: Deeply opens the chest and front shoulders; Stretches the hip flexors and abdominals; Strengthens the back and glutes; Counteracts forward-hunched posture; Powerful heart-opener and energizing; Improves spinal extension
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major (stretched); Rectus abdominis (stretched); Hip flexors (stretched); Erector spinae (strengthened); Gluteus maximus (engaged); Quadriceps (engaged)

Description: Start in a tabletop position on your hands and knees. Hands directly under shoulders, knees under hips. Spread your fingers wide. Press through your palms. Exhale and round your spine toward the ceiling. Drop your head and tuck your tailbone. Pull your navel up toward your spine. Feel the stretch through your back. Continue rounding through the entire spine — neck, mid-back, and lower back. Hold briefly, then transition into Cow Pose by inhaling and arching the spine in the opposite direction. Flow between Cat and Cow for 5 to 10 cycles, syncing breath with movement. Move slowly and mindfully.
Benefits: Improves spinal flexion mobility; Stretches the back, neck, and shoulders; Activates the core (transverse abdominis); Excellent gentle warm-up for the spine; Calming and restorative; Foundational yoga pose accessible to all levels
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae (stretched); Trapezius (stretched); Rectus abdominis (engaged); Transverse abdominis (engaged)

Description: Stand or sit with your back tall and shoulders relaxed. Keep your chest up and shoulders pulled back. Slowly tilt your head back to look up at the ceiling. Continue tilting until you feel a gentle stretch on the front of your neck. Avoid forcing the stretch or jamming the neck back. Hold the position and breathe normally. Slowly return your head to the neutral position. Repeat for several gentle reps.
Benefits: Stretches the front of the neck; Counteracts forward-head posture; Useful for desk workers; Relieves neck tightness; Improves neck mobility
Muscles Worked (Raw): Neck; Sternocleidomastoid; Throat

Description: Sit on the edge of a sturdy chair with both feet flat on the floor. Extend your right leg straight forward with the heel on the floor and toes pointing up. Sit up tall with chest lifted. Place your hands on your right thigh. Hinge forward at the hips over your right leg, keeping your back flat. Slide your hands down your thigh toward your right foot. Feel the stretch through your right hamstring. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Switch legs and repeat.
Benefits: Stretches the hamstring of the extended leg; Convenient for office settings; Accessible for anyone who can sit in a chair; No equipment needed besides a chair; Quick and easy; Useful for desk workers
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings (extended leg); Calves (extended leg); Erector spinae (slight)

Description: Stand tall with feet hip width apart and arms at your sides. Inhale and reach both arms straight up overhead. Bring the biceps close to the ears with palms facing each other. Exhale and bend the knees to sink into a squat position. Sit the hips back as if lowering into a chair. Keep the chest tall and the arms reaching up. Hold the chair pose breathing steadily. Press through the heels and reach the arms higher to deepen the pose.
Benefits: Stretches the chest, shoulders, and lats overhead.; Strengthens the quads, glutes, and calves.; Improves balance and ankle mobility.; Decompresses the spine through the long reach.; Builds focus and breath control.; No equipment needed.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Quadriceps; Gluteus maximus; Anterior deltoid; Erector spinae

Description: Start in tabletop position on hands and knees. Hands directly under shoulders, knees under hips. Inhale into Cow Pose: drop your belly toward the floor, lift your chest and chin upward, and let your tailbone rise. Feel the gentle backbend through your spine. Exhale into Cat Pose: round your spine upward like a Halloween cat, tuck your chin to your chest, and tuck your tailbone under. Press through your hands to fully round the upper back. Continue alternating slowly with your breath: inhale to cow, exhale to cat. Move through the entire spine — neck, mid-back, lower back, and tailbone all participate. Perform 8 to 12 cycles as a warm-up or anytime your back feels stiff.
Benefits: Mobilizes the entire spine through flexion and extension; Warms up the core and back; Relieves tension from prolonged sitting; One of the simplest and most universally beneficial mobility drills; No equipment needed; Calming and rhythmic
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae (cow phase); Rectus abdominis (cat phase); Trapezius and rhomboids; Deep spinal stabilizers; Hip flexors (gentle stretch)

Description: Kneel on the floor with knees hip-width apart. Set your toes flat and the tops of your feet down. Place your hands on your lower back for support. Press your hips forward as you arch the upper back. Reach one hand back to grab the same-side heel. Reach the other hand back to grab the other heel. Press the chest up and let the head fall back. Hold the pose and breathe deeply then come back up slowly.
Benefits: Deep front body stretch; Opens the chest; Stretches the quads; Useful posture pose; Strong yoga backbend; Releases hip flexors
Muscles Worked (Raw): Quadriceps; Hip flexors; Pectoralis major; Anterior deltoid

Description: Stand tall with feet hip width apart. Bring the palms together in front of the chest in a prayer position. Exhale and bend the knees to sink into a squat. Sit the hips back as if lowering into a chair. Keep the chest tall and the prayer hands at the sternum. Press the palms together to open the chest. Hold the position with steady breathing. Press through the heels and stand back tall to release.
Benefits: Strengthens the quads, glutes, and calves.; Stretches the chest and opens the shoulders through prayer.; Improves balance and ankle mobility.; Centers the focus through the prayer hands.; Builds isometric leg strength.; No equipment needed.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Quadriceps; Gluteus maximus; Pectoralis major; Calves

Description: Begin in a high plank position. Hands directly under your shoulders, body in a straight line from heels to head. Shift your weight slightly forward — your shoulders should move slightly past your wrists. Brace your core hard. Engage your glutes and quads. Slowly lower your body by bending your elbows. Keep your elbows tucked tight against your ribs — they should NOT flare out. Stop when your upper arms are parallel to the floor and elbows are at 90 degrees. Maintain a perfectly straight body line. No sagging hips, no piked butt, no dropped chest. Hold for 1 to 3 breaths, then continue to upward-facing dog or push back up. If you cannot maintain form, lower to your knees first.
Benefits: Foundational yoga strength pose; Builds tremendous upper-body and core strength; Develops body control and stability; Repeated many times per yoga class — major strength stimulus; No equipment needed; Improves push-up form and strength
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Triceps brachii (heavy); Anterior deltoid; Serratus anterior; Core (entire trunk); Erector spinae (isometric)

Exercise Name: Chest and Front of Shoulder Stretch
Description: Stand in an open doorway. Place your right forearm against the doorframe with your elbow at shoulder height (90-degree bend in elbow). Step your right foot forward through the doorway. Gently lean your body forward, allowing your right arm to stay against the frame. Feel the stretch across your right chest and front shoulder. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. To deepen, increase the forward lean or rotate your torso slightly to the left. Switch sides and repeat. For both arms simultaneously, stand in the doorway with both forearms against opposite frames.
Benefits: Opens the chest and front shoulders effectively; Counteracts forward-hunched posture; Easy to do at home or in any doorway; Adjustable depth via lean angle; Improves shoulder flexibility for pressing exercises; No equipment needed beyond a doorway
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major (stretched); Pectoralis minor (stretched); Anterior deltoid (stretched); Biceps brachii (stretched)

Description: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Place your hands behind your head with elbows wide. Lengthen the back of your neck. Inhale to prepare. Exhale and curl your head, neck, and shoulders off the floor. Rotate your torso to the right, bringing your left elbow toward your right knee. Pause briefly at the top with controlled engagement. Inhale and rotate back to center. Exhale and rotate to the left. Continue alternating for the desired number of reps. Move with control.
Benefits: Engages both rectus abdominis and obliques; Teaches controlled, mindful core engagement; Foundational Pilates ab exercise; No equipment needed; Improves core endurance and quality of contraction; Builds rotational stability
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Internal and external obliques; Transverse abdominis; Hip flexors (secondary)

Description: Sit on the floor in front of a stability ball. Roll back so the upper back rests on the ball. Walk the feet out to extend the body. Allow the arms to fall back overhead. Brace the core lightly and keep the hips supported. Let the chest open into the stretch. Breathe slowly and deeply to relax. Hold for the desired duration.
Benefits: Stretches the chest deeply.; Opens the front shoulders.; Mobilizes the thoracic spine.; Useful after pressing work.; Improves posture.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Anterior deltoid; Pectoralis minor

Description: Kneel on the floor with your big toes touching and your knees roughly hip-width apart (or wider for a deeper hip stretch). Sit your hips back onto your heels. If your hips do not reach your heels, place a folded blanket or pillow between them for support. Walk your hands forward and lower your torso between or over your thighs. Rest your forehead on the floor or a block if it does not reach. Extend your arms straight out in front of you with your palms down (active version), or rest them alongside your body with palms up (passive, restorative version). Relax your shoulders away from your ears and let your chest sink toward the floor. Breathe slowly into your back ribs. Hold for 30 seconds to several minutes, breathing deeply throughout. To come out, walk your hands back toward your body and slowly sit up on your heels.
Benefits: Gently stretches the lower back, hips, thighs, and ankles; Calms the nervous system and helps reduce stress and anxiety; Decompresses the spine after standing, sitting, or backbends; Excellent recovery pose between more demanding yoga postures; Encourages slow, deep breathing into the back body
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae (lower back); Latissimus dorsi; Gluteus maximus; Hip rotators; Quadriceps and tops of the feet

Description: Begin on hands and knees with hands under shoulders. Sit the hips back on the heels into childs pose. Lower the forehead to the floor and reach the arms forward. Rest in childs pose briefly. Slide the body forward through plank. As the hips reach the floor lift the chest up into cobra. Press the chest up high and arch the upper back gently. Hold cobra briefly. Reverse the flow back to childs pose.
Benefits: Strong back stretch; Opens the chest; Strong yoga flow; Builds spinal mobility; Useful warm-up; Strong cool down move
Muscles Worked (Raw): Spinal erectors; Pectoralis major; Hip flexors

Description: Sit or stand tall. Pull your shoulders back and down. Slowly lower your chin toward your chest. Let the natural weight of your head provide the stretch — do not force it. Optionally place both hands gently on the back of your head and apply very light downward pressure. Feel the stretch through the back of your neck and upper traps. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Slowly release. Repeat 2 to 3 times. Move slowly — never force the cervical spine.
Benefits: Relieves back-of-neck tension; Stretches the upper traps; Quick and accessible; No equipment needed; Counteracts forward head posture; Useful for desk workers throughout the day
Muscles Worked (Raw): Suboccipitals; Splenius capitis; Upper trapezius; Erector spinae (cervical)

Description: Start in a tabletop position on hands and knees. Hands directly under shoulders, knees under hips. Brace your core gently. Keep your arms straight. Exhale and round your spine upward toward the ceiling — like a Halloween cat arching its back. Tuck your chin toward your chest. Tuck your tailbone under. Press through your hands to push the floor away, deepening the upper-back round. Hold for 2 to 3 breaths at the top of the round. Slowly return to a flat back. Repeat 8 to 12 times. Move slowly and feel each vertebra round individually.
Benefits: Mobilizes the spine through flexion; Stretches the erector spinae and lower back; Counteracts excessive arching from poor sitting posture; Quick and accessible; No equipment needed; Calming and centering
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae (stretched); Rectus abdominis (engaged); Trapezius and rhomboids; Transverse abdominis

Description: Sit or stand tall with good posture. Look straight ahead. Without tilting your head up or down, pull your chin straight back — like making a double chin. Imagine someone is pushing your chin straight back into your spine. Hold for 5 to 10 seconds. You should feel a stretch at the base of your skull. Release and relax. Repeat 10 to 15 times. The movement is small — only 1 to 2 inches of retraction. Can be performed against a wall for tactile feedback.
Benefits: Gold-standard for correcting forward head posture; Strengthens deep cervical flexors; Stretches suboccipital muscles; Widely prescribed in physical therapy; No equipment needed; Can be done anywhere, anytime
Muscles Worked (Raw): Deep cervical flexors (longus colli, longus capitis); Suboccipitals (stretched); Upper trapezius (relaxed)

Description: Lie face down on the floor with legs extended and the tops of your feet pressing into the mat. Place your hands on the floor under your shoulders, fingers pointing forward. Elbows tucked close to your body. Press your hips, thighs, and tops of feet firmly into the floor. Inhale and begin lifting your chest off the floor by straightening your arms partially (low cobra) or more fully (high cobra). Only straighten your arms as far as you can while keeping your hips on the floor. Do not push all the way to straight arms if your hips lift. Pull your shoulders back and down, away from your ears. Open your chest. Hold for 5 to 10 breaths. Keep the back of your neck long — look slightly forward, not straight up. Exhale and lower back down under control.
Benefits: Extends and strengthens the spine; Opens the chest and stretches the abdominals; Stretches the shoulders and hip flexors; Gentler than upward-facing dog — accessible to all levels; Counteracts the effects of prolonged sitting and forward-hunched posture; Foundational yoga backbend
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae (strengthened); Pectoralis major (stretched); Rectus abdominis (stretched); Anterior deltoid (stretched); Hip flexors (stretched); Gluteus maximus (engaged to protect lower back)

Description: Lie flat on your back on a mat or comfortable surface. Let your legs fall open and relaxed. Place your arms slightly away from your body with palms up. Allow your shoulders to relax flat to the floor. Close your eyes and breathe slowly. Let go of any tension in the body. Stay still and quiet for several minutes. Slowly come back to seated when ready.
Benefits: Full body relaxation; Calms the nervous system; No equipment needed; Useful at end of yoga; Releases tension; Strong recovery pose
Muscles Worked (Raw): Lower back; Neck; Shoulders

Description: Stand with feet much wider than shoulder-width, toes pointing forward or slightly out. Shift your weight to the right by bending your right knee while keeping your left leg straight. Lower into a deep squat on your right leg. Your left leg extends straight to the side with the foot flexed (toes up). Keep your right heel flat on the floor. Sit your right hip back and down. Hold the deepest position briefly. Feel the stretch in your left adductor and the load in your right leg. Drive through your right foot to stand back up. Shift to the left side and repeat. Continue alternating for the desired total reps.
Benefits: Builds hip mobility and adductor flexibility; Develops unilateral leg strength; Trains balance and coordination; Excellent warm-up for lower-body training; No equipment needed; Improves squat depth over time
Muscles Worked (Raw): Quadriceps (working leg); Gluteus maximus and medius (working leg); Adductors (extended leg, stretched); Hamstrings (extended leg); Calves and ankle stabilizers; Core (stabilizer)

Description: Kneel facing away from a couch, bench, or wall. Place your right shin vertically against the couch with the top of your right foot pressing against the surface. Step your left foot forward into a 90-degree lunge position. Left foot flat on the floor. Brace your core. Squeeze your right glute hard — this protects the lower back. Push your hips forward gently. Feel the deep stretch through your right hip flexor and quad. For more intensity, raise your torso to fully upright and reach your arms overhead. For maximum intensity, gently arch your upper back. Hold for 30 seconds to 2 minutes per side. Breathe deeply.
Benefits: One of the deepest hip flexor and quad stretches available; Critical for anyone who sits a lot; Improves hip extension dramatically; Carries over to squat depth and running performance; Builds glute activation through the back-leg squeeze; Used heavily in mobility-focused programs
Muscles Worked (Raw): Iliopsoas (hip flexor); Rectus femoris (heavy stretch); Vastus muscles; Tensor fasciae latae; Sartorius

Description: Lie flat on your back on the floor. Extend your legs straight, slightly apart, with feet falling open naturally. Place your arms slightly away from your body with palms facing up. Close your eyes. Take a few deep breaths to settle. Consciously relax every muscle in your body — start at your feet and work upward. Release any tension in your jaw, face, neck, and shoulders. Allow your breath to flow naturally. Do not control it. Stay aware but completely relaxed. If thoughts arise, gently return attention to the breath. Hold for 5 to 15 minutes. To exit, gently wiggle fingers and toes, roll to your right side, then sit up slowly.
Benefits: Promotes deep physical and mental relaxation; Reduces stress and lowers cortisol; Allows the body to integrate the benefits of practice; Calms the nervous system; Improves sleep quality with regular practice; Foundation pose of every yoga practice
Muscles Worked (Raw): Full-body relaxation (no muscles actively engaged); Activates the parasympathetic nervous system

Description: Sit on the floor with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Place your hands on the floor behind your hips, fingers pointing toward your feet (or sideways for less strain). Press through your hands and feet to lift your hips up toward the ceiling. Continue lifting until your body forms a tabletop — straight line from knees to shoulders. Squeeze your glutes hard. Open your chest by pulling your shoulder blades down and back. Look forward or slightly up. Hold for 20 to 60 seconds, or “crab walk” forward and back by alternating opposite hand and foot. Lower your hips back to the floor under control.
Benefits: Strengthens the triceps, glutes, and posterior shoulders; Opens the chest, shoulders, and hip flexors; Counteracts forward-hunched posture; Builds wrist and shoulder stability; No equipment needed; Engaging combined exercise
Muscles Worked (Raw): Triceps brachii; Gluteus maximus; Posterior deltoid; Hamstrings; Pectoralis major (stretched); Hip flexors (stretched)

Description: Start on your hands and knees in a tabletop position. Hands under shoulders, knees under hips, spine neutral. Inhale and drop your belly toward the floor while lifting your tailbone and head toward the ceiling. Arch your back gently. Open your chest forward. Look up slightly without crunching your neck. Feel the stretch across your front body and the gentle compression in your lower back. Hold for one breath, then exhale and round your back into Cat Pose. Continue alternating between cow and cat for 8 to 12 cycles. Move with your breath — inhale into cow, exhale into cat.
Benefits: Mobilizes the spine into extension; Warms up the entire back gently; Combined with cat pose, creates spinal flexion-extension flow; Calming and meditative; No equipment needed; Foundational yoga warm-up
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae (engaged); Rectus abdominis (stretched); Pectoralis major (slight stretch); Hip flexors (slight stretch)

Description: Squat down with feet together and place your palms flat on the floor. Set your hands shoulder-width apart in front of you. Plant the fingers wide for stability. Bring your knees up to rest high on the back of your upper arms. Lean forward slowly to shift weight to the hands. Lift one foot off the floor briefly to find balance. Lift both feet off the floor when ready, balancing on the hands. Hold the balance with the gaze forward then lower the feet down.
Benefits: Builds wrist and forearm strength; Trains balance and body control; Strong yoga arm balance; No equipment needed; Useful core builder; Improves coordination
Muscles Worked (Raw): Wrist flexors; Forearms; Anterior deltoid; Core

Description: Stand tall in Mountain Pose with feet together or hip-width apart. Reach both arms straight overhead. Clasp your hands together with index fingers extended (or grip one wrist). Engage your core. Press your feet firmly into the floor. Lean your upper body to the right by bending at the waist. Keep your hips facing forward and level. Feel the stretch through your left side body — obliques, lats, and intercostals. Look up under your top arm or straight ahead. Hold for 5 to 8 breaths. Breathe deeply into the stretched side. Return to center on an inhale and switch sides.
Benefits: Stretches the obliques, lats, and intercostals; Opens the side body and improves lateral flexibility; Improves breathing capacity by opening the rib cage; Energizing and accessible to all levels; No equipment needed; Quick stretch that can be done anywhere
Muscles Worked (Raw): External and internal obliques (stretched side); Quadratus lumborum; Latissimus dorsi (stretched side); Intercostal muscles; Deltoids (overhead position)

Description: Lie face down on the floor with legs extended back. Place your forearms on the floor in front of you, stacked one on top of the other. Rest your forehead on your top forearm. Let your legs relax. Feet can be hip-width apart with toes turned out, or together — whatever is most comfortable. Close your eyes. Breathe deeply into your belly. Feel your belly press into the floor on each inhale and release on each exhale. Hold for 1 to 5 minutes. This is a restorative pose — relax fully into it. To exit, slowly press up to a kneeling position.
Benefits: Decompresses the lower back; Calms the nervous system; Teaches deep belly breathing; Restorative — useful between active poses or as cool-down; Reduces stress and anxiety; No equipment needed
Muscles Worked (Raw): Lower back (gentle decompression); Diaphragm (deep breathing); Full body (relaxation)

Description: Stand or sit tall with feet hip-width apart. Bring your right arm straight across your body at chest height. Place your left hand on the back of your right upper arm, just above the elbow. Gently pull your right arm closer to your chest with your left hand. Feel the stretch through your right posterior shoulder. Keep your shoulders square — do not rotate your torso. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch arms and repeat.
Benefits: Stretches the posterior deltoid and rhomboids; Quick and accessible; Useful between sets of pulling exercises; No equipment needed; Improves shoulder flexibility; Counteracts tight rear shoulders
Muscles Worked (Raw): Posterior deltoid (primary); Rhomboids; Trapezius (middle fibers); Latissimus dorsi (slight)

Description: Kneel on your right knee with your left foot flat in front (90-degree bend in left knee). Squeeze your right glute hard. Push your hips slightly forward to engage the standard hip flexor stretch. Reach your right arm up overhead. Lean your torso to the left (toward the front leg) while maintaining the hip flexor stretch. Feel the deeper stretch through your right hip flexor, IT band, and side body. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch sides and repeat. Use a pad under the kneeling knee for comfort.
Benefits: Deeper hip flexor stretch than the standard kneeling version; Addresses the IT band and lateral hip simultaneously; Improves hip mobility for squats and lunges; Counteracts the effects of prolonged sitting; No equipment needed; Excellent post-workout stretch
Muscles Worked (Raw): Iliopsoas (hip flexor); Tensor fasciae latae; IT band; Quadratus lumborum; Obliques

Description: Stand under a sturdy pull-up bar. Reach up and grip the bar with both hands at shoulder-width, palms facing forward (overhand grip). Lift your feet off the floor. Hang with arms fully extended. Let your shoulders relax slightly into the hang — feel the gentle stretch in your lats and decompression of your spine. Engage your core gently. Do not swing. Hold for 20 to 60 seconds, building up to 90 seconds or more over time. Lower your feet back to the floor when you can no longer maintain the hang. Use a chair or box if you cannot reach the bar from standing. For grip development: alternate overhand and underhand grips on different sets.
Benefits: Decompresses the spine through traction; Builds grip strength and endurance; Improves shoulder mobility and flexibility; Foundational position for pull-ups; Stretches the lats and shoulders; No equipment needed beyond a pull-up bar
Muscles Worked (Raw): Forearms and grip; Latissimus dorsi (stretched); Shoulders (decompression); Core (gentle engagement)

Description: Stand tall with feet together. Shift your weight onto one foot. Bend the other knee and grab the inside of the lifted foot. Lift the lifted foot up and back behind you. Reach the opposite arm forward for balance. Press the foot back into your hand to lift the leg higher. Feel a deep stretch in the front of the lifted leg. Hold the balance then lower the leg. Switch sides.
Benefits: Deep quad and hip flexor stretch; Trains single-leg balance; Opens the chest; No equipment needed; Strong yoga balance pose; Useful for athletes
Muscles Worked (Raw): Quadriceps; Hip flexors; Pectoralis major

Description: Stand with feet hip-width apart, parallel to each other. Distribute your weight evenly across both feet — front, back, inside, and outside edges. Engage your quads slightly to lift your kneecaps. Avoid locking your knees fully. Tilt your pelvis to a neutral position — neither tucked nor anteriorly tilted. Lengthen your spine. Lift your chest. Pull your shoulders back and down. Let your arms hang relaxed at your sides, palms facing your thighs. Lengthen the back of your neck. Tuck your chin slightly. Crown of head reaches up. Hold this position for 1 to 2 minutes, breathing naturally and observing your alignment.
Benefits: Builds posture awareness; Resets alignment after sitting; Foundation for all standing exercises; Calming and grounding; No equipment needed; Useful as a daily posture check
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae (postural); Core (stabilizer); Quadriceps (slight); Foot intrinsic muscles

Description: Start in a tabletop position. Lower onto your forearms with elbows under shoulders. Clasp your hands together or keep palms down, fingers spread. Tuck your toes and lift your hips up and back, forming an inverted V — like Downward Dog but on forearms. Press your forearms firmly into the floor. Lengthen through your spine. Bring your hips toward your hands as much as possible. Heels reach toward the floor. Keep your head between your arms. Engage your core. Hold for 5 to 10 breaths. Breathe deeply. To rest, lower into Child’s Pose.
Benefits: Builds shoulder and upper-back strength; Develops core stability through the inversion; Stretches the hamstrings and calves; Preparation for forearm stand and handstand; Improves shoulder mobility; No equipment needed
Muscles Worked (Raw): Deltoids (heavy isometric); Latissimus dorsi; Trapezius (lower); Core (stabilizer); Hamstrings and calves (stretched); Triceps brachii (isometric)

Description: Kneel on the floor with knees together. Point your feet straight back, with the tops of your feet pressing into the floor. Sit back onto your heels. Your hips should rest on top of your heels. Place your hands on your thighs or at your sides for support. Sit up tall. Feel the stretch through the front of your shins, tops of your feet, and ankles. To deepen, lean back slightly while supporting your weight on your hands behind you. Hold for 20 to 45 seconds. Breathe deeply. To exit, lean forward and lift your hips off your heels carefully.
Benefits: Stretches the often-neglected tibialis anterior; Opens the tops of the feet and ankles; Useful for runners with shin tightness; Helps with shin splint prevention; No equipment needed; Easy to integrate into mobility routines
Muscles Worked (Raw): Tibialis anterior (front of shin); Extensor digitorum longus; Extensor hallucis longus; Foot extensors; Quadriceps (slight stretch)

Description: Lie on your back. Curl your head and shoulders up. Hug your knees to your chest. Brace your core. Press your lower back into the floor. Inhale and simultaneously extend your arms overhead and your legs straight out at a 45-degree angle from the floor. Hold the extended position briefly. Keep your shoulders curled up off the floor. Exhale and circle your arms around to the sides, returning your hands to your knees as you bend your knees back to your chest. Continue for 5 to 10 reps with smooth, coordinated motion. Keep your lower back pressed into the floor. If it lifts, raise the leg angle higher. Move with control — this is about quality, not speed.
Benefits: Builds core endurance and control; Develops limb coordination with stable trunk; Trains the core to resist arching under load; Foundational Pilates mat exercise; No equipment needed; Builds dynamic ab strength
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Hip flexors; Transverse abdominis; Deltoids (arm extension); Quadriceps (leg extension)

Description: Sit on the floor with both legs extended. Sit up tall. Bend your right knee and place your right shin parallel to the front of your mat. Stack your left shin directly on top of your right shin, with your left ankle over your right knee and your left knee over your right ankle. If your top knee floats high above the bottom ankle, use a blanket under your sit bones or try a gentler hip stretch first. Flex both feet to protect your knees. Sit up tall. For a deeper stretch, fold forward from the hips with a flat back. Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply into the stretch. Switch the stacking order and repeat on the other side.
Benefits: Deeply stretches the piriformis and outer hips; Opens the glutes and deep hip rotators; Improves external hip rotation; More intense than standard pigeon pose for many lifters; Calming and restorative; Develops hip flexibility over time
Muscles Worked (Raw): Piriformis; Gluteus maximus and medius; Deep hip external rotators; IT band (tensor fasciae latae)

Exercise Name: Downward Facing Dog Adho Mukha Svanasana
Description: Start on your hands and knees in tabletop position. Hands shoulder-width apart, knees hip-width apart. Tuck your toes and lift your hips up and back into an inverted V shape. Press your hands firmly into the floor. Spread your fingers wide. Straighten your legs as much as comfortable. It is okay to keep a slight bend in the knees. Press your heels toward the floor — they may not reach. Lengthen your spine. Push your hips up and back. Your body should form an inverted V. Let your head hang naturally between your arms. Keep your neck relaxed. Hold for 5 to 10 breaths. Breathe deeply.
Benefits: Stretches the hamstrings, calves, and shoulders; Strengthens the arms, shoulders, and core; Decompresses the spine; Improves circulation; Foundational yoga pose; Calming and energizing simultaneously
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings (stretched); Gastrocnemius and soleus; Latissimus dorsi (stretched); Anterior deltoid (loaded); Triceps brachii; Core (stabilizer); Erector spinae

Description: Start on your hands and knees with your wrists directly under your shoulders and your knees directly under your hips. Spread your fingers wide and press firmly through your palms and knuckles. Tuck your toes under. Exhale and lift your knees away from the floor, sending your hips up and back. Keep a slight bend in your knees at first. Lengthen your tailbone away from your pelvis and press it gently toward the ceiling. Your body should form an inverted V. Press your heels down toward the floor (they do not need to touch) and gradually straighten your legs without locking your knees. Rotate your upper arms outward to broaden your shoulders away from your ears. Keep your head between your upper arms with your gaze toward your navel or feet. Hold for 5 to 10 deep breaths. To exit, lower your knees back down to a tabletop position or step forward into a forward fold.
Benefits: Stretches the hamstrings, calves, and Achilles tendons; Opens the shoulders, chest, and lats; Strengthens the arms, shoulders, and core; Decompresses the spine and helps relieve back tension; Mild inversion that improves circulation and energy; Builds full-body awareness and is a key transitional pose in vinyasa flows
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings; Gastrocnemius and soleus (calves); Latissimus dorsi; Deltoids; Triceps; Serratus anterior; Erector spinae

Description: Start in a downward facing dog with hips high and arms strong. Press the chest toward the thighs and aim heels toward the floor. Lift one hand off the floor. Reach that hand under the body to touch the opposite foot. Allow the hips to shift slightly during the reach. Return the hand to the floor and reset the dog position. Reach the other hand to the opposite foot. Continue alternating reaches for the full set.
Benefits: Stretches the hamstrings dynamically.; Opens the lats and shoulders.; Improves rotational mobility through the cross reach.; Trains balance on three points of contact.; No equipment needed.; Excellent warm up before squats and deadlifts.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings; Latissimus dorsi; Obliques; Posterior deltoid

Description: Start in a high plank with hands under shoulders and body straight. Push the hips up and back into a downward facing dog. Press the chest toward the thighs and aim heels toward the floor. From the dog position, round the spine by tucking the tailbone. Then arch the spine and lift the chest toward the floor. Continue alternating between rounding and arching the spine. Keep the arms strong and the hands grounded. Maintain steady breathing through every movement.
Benefits: Mobilizes the entire spine through flexion and extension.; Stretches the hamstrings and calves.; Opens the shoulders and chest.; Decompresses the lumbar spine.; Improves overall spinal health.; No equipment needed.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae; Hamstrings; Latissimus dorsi; Anterior deltoid

Description: Sit on the floor with your legs spread wide in a V-shape. Flex both feet so your toes point up. Sit up tall through the spine. Place your hands on the floor in front of you. Hinge at the hips and walk your hands forward. Lower your torso toward the floor as far as is comfortable. Keep your back as long as possible without rounding. Hold the pose and breathe deeply, then walk your hands back to sit up.
Benefits: Deeply opens the hips and inner thighs; Stretches the hamstrings; Lengthens the lower back; Calms the nervous system; Useful for yin yoga practice
Muscles Worked (Raw): Adductors; Hamstrings; Hips; Spine

Description: Sit on the floor with one leg bent at 90 degrees in front and the other bent at 90 degrees to the side. Both knees should be on the floor in their bent positions. Place hands on the floor at your sides for stability. Brace the core and lift the chest tall. Pivot the hips to flip both legs to the opposite 90 90 position. Try to keep both knees on the floor throughout the transition. Hold briefly in the new 90 90 position. Continue switching sides for the full set.
Benefits: Improves internal and external hip rotation.; Opens tight hip capsules.; Strengthens the hip rotators.; Excellent before squats and lunges.; No equipment needed.; Carryover to athletic hip movement.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus medius; Gluteus maximus; Hip flexors; Adductors

Description: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Reach both arms overhead. Lean to the right side, reaching your left arm over your head and across. Return to center. Lean to the left side, reaching your right arm over and across. Return to center. Twist your torso to the right, letting your arms swing. Twist to the left. Continue alternating side bends and twists for 10 to 15 reps each direction.
Benefits: Dynamically warms up the entire back; Mobilizes the thoracic spine; Stretches the lats and obliques; Excellent pre-workout warm-up; No equipment needed; Engaging and active
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi; Obliques; Erector spinae; Quadratus lumborum; Thoracic spine rotators

Description: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Extend both arms forward at shoulder height. Brace your core gently. Swing both arms back as far as comfortable, opening your chest. Pause briefly at the back of the swing. Bring your arms back forward, crossing them at the chest if comfortable. Continue swinging back and forward in a controlled rhythm. Move at a moderate pace — not ballistic. Perform 10 to 15 reps as part of a warm-up.
Benefits: Dynamically warms up the chest and front shoulders; Increases blood flow before training; Improves shoulder mobility; Excellent pre-workout warm-up; No equipment needed; Engaging and active
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major (stretched dynamically); Anterior deltoid; Rhomboids (engaged on backswing); Trapezius (middle fibers)

Description: Stand tall. Shift your weight to your right leg with a slight knee bend. Cross your left leg over your right thigh. If possible, hook your left foot behind your right calf. Extend your arms forward and cross your right arm over your left at the elbows. Bend your elbows and try to bring your palms together (or backs of hands together). Lift your elbows to shoulder height. Reach your fingertips toward the ceiling. Sink slightly deeper into your standing leg. Keep your core engaged for balance. Hold for 5 to 10 breaths. Gaze at a fixed point for balance. Unwind and switch sides.
Benefits: Deeply stretches the upper back, shoulders, and outer hips; Builds single-leg balance and ankle stability; Improves concentration and focus; Strengthens the standing leg; Opens the rhomboids and posterior deltoid; No equipment needed
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rhomboids and trapezius (stretched); Posterior deltoid (stretched); Gluteus medius (stretched); Quadriceps (standing leg); Core (anti-rotation); Calves and ankle stabilizers

Description: Stand tall with feet together and a slight bend in the knees. Lift one leg and cross it over the other thigh. Hook the foot behind the standing leg calf if possible. Cross the opposite arm under and over so the elbows stack. Wrap the forearms around each other and bring the palms together. Lift the elbows up to shoulder height. Sink down slightly to deepen the pose. Hold the balance and breathe. Switch sides.
Benefits: Stretches the upper back; Opens the shoulders; Trains balance; No equipment needed; Strong yoga twist; Releases shoulder tension
Muscles Worked (Raw): Posterior deltoid; Rhomboids; Hip flexors

Description: Stand facing a wall, arm’s length away. Extend your right arm straight to the side at shoulder height. Palm facing the wall. Place your right palm flat against the wall with fingers pointing back behind you. Slowly rotate your body away from the wall while keeping the arm straight and the palm on the wall. Feel the stretch through your right biceps and forearm. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch arms and repeat. Adjust the angle of the arm (higher or lower) to target different fibers.
Benefits: Stretches the biceps brachii and brachialis; Counteracts tightness from heavy pulling and curling; Improves elbow extension; Helps prevent elbow tendinitis; No equipment needed beyond a wall; Quick and accessible
Muscles Worked (Raw): Biceps brachii; Brachialis; Brachioradialis; Pectoralis major (slight)

Description: Stand tall with feet at hip-width. Place your fingertips on top of each shoulder. Keep the arms bent at the elbows. Brace your core and keep your chest up. Begin circling the elbows forward in big arcs. Reach the elbows up high and bring them down low. Continue several circles in one direction. Reverse the direction and circle the elbows backward.
Benefits: Mobilizes the shoulders; Warms up the rotator cuff; No equipment needed; Useful warm-up move; Easy to add to any session; Improves shoulder mobility
Muscles Worked (Raw): Anterior deltoid; Posterior deltoid; Rotator cuff

Description: Stand or sit tall. Raise your right arm out to the side at shoulder height with elbow bent at 90 degrees, forearm pointing up (palm facing forward). Use your left hand to gently grip the back of your right wrist. Slowly press your right forearm down toward the floor (internally rotating the shoulder). Stop when you feel a gentle stretch through the back of your right shoulder. Hold for 15 to 20 seconds. Breathe deeply. Then reverse — press the forearm back up (externally rotating). Switch arms and repeat. Apply only gentle pressure — never force shoulder rotation.
Benefits: Stretches the rotator cuff; Improves shoulder mobility; Excellent shoulder warm-up; Useful for rehabilitation; No equipment needed; Quick and accessible
Muscles Worked (Raw): Infraspinatus (external rotator); Teres minor; Subscapularis (internal rotator); Posterior deltoid

Description: Sit on a stability ball. Walk your feet forward and slowly roll your body back so your upper back and shoulders rest on the ball. Keep your knees bent at 90 degrees with feet flat on the floor. Allow your head to relax back. Reach your arms overhead toward the floor. Let gravity decompress your spine. Feel the stretch through your back, chest, and abs. Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply and relax. To exit, drop your hips toward the floor and roll forward off the ball, then sit up. Use a smaller ball for less depth or a larger ball for more arch. Stop immediately if you feel any spine discomfort or dizziness.
Benefits: Decompresses the spine; Counteracts forward-hunched posture from sitting; Stretches the abs, chest, and front shoulders; Calming and restorative; Excellent post-workout cool-down; Improves spinal extension mobility
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae (decompressed); Rectus abdominis (stretched); Pectoralis major (stretched); Anterior deltoid (stretched); Hip flexors (stretched)

Description: Place a stability ball on the floor behind you. Kneel on your right knee with your left foot flat in front in a 90-degree lunge. Place the top of your right foot on the stability ball behind you. Squeeze your right glute hard. Push your hips forward. The ball allows your back leg to extend further than the floor would, creating a deeper hip flexor stretch. Keep your torso upright. Reach your arms overhead for more intensity. Use the ball gently — do not bounce or push aggressively. Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch sides and repeat.
Benefits: Deeper hip flexor stretch than floor versions; Comfortable support from the ball; Allows the back leg to extend fully; Excellent for very tight hip flexors; Builds stability through balance demand on the ball; Useful when a couch is unavailable
Muscles Worked (Raw): Iliopsoas; Rectus femoris; Tensor fasciae latae; Sartorius

Description: Stand or sit tall with shoulders pulled back and down. Clasp your hands behind your head with elbows wide. Pull your elbows back, opening your chest as much as possible. Squeeze your shoulder blades together. Lift your chest tall. Avoid arching your lower back. Feel the deep stretch across your chest and front shoulders. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Release and repeat 2 to 3 times.
Benefits: Deeply opens the chest and front shoulders; Counteracts forward-rounded posture; Quick and accessible; No equipment needed; Excellent post-workout stretch; Improves overhead pressing position
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major (stretched); Anterior deltoid (stretched); Biceps brachii; Rhomboids and mid-traps (engaged)

Description: Place a stability ball in front of you. Kneel down behind the ball. Drape your body forward over the top of the ball. Wrap your arms around the front of the ball. Allow the chest to sink into the ball. Feel the stretch through the chest and front shoulders. Hold the position and breathe slowly. Slowly come back up off the ball.
Benefits: Stretches the chest; Opens the front shoulders; Releases upper back tension; Useful cool-down stretch; Easy to add to any session; Strong passive stretch
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Anterior deltoid; Latissimus dorsi

Description: Kneel on the floor with a stability ball in front of you. Place both forearms on the ball. Sit your hips back toward your heels. Let your chest sink toward the floor. Roll the ball forward by extending your arms. Press your chest down as you reach. Feel the deep stretch through your lats, armpits, and shoulders. Keep your spine long and head between your arms. Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply. Slowly walk the ball back toward you to release. For a unilateral version, hinge to one side and stretch one lat at a time.
Benefits: Deeply stretches the lats and side body; Ball allows greater reach than fixed surfaces; Opens the shoulders and armpits; Decompresses the spine; Excellent post-pulling-day stretch; Calming and restorative
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi (deep stretch); Teres major; Triceps brachii (long head); Posterior deltoid; Erector spinae (lengthened)

Exercise Name: Exercise Ball Lower Back Prone Stretch
Description: Kneel in front of a stability ball. Lower the body forward over the ball. Allow the abdomen and chest to drape over the top. Set the arms relaxed at the sides or in front. Set the feet wide on the floor for support. Allow the spine to round and the back to relax. Breathe slowly and deeply. Hold for the desired duration.
Benefits: Decompresses the lower back.; Stretches the spine.; Useful after heavy lifting.; Joint friendly release.; Calms the nervous system.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae; Quadratus lumborum; Gluteus maximus

Exercise Name: Exercise Ball Lying Side Lat Stretch
Description: Kneel next to a stability ball. Lower the side of the body onto the ball. Set the bottom leg long on the floor for stability. Reach the top arm straight overhead. Allow the side body to drape over the ball. Breathe slowly and deeply into the stretch. Hold for the desired duration. Switch sides and repeat.
Benefits: Stretches the lats.; Opens the obliques.; Decompresses the side body.; Useful for shoulder mobility.; Joint friendly stretch.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi; Obliques; Quadratus lumborum

Description: Start in Warrior II: right foot forward with knee bent 90 degrees, left leg extended back, hips open, arms extended. Place your right forearm on your right thigh just above the knee. Press elbow into thigh. Reach your left arm up and overhead, alongside your ear. Palm faces the floor. Form a straight line from your left foot through your hips, torso, and left arm. Open your chest toward the ceiling. Press your back foot firmly into the floor. Look up at your top hand or forward if that strains your neck. Hold for 5 to 8 breaths. Use each exhale to deepen the stretch. Return to Warrior II, then switch sides.
Benefits: Deeply stretches the side body and obliques; Builds leg endurance through the lunge hold; Opens the hips and groin; Stretches the inner thigh of the front leg; Improves balance and concentration; Foundational standing yoga pose
Muscles Worked (Raw): Quadriceps (front leg); Adductors (front leg); Obliques and intercostals (top side); Latissimus dorsi (stretched); Hip flexors (back leg, stretched)

Description: Sit on the floor or a chair with one leg crossed over the other. Hold the ankle of the top leg with one hand for support. Use the other hand to slowly rotate the foot in a full circle. Move the ankle through its complete range of motion. Complete several circles in one direction. Reverse and rotate the ankle in the opposite direction. Repeat the rotations on the other ankle. Continue rotations in both directions for each ankle.
Benefits: Improves ankle mobility through full range.; Reduces stiffness in the foot and ankle joints.; Excellent warm up for runners and lifters.; No equipment needed.; Helps prevent ankle sprains.; Easy to do anytime, anywhere.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Calves; Soleus; Tibialis anterior

Description: Stand in a doorway. Bend your right elbow to 90 degrees. Place your right forearm against the doorframe with the elbow at shoulder height.
