Gently step your right foot forward through the doorway. Feel the stretch through the front of your right shoulder and chest. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Adjust the elbow height to target different fibers — higher elbow stretches lower chest, lower elbow stretches upper chest. Switch arms and repeat. Avoid overstretching — go only to a comfortable depth.
Benefits: Opens the front of the shoulder and chest; Improves shoulder external rotation range; Counteracts tight front delts from pressing; Easy to do in any doorway; No equipment needed; Quick and accessible
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Anterior deltoid; Subscapularis (rotator cuff); Biceps brachii (slight)

Exercise Name: Feet and Ankles Side to Side Stretch
Description: Stand tall with the feet shoulder width apart. Hold a wall or rail for balance support if needed. Brace the core and keep the chest up. Roll both feet onto their outside edges. Hold for a beat at the outer position. Roll both feet onto their inside edges. Hold for a beat at the inner position. Continue rocking side to side for the working set.
Benefits: Mobilizes the ankle joint.; Stretches the lower leg muscles.; Useful for warm-up and recovery.; Improves balance and foot control.; Reduces ankle stiffness.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Tibialis anterior; Calves; Soleus

Description: Sit on the floor with the legs extended in front. Brace your core and keep the spine tall. Lift one foot slightly off the floor. Rotate the ankle in a slow circle in one direction. Continue full range circles for several repetitions. Reverse direction and circle the other way. Point the toes forward then flex them back to the shin. Repeat the full sequence with the other foot.
Benefits: Builds ankle mobility; Useful for runners; Stretches the feet; No equipment needed; Strong warm-up move; Easy to do anywhere
Muscles Worked (Raw): Calves; Tibialis anterior; Peroneals

Description: Stand or sit. Extend your right arm straight in front with the palm facing down. Use your left hand to gently push your right hand down, flexing the wrist forward. Keep your right elbow straight throughout. Feel the stretch through the top of your right forearm and the back of your right hand. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch hands and repeat. Avoid letting your shoulder rotate inward — keep it neutral. Apply only gentle pressure.
Benefits: Stretches the wrist extensors and forearm extensors; Helps prevent tennis elbow; Balances out gripping/flexion-dominant activities; Quick and accessible; No equipment needed; Useful for typists, climbers, and lifters
Muscles Worked (Raw): Wrist extensors (extensor carpi radialis, extensor carpi ulnaris); Extensor digitorum; Brachioradialis; Anconeus

Description: Extend your right arm straight out in front of you at shoulder height. Palm facing down. Gently flex your right wrist down so your fingers point toward the floor. With your left hand, gently press the back of your right hand toward your body to deepen the stretch. Optionally, curl your right fingers into a loose fist to add an extensor stretch. Feel the stretch through the back of your right forearm. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch arms and repeat. Perform two to three times per arm.
Benefits: Stretches the forearm extensors; Helps prevent tennis elbow; Relieves forearm fatigue from gripping work; Quick and accessible; No equipment needed; Useful for climbers, lifters, and computer users
Muscles Worked (Raw): Extensor digitorum; Extensor carpi radialis; Extensor carpi ulnaris; Brachioradialis

Description: Stand or sit. Extend your right arm straight in front of you with the palm facing up. Use your left hand to gently pull the fingers of your right hand back, toward your body. Keep your right elbow straight throughout. Feel the stretch through your right palm and the inside of your right forearm. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch hands and repeat. For deeper stretch: extend the wrist further or include thumb extension. Apply gentle pressure only — never force the stretch.
Benefits: Stretches the wrist flexors and finger flexors; Essential for grip-intensive activities; Helps prevent forearm overuse injuries; Useful for typists, climbers, lifters, and musicians; Quick and accessible; No equipment needed
Muscles Worked (Raw): Wrist flexors (flexor carpi radialis, flexor carpi ulnaris); Flexor digitorum superficialis; Flexor digitorum profundus; Palmaris longus

Description: Hold both hands out in front of you with palms facing down. Spread your fingers as wide as possible. Hold for 5 seconds. Slowly close your hands into tight fists. Hold for 5 seconds. Repeat the open-close sequence 5 times. Next, use your left hand to gently pull each finger of your right hand backward into extension, holding each for 5 seconds. Repeat for the left hand. Finish with finger circles — small clockwise and counter-clockwise circles with each finger. Total time: 2 to 3 minutes for both hands.
Benefits: Improves hand mobility; Releases gripping and typing tightness; Useful for climbers, lifters, and typists; Helpful for anyone with hand stiffness; Quick and accessible; No equipment needed
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hand intrinsic muscles; Finger flexors and extensors; Lumbricals and interossei; Forearm flexors and extensors (secondary)

Description: Lie flat on your back with legs extended and feet together. Arms at your sides. Place your hands palms-down underneath your hips. Slide your forearms and elbows under your body. Press your forearms and elbows into the floor. Lift your chest and arch your upper back off the floor. Tilt your head back and gently rest the crown of your head on the floor (do not put weight on it). Open your chest fully. The weight should be on your forearms, not your head or neck. Hold for 5 to 8 breaths. Breathe deeply into your chest. To exit, lift your head, lower your back, and rest flat on the floor.
Benefits: Opens the chest and throat; Stretches the front of the neck and shoulders; Counter pose to shoulder stand and forward folds; Improves posture and breathing capacity; Energizing and uplifting; No equipment needed
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae (upper back); Pectoralis major (stretched); Anterior deltoid (stretched); Sternocleidomastoid (stretched); Hip flexors (slight)

Description: Stand facing a sturdy bar at chest to head height (squat rack barbell, doorway pull-up bar, or sturdy pole). Grip the bar with both hands at shoulder-width using an overhand grip. Walk your feet back and lean your hips away from the bar, keeping your arms straight. Allow your body to hinge backward at the hips — your arms and torso form a straight line. Push your hips back and let the bar traction your spine and lats. Feel the deep stretch through your lats, shoulders, and upper back. Hold for 20 to 45 seconds. Breathe deeply. Walk forward to release and stand up.
Benefits: Decompresses the spine; Stretches the lats and shoulders; Accessible — feet stay on the floor; Adjustable depth via foot position; No equipment needed beyond a bar; Excellent post-pull-up cooldown
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi (stretched); Teres major; Posterior deltoid; Erector spinae; Forearms (grip)

Description: Stand tall with the feet hip width apart. Brace your core and keep the chest up. Lift one knee up toward the chest for hip flexion. Hold briefly at the top. Lower the leg and swing it back behind you for extension. Squeeze the glute at the back position. Return to start and repeat the pattern. Finish all reps then switch sides.
Benefits: Mobilizes the hips; Trains the hip flexors; Strong warm-up move; Useful mobility drill; Builds hip range; Activates the glutes
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hip Flexors; Gluteus maximus; Hamstrings

Description: Lie face down on the floor with legs extended. Extend both arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height — body and arms form a T. Thumbs point up to the ceiling, palms facing down. Press your forehead into the floor or look at the floor between your arms. Engage your core and glutes for stability. Lift both arms straight up off the floor by squeezing your shoulder blades together. Hold for 1 to 2 seconds at the top. Lower under control. Repeat for 12 to 15 reps. Use no weight or light dumbbells.
Benefits: Activates the rear delts and mid-traps directly; No equipment needed; Builds postural muscles; Excellent rehab and warm-up exercise; Counteracts forward-rounded shoulders; Improves shoulder mobility
Muscles Worked (Raw): Posterior deltoid; Trapezius (middle fibers); Rhomboids; Erector spinae (slight)

Description: Place a foam roller on the floor. Lie face down with the roller under your hip flexors. Support your weight on your forearms. Cross one leg behind the other for stability. Slowly roll your hips over the roller from the top of the thigh to the hip bone. Pause on any tight spots and breathe through them. Continue rolling for a comfortable duration. Switch sides and repeat.
Benefits: Releases tight hip flexors; Improves hip mobility; Useful before lower body training; Great for desk workers; Reduces hip soreness
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hip flexors; Hips; Quadriceps

Description: Place a foam roller on the floor. Sit with one shin in front of you bent at a 90-degree angle. Position the roller under the front leg glute. Extend the back leg straight behind you. Place your hands on the floor for support. Lean forward to apply pressure to the glute. Slowly shift back and forth over the tight spots. Switch sides and repeat.
Benefits: Releases tight glutes; Combines stretch with myofascial release; Improves hip mobility; Useful for runners and lifters; Relieves deep glute tension
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus maximus; Gluteus medius; Piriformis

Description: Stand facing a wall with a foam roller pressed vertically against it. Place both forearms on the roller with the elbows bent. Brace the core and keep the chest up. Roll the foam roller up the wall by reaching the arms overhead. Press the arms forward to upwardly rotate the shoulder blades. Reach up as far as possible with the elbows close. Roll the foam roller back down with control. Continue for the working set.
Benefits: Activates the serratus anterior.; Improves overhead mobility.; Builds shoulder health.; Useful warm-up.; Trains scapular control.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Serratus anterior; Trapezius; Anterior deltoid

Description: Stand or sit tall. Extend your right arm straight in front with the palm facing up. Pin your right elbow against your side. Keep your right forearm horizontal. Use your left hand to gently rotate your right forearm further into supination — palm twists more upward and outward. Apply slow, gentle rotation. Stop when you feel a stretch. Feel the stretch through the front of your right forearm. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch arms and repeat. Move slowly and never force the rotation.
Benefits: Stretches the pronator muscles; Relieves forearm tightness from gripping and pulling; Improves wrist and elbow mobility; Useful for lifters, golfers, and racquet sport athletes; Quick and accessible; No equipment needed
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pronator teres; Pronator quadratus; Wrist flexors (secondary); Brachioradialis

Description: Stand with your back against a wall. Feet 6 to 12 inches from the wall. Press your lower back, upper back, and head against the wall. Place your forearms flat against the wall at shoulder height, elbows at 90 degrees. Slide your forearms up the wall as high as possible while maintaining full wall contact. Slide back down to the starting position. Keep forearms, elbows, and wrists in contact with the wall throughout. If you cannot maintain contact, your thoracic mobility needs work. Aim for 10 to 15 reps.
Benefits: Develops thoracic extension and shoulder mobility; Reveals mobility limitations clearly; Physical therapy staple; No equipment needed; Builds scapular control; Excellent warm-up before overhead work
Muscles Worked (Raw): Serratus anterior; Lower trapezius; Rotator cuff; Thoracic extensors

Exercise Name: Forearms Stand Yoga Pose Pincha Mayurasana
Description: Kneel on the floor with the forearms placed shoulder width apart. Press the palms flat with the elbows directly under the shoulders. Walk the feet in toward the elbows. Lift the hips high so the torso comes vertical. Kick one leg up overhead to start the inversion. Drive the second leg up to meet the first. Squeeze the legs together and point the toes. Hold balanced on the forearms then come down with control.
Benefits: Builds serious shoulder and arm strength.; Improves balance and body awareness.; Stretches the spine in inversion.; Trains the core for stability.; Advanced inversion progression.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Anterior deltoid; Trapezius; Core; Triceps brachii

Description: Stand tall with feet hip width apart. Brace your core and lengthen the spine up. Hinge forward at the hips with a long spine. Continue folding forward toward the floor. Let the head and arms hang heavy. Hold the lower legs or floor with the hands. Hold the stretch with steady breath letting gravity deepen it. Roll up slowly to standing one vertebra at a time.
Benefits: Stretches the hamstrings; Releases the lower back; No equipment needed; Useful cool down move; Easy to do anywhere; Trains hip mobility
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings; Spinal erectors; Calves

Description: Sit or stand tall with shoulders relaxed and pulled back. Slowly tuck your chin toward your chest. Let your head drop forward naturally. Place both hands lightly on the back of your head. Do not press hard. Let the weight of your hands gently increase the stretch. Do not actively pull down. Feel the stretch through the back of your neck and upper traps. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply and relax your shoulders. Slowly release by removing your hands and lifting your head upright. Perform two to three holds.
Benefits: Relieves neck tension from phone use and desk work; Stretches the upper traps and posterior neck muscles; Quick and accessible — works anywhere; No equipment needed; Gentle enough for daily use; Often relieves tension headaches
Muscles Worked (Raw): Upper trapezius; Levator scapulae; Posterior cervical muscles; Splenius capitis

Description: Start in a high plank position. Hands directly under shoulders, body in a straight line. Shift your weight slightly forward so your shoulders move past your wrists. Lower your body by bending at the elbows. Keep elbows tucked tight against your ribs. Lower until your upper arms are parallel to the floor (elbows at 90 degrees). Maintain a perfectly straight body line from heels to head. No sagging hips, no piked butt. Hold for 1 to 5 breaths. To exit, push back up to plank or roll forward into upward-facing dog. If too difficult, drop to your knees first (knees-down chaturanga).
Benefits: Builds tremendous upper-body and core strength; Foundational vinyasa yoga pose; Develops stability and body control; Strengthens the chest, shoulders, and triceps; No equipment needed; Builds endurance for longer yoga practices
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Triceps brachii (heavy emphasis); Anterior deltoid; Serratus anterior; Core (entire trunk); Erector spinae (isometric)

Description: Start on your hands and knees. Spread your knees as wide as comfortable. Flex your feet so the inside edges of your feet press into the floor. Toes pointing out to the sides. Lower onto your forearms. Keep your hips directly above your knees. Slowly press your hips back toward your heels. Feel the deep stretch in your inner thighs and groin. Use a folded blanket or yoga mat under your knees for comfort. Hold for 1 to 3 minutes. Breathe deeply and slowly. To exit, walk your knees back together and rest in Child’s Pose. Approach this pose gradually — depth comes over weeks of practice.
Benefits: Deeply opens the adductors, groin, and inner hips; Improves hip flexibility for sumo squats and wide-stance lifts; Releases tension in the inner thighs; Used by physical therapists for hip rehabilitation; Calming despite the intensity; No equipment needed
Muscles Worked (Raw): Adductor magnus, longus, brevis (deep stretch); Gracilis; Pectineus; Hip flexors

Description: Get on your hands and knees on a mat. Slowly walk the knees out wide to the sides. Set the inside of the feet flat on the floor. Lower onto the forearms with elbows under shoulders. Drop your hips back and down toward the floor. Feel a deep stretch in the inner thighs and groin. Breathe slowly and let the hips sink lower. Hold the position then come back up gently.
Benefits: Deep groin stretch; Opens the adductors; Useful hip mobility pose; No equipment needed; Strong yoga hip opener; Releases inner thigh tension
Muscles Worked (Raw): Adductors; Hip flexors; Gluteus maximus

Description: Stand or sit tall with the chest up and shoulders relaxed. Brace the core and keep the spine neutral. Slowly tuck the chin and lower the head toward the chest. Hold the front stretch briefly and breathe steadily. Slowly lift the chin and tilt the head back to look up. Hold the back stretch briefly without overextending. Return the head to a neutral position. Continue alternating front and back stretches for the full set.
Benefits: Relieves tension in the neck and upper traps.; Improves cervical spine mobility.; Reduces stiffness from desk work.; No equipment needed.; Excellent quick break stretch.; Easy to do throughout the day.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Trapezius; Sternocleidomastoid; Levator scapulae

Description: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Step your right foot forward about a foot. Keep the right leg straight and the right heel pressed into the floor. Lift the toes of your right foot off the floor (dorsiflexion). Bend your back (left) knee slightly. Place both hands on your left thigh for support. Hinge forward at the hips over your right leg, keeping your back flat. Continue hinging until you feel a deep stretch in your right hamstring. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch sides and repeat.
Benefits: Deeply stretches the hamstring of the front leg; Targets one hamstring at a time; Easy to perform anywhere; No equipment needed; Improves hamstring flexibility for hinging exercises; Reveals left-right tightness
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings (front leg); Gastrocnemius (front leg); Erector spinae

Description: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Brace your core lightly. Keep a soft bend in the knees if needed. Hinge at the hips to fold the torso forward. Reach your hands down toward the toes. Allow the head to hang relaxed. Feel the stretch through the hamstrings and back. Hold then slowly roll back up.
Benefits: Stretches the hamstrings; Releases lower back tension; No equipment needed; Easy basic stretch; Useful warm-up move; Strong fundamental stretch
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings; Spinal erectors; Calves

Description: Sit on the floor with both legs extended in front of you. Bend your right knee and gently place your right foot on top of your left thigh, sole facing up. Bend your left knee and place your left foot on top of your right thigh. Both knees should rest on the floor. Sit up tall with chest lifted. Place your hands on your knees with palms facing up or in a mudra position. Sit with a long spine and relaxed shoulders. Hold for as long as comfortable — start with 1 minute, build up gradually. If you cannot achieve full lotus, use Half Lotus or Easy Pose instead. Never force this pose.
Benefits: Most stable seated meditation position; Develops extreme hip external rotation flexibility; Calming and grounding for meditation; Improves posture and spinal alignment; Traditional yoga seated pose; No equipment needed
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hip external rotators; Adductors; Knees and ankles (mobility demand); Erector spinae (postural)

Description: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Arms at your sides for balance, or extended forward. Brace your core gently. Swing your right leg forward and up, kicking it as high as your flexibility allows. Keep the leg straight. Lower your right leg under control. Immediately swing your left leg up the same way. Continue alternating legs in a steady rhythm. Stay tall through your torso — do not lean back. Perform 8 to 15 kicks per leg as a warm-up.
Benefits: Dynamically stretches the hamstrings; Activates the hip flexors and quads; Excellent dynamic warm-up; Builds coordination and balance; No equipment needed; Increases hamstring mobility over time
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings (stretched); Hip flexors (kicking leg); Quadriceps; Calves (standing leg); Core (stabilizer)

Description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out. Squat down as deep as possible — hips below knees. Keep heels on the floor. Widen stance or angle toes more if heels rise. Hold the deep position. Arms forward for counterbalance. Breathe deeply and relax into the position. Hold for 30 to 120 seconds. Use a support (pole, rack) if you cannot hold unsupported. Practice daily for best mobility gains.
Benefits: Develops deep squat mobility; Improves hip, ankle, and thoracic flexibility; Foundational human movement pattern; No equipment needed; Daily practice yields best results; Reveals and addresses mobility limitations
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hip flexors and adductors (stretched); Calves and ankles (dorsiflexion); Quadriceps (isometric); Erector spinae

Description: Stand with feet slightly wider than hip-width, toes turned out 30 to 45 degrees. Squat down as low as possible. Keep your heels flat on the floor if you can. Bring your hands together at your heart in prayer position. Place your elbows against your inner knees. Press your elbows out against your knees, gently spreading them open. Sit up tall through your spine. Lift your chest. If your heels lift, place a folded blanket or yoga block under them. Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply into your belly. To exit, place your hands on the floor and slowly straighten your legs.
Benefits: Deeply opens the hips, groin, and ankles; Strengthens the legs and core; Improves squat mobility; Relieves lower-back tension; Aids digestion through compression; Foundational deep-squat position
Muscles Worked (Raw): Adductors (stretched); Hip flexors (deep position); Quadriceps (isometric); Calves and soleus (stretched); Erector spinae

Description: Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width. Point the toes slightly out. Squat down as deep as possible with feet flat. Bring your hands together in front of your chest in a prayer position. Press the elbows against the inside of your knees. Use the elbows to push the knees wider apart. Sit tall in the deep squat with the chest up. Hold the pose and breathe deeply then come back up.
Benefits: Deep hip opener; Stretches the adductors; Mobilizes the ankles; Useful for squat depth; No equipment needed; Strong yoga pose
Muscles Worked (Raw): Adductors; Hip flexors; Calves

Description: Sit on the floor with knees bent and feet flat. Hold the back of the thighs and lean back slightly. Lift the feet off the floor with the shins parallel to the floor. Keep the chest tall and the back straight. Release the hands and reach the arms forward parallel to the floor. Brace the core and balance on the hips. Hold the half boat position breathing steadily. Lower the feet to release.
Benefits: Strengthens the deep core and abs.; Improves balance and concentration.; Engages the hip flexors and quads.; No equipment needed.; Builds posture and seated control.; Excellent yoga pose for core endurance.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Hip flexors; Quadriceps; Erector spinae

Description: Lie face down on the floor with legs straight and forearms on the floor. Press up onto the forearms with elbows under shoulders. Bend one knee and bring the heel toward the same side hip. Reach back with the same side hand and grasp the foot. Press the foot gently toward the hip to deepen the stretch. Keep the chest tall and the hips square to the floor. Hold the position breathing steadily. Release the foot slowly and switch sides.
Benefits: Deeply stretches the quadriceps and hip flexors.; Opens the front of the body.; Improves shoulder mobility through the back reach.; Strengthens the back and core.; No equipment needed.; Excellent counter to long sitting.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Quadriceps; Hip flexors; Pectoralis major; Erector spinae

Description: Start in Triangle Pose with right leg forward, left arm reaching up. Bend your right knee slightly. Slide your left hand up your left thigh. Place your right hand on the floor (or a block) about 12 inches in front of and outside your right foot. Shift your weight onto your right leg. Lift your left leg parallel to the floor. Straighten your right leg. Stack your left hip directly over your right hip. Reach your left arm toward the ceiling. Stack your left shoulder over your right. Gaze up at your top hand or straight ahead for balance. Hold for 5 to 8 breaths. To exit, bend the standing knee and release back into Triangle.
Benefits: Builds single-leg balance and ankle stability; Strengthens the standing-leg glute and core; Improves lateral flexibility and hip mobility; Opens the chest and shoulders; Develops focus and body awareness; Intermediate yoga balance pose
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus medius (standing leg); Quadriceps and hamstrings (standing leg); Obliques (lateral stability); Deltoids (extended arm); Ankle stabilizers

Description: Start in a downward dog or table top position. Bring one knee forward toward the wrist of the same side. Set the bent knee on the floor with the shin angled forward. Extend the back leg straight behind with the top of the foot on the floor. Square the hips toward the floor. Lower the torso forward over the front leg. Hold the stretch with steady breath. Walk back to the start. Switch legs and repeat.
Benefits: Deep glute stretch; Stretches the hip flexors; Strong yoga hip opener; Builds hip mobility; Useful cool down move; Easy to do anywhere
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus maximus; Hip flexors; Piriformis

Description: Stand in Mountain Pose at the top of your mat. Inhale. Inhale and sweep your arms overhead into Upward Salute. Exhale and fold forward from the hips into Standing Forward Fold. Inhale and lift your torso halfway, flattening your back. Hands on shins or fingertips on the floor. Exhale and fold forward again into Standing Forward Fold. Inhale and rise up with a flat back, sweeping arms overhead into Upward Salute. Exhale and bring hands together at the heart in Mountain Pose. That is one round. Repeat 5 to 10 rounds, moving with the breath.
Benefits: Warms up the spine and hamstrings without floor work; Excellent for limited mobility or early-morning practice; Links breath to movement; Quick — each round takes 15 to 20 seconds; No equipment needed; Energizing and centering
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae (lengthened); Hamstrings (stretched); Calves (stretched); Deltoids (overhead reach); Core (transitions)

Description: Sit on the floor. Lean back slightly with hands behind you for support. Extend your right leg straight in front of you, lifted a few inches off the floor. Draw circles with your right foot — clockwise for the desired reps, then counterclockwise. Keep the circles controlled and smooth. Your left foot stays flat on the floor for stability. Complete circles in both directions, then switch legs. Keep your core braced throughout. Aim for 8 to 10 circles per direction per leg.
Benefits: Builds hip flexor strength and control; Improves hip mobility; Develops lower ab stability; No equipment needed; Useful warm-up or rehab exercise; Builds hip joint awareness
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hip flexors (iliopsoas); Rectus abdominis (lower); Quadriceps (leg hold); Adductors and abductors (circle); Core (stabilizer)

Description: Seated single-leg hamstring stretch:Sit on the floor with one leg extended in front of you and the other foot tucked against your inner thigh. Hinge at the hips (not the lower back) and reach toward the toes of the extended leg. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then switch sides. Standing hamstring stretch:Place one heel on a low step or curb with the leg straight and toes pointing up. Hinge at the hips and lean your chest toward the extended leg until you feel a stretch along the back of the thigh. Keep your back flat. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds per side. Lying hamstring stretch:Lie on your back and loop a strap or towel around the ball of one foot. Keep the other leg flat on the floor. Straighten the lifted leg toward the ceiling and gently pull it closer using the strap until you feel a stretch. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then switch. For all variations, the stretch should come from a hip hinge, not from rounding your spine. Breathe deeply and ease deeper into the stretch on each exhale. Stretch daily for noticeable flexibility gains within a few weeks. Hamstrings respond well to consistent, frequent stretching.
Benefits: Increases flexibility and range of motion at the hips; Reduces lower-back tension caused by tight hamstrings pulling on the pelvis; Improves squat depth, deadlift setup, and overall lifting mechanics; Reduces injury risk in running, sprinting, and field sports; Helps relieve sciatic-type discomfort when paired with glute and hip stretches
Muscles Worked (Raw): Semitendinosus; Semimembranosus; Biceps femoris (long and short heads); Gastrocnemius (when the foot is dorsiflexed)

Description: Stand tall with feet shoulder width apart. Clasp both hands together and reach them up overhead. Inhale and reach tall through the clasped hands. Begin to circle the hands to one side and down toward the toes. Hinge at the hips with a flat back as the hands lower. Touch the toes or shins at the bottom of the bend. Continue the circular path back up the other side and overhead. Repeat the circular flow for the full set.
Benefits: Stretches the hamstrings and lower back.; Opens the shoulders through the overhead clasp.; Improves spinal mobility through the circular flow.; Acts as a dynamic warm up.; No equipment needed.; Loosens up the entire posterior chain.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings; Erector spinae; Latissimus dorsi; Obliques

Exercise Name: Hands Reversed Clasped Circular Toe Touch
Description: Stand tall with the feet shoulder width apart. Clasp the hands behind the back with palms facing up. Brace the core and keep the chest up. Hinge forward at the hips into a forward fold. Reach the clasped hands overhead and toward the floor. Circle the torso slowly to one side. Continue circling around through the fold. Return to the start and reverse direction.
Benefits: Stretches the hamstrings.; Mobilizes the spine.; Opens the chest and shoulders.; Improves circulation through the trunk.; Useful warm-up or cool-down.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings; Erector spinae; Pectoralis major; Anterior deltoid

Description: Stand tall with feet hip width apart. Inhale and reach the arms up overhead. Exhale and hinge forward at the hips with a flat back. Lower the torso toward the legs as far as comfortable. Place the hands palms up under the soles of the feet. The toes should rest on the inside of the wrists. Pull gently with the arms to deepen the forward fold. Hold the pose breathing steadily then release.
Benefits: Deeply stretches the hamstrings and calves.; Opens the lower back and spine.; Improves shoulder and arm flexibility.; Calms the nervous system through the inversion.; No equipment needed.; Excellent counter to long sitting.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings; Erector spinae; Calves; Latissimus dorsi

Description: Stand facing a fixed overhead bar. Reach up and grab the bar with both hands shoulder-width apart. Use an overhand or neutral grip, whichever feels comfortable. Step your feet back slightly under the bar. Lean your hips back and let your arms straighten. Allow your shoulders to stretch overhead and your chest to open. Keep your feet planted and arms straight. Hold the position and breathe deeply, then step forward to release.
Benefits: Stretches the lats and shoulders; Opens the chest; Decompresses the spine; Useful after pulling or pressing training; Eases tight upper body
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi; Shoulders; Pectoralis major

Description: Stand on your right leg with your left foot crossed and resting on your right knee. Keep your left ankle on top of your right thigh in a figure-four position. Hold your arms out in front of you for balance. Brace your core and pull your shoulders back. Sit back and squat down on your right leg as far as you can. Allow your torso to lean forward as you descend for balance. Continue down until you feel a deep stretch in your right hip. Drive up through your right heel to stand back up. Switch sides.
Benefits: Builds single-leg balance; Deep hip rotator and adductor stretch; Improves ankle mobility; Develops single-leg strength; Useful mobility drill; No equipment required
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus maximus; Adductors; Quadriceps; Hip flexors; Piriformis

Description: Lie flat on your back. Bend your knees and bring them toward your chest. Reach up and grab the outsides of your feet with your hands. If you cannot reach your feet, hold your shins or use a yoga strap looped around your feet. Open your knees wider than your torso and pull them gently down toward your armpits. Keep your ankles directly above your knees so your shins are vertical. Press your tailbone, sacrum, and lower back firmly into the floor. Relax your shoulders and head onto the floor. Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply into your belly. Gently rock side to side for added massage if desired. Release by letting your feet down and hugging your knees to your chest.
Benefits: Decompresses the lower spine; Deeply opens the hips and stretches the inner thighs; Calming and restorative; Relieves lower-back tension; Gentle enough for daily practice; Often used to end yoga classes for relaxation
Muscles Worked (Raw): Adductors (inner thighs, stretched); Hip flexors (stretched); Erector spinae (decompressed); Gluteus maximus and medius

Description: Stand at the edge of a step or platform. Place the balls of both feet on the step with your heels hanging off the back. Hold a railing or wall for balance. Slowly lower your heels down below the level of the step as far as comfortable. Feel the deep stretch through your calves, Achilles tendons, and plantar fascia. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Press through the balls of your feet to return to neutral. Repeat 2 to 3 times. For single-leg version: stand on one foot at a time for a deeper stretch.
Benefits: Stretches the entire calf complex (gastroc and soleus); Opens the Achilles tendon; Stretches the plantar fascia; Improves ankle dorsiflexion; Critical for runners and lifters with tight calves; Helps prevent plantar fasciitis
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gastrocnemius; Soleus; Achilles tendon; Plantar fascia; Tibialis posterior

Description: Kneel on the floor with knees together and feet hip-width apart, tops of feet on the floor. Sit back between your heels, lowering your hips toward the floor between your feet. If your hips do not reach the floor comfortably, place a yoga block or folded blanket between your heels to sit on. Sit up tall with chest lifted and shoulders relaxed. Place your hands on your thighs, palms down or up. Feel the gentle stretch through your quadriceps, knees, and tops of your ankles. Hold for 30 seconds to several minutes. Breathe deeply. To exit, lean forward onto your hands, then carefully extend one leg at a time.
Benefits: Stretches the quadriceps, knees, and ankles; Encourages tall spinal posture; Traditional meditation and breathing pose; Improves digestion when held after meals; Calming and grounding; No equipment needed (block recommended for tight hips)
Muscles Worked (Raw): Quadriceps (stretched); Ankle flexors (stretched); Hip flexors (slight); Erector spinae (postural)

Description: From Downward Dog or standing, step your right foot forward into a deep lunge. Keep your left leg straight behind you with the heel lifted. Press through the ball of your left foot. Bend your right knee to roughly 90 degrees. Knee directly over ankle. Lift your torso upright. Reach both arms overhead with palms facing each other. Square your hips to face forward. Engage your back leg by lifting your kneecap and pressing through your heel. Brace your core and lift your chest. Gaze forward or up. Hold for 5 to 8 breaths. Breathe deeply. Exit and switch sides.
Benefits: Builds quad and glute strength in the front leg; Stretches the hip flexors of the back leg; Improves balance and stability; Strengthens the calves and ankle stabilizers; Opens the chest and shoulders with arms overhead; Foundational yoga standing pose
Muscles Worked (Raw): Quadriceps (front leg); Gluteus maximus (front leg); Hip flexors (back leg, stretched); Calves (back leg); Deltoids (arms overhead); Core (stabilizer)

Description: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart. Place your hands on your hips. Begin rotating your hips in a large circle to the right — forward, right, back, left, and back to forward. Make the circles as large as your mobility allows. Keep your feet planted and your head and shoulders mostly still — the movement comes from the hips. Perform 8 to 10 circles in one direction. Reverse direction and perform 8 to 10 circles the other way. Move at a moderate, controlled pace — this is a mobility drill, not a workout. Excellent warm-up before lower-body training.
Benefits: Mobilizes the hip joint through full range; Warms up the hip flexors, rotators, and adductors; Improves hip mobility for squats and deadlifts; No equipment needed; Easy to integrate into any warm-up; Improves balance and proprioception
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hip flexors; Gluteus maximus and medius; Adductors; Hip rotators; Quadratus lumborum

Description: Kneel on your right knee with your left foot flat in front in a half-kneeling position. Place your hands on your left knee or hips for stability. Squeeze your right glute hard. This tilts your pelvis posteriorly and protects the lower back. Drive your hips forward by pushing through your right glute and front foot. Feel the deep stretch through the front of your right hip (hip flexor) and quad. Keep your torso upright. Avoid arching your lower back. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch sides and repeat.
Benefits: Opens the hip flexors; Improves hip extension range; Critical for sprinting, deadlifting, and squatting; Counteracts prolonged sitting; No equipment needed; Quick and accessible
Muscles Worked (Raw): Iliopsoas (hip flexor); Rectus femoris; Tensor fasciae latae; Sartorius; Gluteus maximus (engaged for protection)

Description: Sit on a chair or the floor with feet flat. Cross your right ankle over your left knee, just above the kneecap. Flex your right foot to protect the knee. Sit up tall. Place your right hand gently on your right knee. Lean forward from the hips with a flat back until you feel a deep stretch in your right outer hip and glute. Optionally, gently press your right knee down with your hand to deepen the stretch. Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply and relax into the stretch. Switch sides and repeat. The stretch should be felt in the glute, not the knee. If you feel knee pain, ease back.
Benefits: Targets the deep hip external rotators; Relieves outer hip and sciatic tension; Improves hip mobility for squats and lateral movements; Practical for office or daily use; No equipment needed; Calming and restorative
Muscles Worked (Raw): Piriformis; Gemelli (superior and inferior); Obturators (internus and externus); Quadratus femoris; Gluteus maximus and medius

Exercise Name: Hip Flexor Stretch Rear Foot Elevated
Description: Position yourself near a couch, bench, or wall. Kneel facing away from the elevated surface. Place your right foot up on the surface behind you, with your right knee on the floor and the top of your right foot pressing back against the surface. Step your left foot forward into a 90-degree lunge position. Brace your core. Squeeze your right glute hard. Push your hips forward. For more intensity, raise your torso fully upright and reach your arms overhead. For maximum intensity, gently arch your upper back. Feel the deep stretch through your right hip flexor and quad. Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch sides.
Benefits: One of the deepest hip flexor and quad stretches available; Essential for chronically tight hips from sitting; Improves hip extension dramatically; Carries over to squat depth and running performance; Builds glute activation through the back-leg squeeze; Used heavily in mobility-focused training programs
Muscles Worked (Raw): Iliopsoas (hip flexor); Rectus femoris (heavy stretch); Vastus muscles (quadriceps); Tensor fasciae latae; Sartorius

Description: Start in Warrior I: right foot forward, left foot back at a 45-degree angle, hips squared forward, front knee bent at 90 degrees. Clasp your hands together behind your back. Pull your shoulders back and down. Inhale and lift your chest. Exhale and fold your torso forward to the inside of your front leg. Lower your shoulder to the inside of your front knee. Reach your clasped hands up and over your head. Press through the outside edge of your back foot. Keep your front knee tracking over your ankle. Hold for 5 to 8 breaths. Breathe deeply. Inhale to rise back to Warrior I. Release your hands and switch sides. If clasping hands is too difficult, hold a strap between them.
Benefits: Combines lunge depth with chest and shoulder opening; Stretches the shoulders, chest, and back; Builds leg strength through the Warrior position; Stretches the hip flexors of the back leg; Improves shoulder mobility; Calming and grounding
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major (stretched); Anterior deltoid (stretched); Hamstrings (front leg); Hip flexors (back leg); Quadriceps (front leg, isometric); Erector spinae

Exercise Name: Intermediate Hip Flexor and Quad Stretch
Description: Kneel on your right knee with your left foot flat in front (90-degree bend in left knee). Reach back with your right hand and grab the top of your right foot. Gently pull your right foot toward your right glute. You should feel a deep stretch in the front of your right thigh and hip. Squeeze your right glute to enhance the hip flexor stretch. Keep your torso upright. Place your left hand on your left knee for balance. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Release and switch sides. Use a strap if you cannot reach your foot directly.
Benefits: Stretches the hip flexors and rectus femoris simultaneously; More efficient than separate hip flexor and quad stretches; Excellent for tight hips from sitting or running; Improves hip extension for squats, lunges, and running; No equipment needed; Time-efficient combined stretch
Muscles Worked (Raw): Iliopsoas (hip flexor); Rectus femoris (crosses hip and knee); Quadriceps (vastus muscles); Tensor fasciae latae

Description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart. Hands on hips. Push your hips forward. Circle your hips to the right — forward, right, back, left. Continue in smooth circles for 10 to 15 rotations. Reverse direction for 10 to 15 rotations. Make the circles as large as comfortable. Keep your upper body relatively still — hips do the work. Perform as a warm-up before leg training.
Benefits: Mobilizes the hip joint; Warms up hip muscles and tendons; Increases blood flow to the hips; No equipment needed; Quick and accessible; Standard warm-up exercise
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hip flexors; Hip extensors; Hip abductors and adductors; Core (slight)

Description: Lie flat on your back with both legs extended. Bend your right knee and bring it toward your chest. Clasp both hands around your right shin or behind your right thigh. Gently pull your right knee closer to your chest until you feel a comfortable stretch in your right glute and lower back. Keep your left leg flat on the floor (or bend the left knee with foot flat for less intensity). Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply and relax into the stretch. Release and switch to the left knee. For a deeper stretch, pull both knees to your chest simultaneously and rock gently side to side. Perform two to three holds per side.
Benefits: Relieves lower-back tension and tightness; Stretches the glutes and hip extensors; Decompresses the lumbar spine; Gentle enough for daily use and rehabilitation; No equipment needed; Calming and restorative
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus maximus (stretched); Erector spinae (lower back, stretched); Hamstrings (secondary stretch); Hip extensors

Description: Stand tall. Reach your right arm behind your back with the elbow bent. The back of your right hand should rest against your lower back, palm facing outward. With your left hand, reach down and gently pull your right hand higher up your back. Feel the stretch through the back of your right shoulder. For more intensity, hold a small towel between your hands and use it to assist the pull. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch arms and repeat. Stop if you feel any sharp shoulder pain.
Benefits: Stretches the posterior shoulder capsule; Improves internal rotation; Helps prevent shoulder impingement; Useful for overhead athletes; No equipment needed (towel optional); Quick to perform
Muscles Worked (Raw): Posterior shoulder capsule; Infraspinatus; Teres minor; Posterior deltoid

Description: Lie flat on your back with both legs extended. Extend both arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height — body forms a T or cross shape. Bend your right knee and bring it up toward your chest. Use your left hand to gently pull your right knee across your body to the left. Keep your right shoulder pressed into the floor — your hips will rotate but shoulders stay grounded. Look toward your right hand for added neck stretch. Feel the stretch through your right outer hip, lower back, and chest. Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Switch sides and repeat.
Benefits: Stretches the lower back, glutes, and obliques; Combines spinal twist with hip stretch; Calming and restorative; Excellent before sleep or as a cool-down; No equipment needed; One of the most effective spinal twists
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae (lower back); Gluteus medius and maximus; Obliques; Quadratus lumborum; Pectoralis major (stretched); Hip rotators

Description: Start on your hands and knees in tabletop position. Reach your right arm up toward the ceiling, opening your chest to the right. Look up at your right hand. Then reach your right arm down and underneath your left armpit, rotating your torso. Lower your right shoulder and the right side of your head to the floor. Continue alternating: reaching up and over, then down and through. Feel the rotation through your thoracic spine and stretch through your shoulder. Move slowly with breath control. Inhale up, exhale through. Perform 5 to 8 reps per side.
Benefits: Mobilizes the thoracic spine through rotation; Stretches the rear shoulders and rhomboids; Excellent warm-up for upper-body training; Easier on the lower back than standing rotations; No equipment needed; Useful for shoulder mobility too
Muscles Worked (Raw): Thoracic spine rotators; Rhomboids and mid-traps (stretched); Posterior deltoid (stretched); Obliques; Latissimus dorsi

Description: Stand with your feet together and knees slightly bent. Place both hands on your knees. Lean forward slightly so your weight is on your hands. Brace your core for stability. Slowly draw circles with both knees together. Move in one direction for a comfortable number of reps. Reverse and circle in the other direction. Keep the movement slow and controlled.
Benefits: Warms up the knees and hips; Improves joint mobility; Useful before lower body training; Loosens stiff knees; Gentle on the body
Muscles Worked (Raw): Knees; Hips; Quadriceps

Description: Kneel on the floor facing a bench, chair, or elevated surface. Place both hands on the surface behind you (or clasp them behind your back). Keep your knees under your hips. Sit upright initially. Lean forward while keeping your arms extended behind you. Your chest should open up. Feel the deep stretch across your chest and front shoulders. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply into the stretch. Return to the starting position slowly. Repeat two to three times.
Benefits: Deeply stretches the pectoralis major and anterior deltoid; Kneeling position provides a stable base; Counteracts forward-hunched posture; Improves shoulder flexibility for pressing exercises; No equipment needed (elevated surface optional); Gentle enough for daily practice
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major (stretched); Anterior deltoid (stretched); Biceps brachii (stretched); Serratus anterior (stretched)

Description: Set up on hands and knees in a quadruped position. Place the hands under the shoulders and knees under the hips. Brace your core and keep the back flat. Lift one knee out to the side. Circle the knee forward toward the hand. Continue the circle back to the start position. Maintain a steady tempo. Finish all reps then switch sides.
Benefits: Mobilizes the hips; Strong warm-up drill; Useful before training; Builds hip range; Activates the glutes
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hip Flexors; Gluteus medius; Gluteus maximus

Description: Kneel on your right knee on a pad or soft surface. Place your left foot flat on the floor in front, with the left knee bent at roughly 90 degrees. Keep your torso upright. Place your hands on your left knee or on your hips. Squeeze your right glute — this tilts the pelvis posteriorly and intensifies the stretch. Gently push your hips forward while maintaining the upright torso and the glute squeeze. Feel the stretch in the front of your right hip (hip flexor area) and upper right thigh. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply and relax into the stretch. Switch sides and repeat. For a deeper stretch, raise the arm on the kneeling side overhead and lean slightly away.
Benefits: Directly stretches the iliopsoas and rectus femoris; Counteracts the effects of prolonged sitting; Improves hip extension for squats, lunges, and running; Relieves lower-back tension caused by tight hip flexors; No equipment needed (pad optional); One of the most important stretches for desk workers
Muscles Worked (Raw): Iliopsoas (hip flexor); Rectus femoris (quad, crosses the hip); Tensor fasciae latae; Sartorius

Description: Kneel on the floor in front of a flat bench (or coffee table). Hips directly above knees. Place your forearms on the bench with palms facing each other or up. Elbows roughly shoulder-width apart. Walk your knees back so your forearms remain on the bench but your hips move further from the bench. Lower your chest and head down between your arms toward the floor. Press your hips back toward your heels. Keep your back flat — do not round it. Feel the deep stretch through your lats, shoulders, and upper back. Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply and let gravity deepen the stretch. To exit, walk your knees forward and rise.
Benefits: Deeply stretches the lats, shoulders, and upper back; Improves overhead mobility for pressing; Counteracts hunched posture; Decompresses the spine; Useful warm-up for overhead pressing or pull-ups; Easy to set up
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi (deep stretch); Teres major; Pectoralis major (stretched); Triceps brachii (stretched); Erector spinae

Description: Kneel on the floor with one knee down and the other foot in front. Place a pad under the back knee for comfort. Position the front foot directly under the front knee. Tuck your pelvis slightly to lengthen the lower back. Squeeze the back glute to deepen the stretch. Press your hips gently forward until you feel a stretch in the front of the back hip. Hold the position and breathe deeply. Slowly come out of the stretch and switch sides.
Benefits: Opens tight hip flexors; Relieves hip stiffness from sitting; Improves hip mobility; Useful for runners and lifters; Lengthens the iliopsoas and quads
Muscles Worked (Raw): Iliopsoas; Hip flexors; Quadriceps

Description: Kneel on the floor in front of a flat bench. Hips above knees. Place both forearms on the bench with palms facing each other. Elbows shoulder-width apart. Walk your knees back so your hips move further from the bench but your forearms stay on it. Lower your chest and head down between your arms toward the floor. Press your hips back toward your heels. Keep your back flat — do not round it. Feel the deep stretch through your lats, shoulders, and upper back. Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply and let gravity deepen the stretch. To exit, walk your knees forward and rise.
Benefits: Deep lat and shoulder stretch with bench support; Improves overhead mobility; Decompresses the spine; Counteracts hunched posture; Excellent warm-up before pull-ups or pressing; Easy to set up
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi (deep stretch); Teres major; Pectoralis major (stretched); Triceps brachii (stretched); Erector spinae

Description: Kneel on your right knee. Left foot forward, knee at 90 degrees. Keep your torso upright. Push your hips forward until you feel a stretch in the front of your right hip. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. You can raise your right arm overhead to increase the stretch. Switch sides. Breathe deeply into the stretch. Perform 2 to 3 holds per side.
Benefits: Essential hip flexor stretch for desk workers; Opens tight hip flexors from sitting; Improves hip extension range; Reduces lower back pain risk; No equipment needed; One of the most important daily stretches
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hip flexors (iliopsoas); Rectus femoris; Quadriceps (slight stretch)

Description: Set up on hands and knees in a quadruped position. Place the hands under the shoulders and knees under the hips. Brace your core and keep the back flat. Lift one leg straight back behind you. Sweep the leg in a half circle out to the side. Continue the sweep to the front of the body. Reverse the path back to the start. Finish all reps then switch sides.
Benefits: Mobilizes the hips; Strong warm-up drill; Useful before training; Builds hip range; Activates the glutes
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hip Flexors; Gluteus medius; Gluteus maximus

Description: Kneel on the floor and sit your hips back onto your heels. Place your hands on your thighs. Sit up tall through the spine. Slowly tilt your head to one side, bringing the ear toward the shoulder. Avoid forcing the stretch or shrugging the shoulder. Hold for a comfortable duration. Return to center and tilt to the other side. Continue alternating sides.
Benefits: Relieves neck tension; Stretches the upper traps; Useful for desk workers; Stable kneeling base; Easy and gentle on the body
Muscles Worked (Raw): Neck; Traps; Sternocleidomastoid

Exercise Name: Kneeling One Arm Reach Roll Lift
Description: Set up on hands and knees on the floor. Brace the core and keep the back flat. Reach one arm forward along the floor. Roll the wrist so the palm faces up. Lift the arm off the floor and rotate it open. Reach the arm up and back to open the chest. Pause briefly at the top of the rotation. Reverse the motion and continue for all reps then switch.
Benefits: Mobilizes the shoulder.; Trains scapular control.; Opens the chest.; Useful warm-up.; Improves rotational mobility.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Anterior deltoid; Trapezius; Rhomboids; Serratus anterior

Exercise Name: Kneeling Push Up to Child Pose
Description: Begin in a kneeling push up position with hands under the shoulders. Set the body in a straight line from head to knees. Brace your core and keep the back flat. Lower the chest toward the floor. Press back up to lockout. Sit the hips back onto the heels. Stretch the arms forward into child pose. Hold briefly then return to the start position.
Benefits: Trains the chest; Stretches the back; Strong flow move; Useful warm-up; Builds shoulder mobility; Combines push and stretch
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Triceps brachii; Latissimus dorsi

Description: Kneel on the floor with one knee down and the other leg out to the side. Place a pad under the kneeling leg for comfort. Extend the side leg straight out with toes pointed forward. Place your hands on the floor or your front knee for support. Sit your hips back slightly to feel a stretch in the inner thigh and hip. Keep the side leg straight as you sink deeper. Hold the position and breathe deeply. Slowly come out of the stretch and switch sides.
Benefits: Stretches the sartorius muscle; Opens the inner thigh and hip; Useful for runners; Improves hip mobility; Relieves tight hip flexors
Muscles Worked (Raw): Sartorius; Hip flexors; Adductors

Description: Kneel on the floor on hands and knees. Place your palms flat on the floor. Rotate your hands so your fingers point back toward your knees. Palms still flat. Slowly lean back, shifting your hips toward your heels. Feel the stretch through your wrist flexors and forearms. Adjust how far back you lean to control the intensity. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Slowly return forward to release. Repeat two to three times. Use a pad under your knees if needed.
Benefits: Deeply stretches the wrist flexors and forearms; Essential for grip-intensive training; Helps prevent wrist and forearm overuse injuries; Useful for desk workers with tight wrists; No equipment needed; Adjustable depth via lean angle
Muscles Worked (Raw): Wrist flexors (flexor carpi radialis, flexor carpi ulnaris); Palmaris longus; Forearm flexors

Description: Start on hands and knees with hands under shoulders. Extend one leg straight out to the side. Keep the foot flat on the floor and toes pointing forward. Brace your core and keep the back flat. Sit the hips back toward the heel of the bent leg. Feel the stretch in the inner thigh of the extended leg. Hold the stretch with steady breath. Return to the start. Switch sides and repeat.
Benefits: Strong adductor stretch; Stretches the hip flexors; No equipment needed; Useful warm-up move; Builds hip mobility; Strong cool down stretch
Muscles Worked (Raw): Adductors; Hip flexors; Gluteus medius

Description: Lie on your back next to a doorframe or wall corner with your right hip aligned to the wall edge. Extend your right leg straight up the wall or doorframe. Your leg should be vertical. Keep your left leg extended through the doorway or along the floor. Press your right heel into the wall to engage the leg slightly. Adjust your distance from the wall to control the stretch intensity. Hold for 30 seconds to 2 minutes. Breathe deeply and let gravity deepen the stretch. Switch sides and repeat. Alternative: lie on the floor and use a strap looped around your foot to hold the leg up.
Benefits: Passive hamstring stretch — gentle and effective; Allows long holds without active effort; Adjustable depth based on distance from wall; Excellent for tight hamstrings; Calming and restorative; Works at home with just a wall
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings (primary); Calves (secondary); Lower back (gentle decompression)

Exercise Name: Legs Up the Wall Yoga Pose
Description: Sit on the floor next to a wall with one hip touching it. Roll onto the back while swinging the legs up the wall. Set the hips as close to the wall as comfortable. Allow the legs to rest vertical against the wall. Place the arms at the sides palms up. Close the eyes and relax the body. Breathe slowly and deeply. Hold the pose for the desired duration.
Benefits: Decompresses the lower back.; Drains fluid from the legs.; Stretches the hamstrings gently.; Calms the nervous system.; Useful for recovery.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings; Erector spinae; Calves

Description: Start in a low lunge with right foot forward and left knee on the floor. Walk your right foot to the outside of your right hand so both hands are on the inside of your right foot. Lower your forearms to the floor (or onto a block). Your right knee bends naturally to the outside. Press your hips down and forward. Feel the deep stretch in your left hip flexor and right inner thigh. Keep your back leg active — press the top of your back foot into the floor. Lengthen through the crown of your head. Relax your face. Hold for 30 to 90 seconds. Breathe deeply. To exit, press back into a hands-and-knees position. Switch sides.
Benefits: Deeply opens the hip flexors, hamstrings, and groin; Improves hip mobility for squats and lunges; Stretches the calves and ankles; Relieves lower-back tension; Calming despite the intensity; Used by athletes and physical therapists
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hip flexors (back leg, stretched); Hamstrings (front leg, stretched); Adductors (front leg); Quadriceps (back leg); Calves and ankles (back leg)

Description: Kneel on a soft mat with the hips down on the heels. Place one hand behind the head with the elbow flared. Place the other hand on the floor in front. Brace your core and keep the hips square. Rotate the upper back to bring the elbow toward the ceiling. Open the chest and follow the elbow with the eyes. Reverse the rotation to bring the elbow toward the opposite hand. Finish all reps then switch sides.
Benefits: Improves T spine mobility; Strong upper back drill; Useful warm-up; Builds thoracic rotation; Useful for posture
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae; Latissimus dorsi; Posterior deltoid

Description: Sit on the floor with legs extended. Bend your right knee. Use your hands to lift your right foot and place it high on your left thigh, with the sole facing up. Bend your left knee and lift your left foot to place it high on your right thigh. Both knees should rest on the floor. Sit up tall. Place your hands on your knees with palms up or down. Lengthen through your spine. Relax your shoulders. Hold for 1 to 5 minutes (or longer for meditation). Breathe deeply. Switch which leg is on top regularly to balance hip mobility.
Benefits: Classic meditation posture used for thousands of years; Calms the nervous system; Develops deep hip external rotation; Promotes upright posture; No equipment needed; Symbol of yoga and meditation practice
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hip external rotators (stretched); Adductors (stretched); Quadriceps (stretched); Erector spinae (engaged for upright posture)

Description: Sit on the floor with legs extended. Bend one leg and pull the foot up onto the opposite thigh. Set the foot with the sole facing up near the hip. Bend the other leg and lift the foot up onto the opposite thigh. Set the second foot with the sole facing up near the hip. Sit tall through the spine. Rest the hands on the knees with palms up. Hold the pose with steady breath. Release with control.
Benefits: Deep hip stretch; Strong meditation pose; Builds hip mobility; Stretches the glutes; Useful for meditation; Strong yoga pose
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hip flexors; Gluteus maximus; Adductors

Description: Sit on the floor with the legs extended forward. Bend one leg and place the foot on the opposite thigh. Bend the other leg and place that foot on the opposite thigh. Sit tall with the back upright. Rest the hands on the knees palms up. Close your eyes and breathe deeply. Allow the hips to settle and open with each breath. Hold the pose then carefully release the legs.
Benefits: Deep hip opener; Trains breath control; Calming meditation pose; No equipment needed; Useful yoga pose; Strong yoga finisher
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hip flexors; Adductors; Gluteus maximus

Exercise Name: Low Lunge Yoga Pose Anjaneyasana I
Description: Step one foot forward into a lunge stance. Lower the back knee to the floor. Set the front shin near vertical. Brace your core and keep the chest up. Press the hips forward to deepen the stretch. Reach the arms straight up overhead. Look up toward the hands. Hold the pose then switch sides.
Benefits: Opens the hip flexors; Stretches the quads; Strong yoga pose; Useful warm-up; Builds hip mobility
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hip Flexors; Quadriceps; Psoas

Description: From Downward Dog or a standing position, step your right foot forward between your hands. Lower your left knee to the floor. Pad your knee with a folded towel if needed. Slide your left knee back until you feel a comfortable stretch in your left hip. Sink your hips down and forward. Keep your right knee directly over your right ankle. Lift your torso upright. Reach both arms overhead with palms facing each other. Square your hips to face forward. Squeeze your left glute to deepen the stretch. Hold for 5 to 10 breaths. Breathe deeply. Exit and switch sides.
Benefits: Deeply stretches the hip flexors and quadriceps; Opens the front of the hip and groin; Strengthens the front leg isometrically; Improves hip mobility for squats and deadlifts; Counteracts the effects of prolonged sitting; Foundational yoga pose
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hip flexors (back leg, deeply stretched); Quadriceps (back leg, stretched); Quadriceps and glutes (front leg, isometric); Psoas major

Description: Stand tall. Step your right foot forward into a long lunge stance, three to four feet of separation. Lower your back (left) knee toward the floor. Keep your front (right) knee bent at roughly 90 degrees. Place your hands on your front knee or on the floor on either side of the front foot. Press your hips forward and down. Squeeze your back glute to deepen the stretch. Lift your chest. Keep your torso upright. Feel the stretch in your back hip flexor and front hamstring. Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch sides and repeat.
Benefits: Opens the hip flexors of the back leg; Stretches the hamstrings of the front leg; Improves hip extension for squats and running; Counteracts the effects of prolonged sitting; Foundational mobility exercise; No equipment needed
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hip flexors (back leg, stretched); Hamstrings (front leg, stretched); Adductors; Quadriceps (back leg, mild stretch)

Description: Lie flat on your back with both legs extended. Lift your right leg straight up. Cross it over your body to the left. Use your left hand to pull your right leg further across, gently increasing the stretch. Try to keep your right shoulder pressed into the floor — your hips will rotate but your shoulders should stay grounded. Feel the stretch through your right outer hip, IT band, and lower back. Extend your right arm out to the right for a deeper torso twist. Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch sides and repeat.
Benefits: Stretches the outer hip and IT band; Stretches the gluteus medius; Combines hip and spinal twist mobility; Calming and restorative; Excellent for runners and cyclists; No equipment needed
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus medius and minimus; Tensor fasciae latae; IT band; Quadratus lumborum; Erector spinae

Description: Lie on your back. Arms at your sides or gripping behind your head for support. Raise both legs a few inches off the floor. Draw a large clockwise circle with your legs — right, up, left, down. Keep legs together and straight throughout. Complete circles clockwise, then reverse counterclockwise. Maintain lower back contact with the floor. Aim for 5 to 8 circles per direction. The larger the circle, the harder the exercise.
Benefits: Loads the core from every angle through the circle; Targets lower abs, obliques, and hip flexors; No equipment needed; Engaging and challenging; Builds core endurance; Develops body control
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Obliques; Hip flexors; Transverse abdominis

Description: Lie flat on your back with both legs extended. Loop a towel or yoga strap around the ball of your right foot. Hold both ends with your hands. Lift your right leg straight up toward the ceiling. Pull the towel gently toward your chest, dorsiflexing your foot (toes toward your shin). Keep your right knee straight throughout. Feel the stretch through your right calf — gastrocnemius primarily. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch to the left foot and repeat.
Benefits: Deeply stretches the gastrocnemius and soleus; Comfortable supine position allows full relaxation; Towel provides controlled depth; Easier on the body than standing calf stretches; Improves ankle dorsiflexion; Excellent post-workout calf stretch
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gastrocnemius; Soleus; Achilles tendon; Plantar fascia (secondary); Hamstrings (secondary)

Description: Lie on your back on a firm surface. No pillow. Look at the ceiling. Tuck your chin — press the back of your head into the floor. You should feel a gentle stretch at the base of your skull. Hold for 5 to 10 seconds. Relax. Repeat 10 to 15 times. The floor provides feedback — you can feel the retraction. Easiest chin tuck variation.
Benefits: Easiest chin tuck variation; Floor provides tactile feedback; Gravity assists the retraction; Useful for rehabilitation; No equipment needed; Builds deep cervical flexor awareness
Muscles Worked (Raw): Deep cervical flexors; Suboccipitals (stretched)

Description: Lie flat on your back with both arms extended out to the sides, palms facing the ceiling. Bend your right knee and lift your right leg up. Cross your right leg over your body to the left side, letting it fall toward the floor. Use your left hand to gently press your right knee toward the floor for a deeper stretch. Try to keep your right shoulder pressed into the floor — your hips will rotate but your shoulders should stay grounded. Turn your head to the right to deepen the spinal twist. Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch sides and repeat.
Benefits: Mobilizes the thoracic and lumbar spine; Stretches the outer hip and IT band; Calming and restorative; No equipment needed; Excellent before sleep or as a cool-down; Relieves lower-back tension
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae; Quadratus lumborum; Gluteus medius and maximus; Tensor fasciae latae; Obliques

Description: Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Cross your right ankle over your left knee, resting it just above the kneecap. Flex your right foot. Reach both hands through the gap between your legs and clasp them behind your left thigh (or on top of your left shin). Gently pull your left thigh toward your chest. As you pull, your right knee will naturally open outward. Feel the deep stretch in your right glute and outer hip. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply and relax into the stretch. Release and switch sides. Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor throughout.
Benefits: Deeply stretches the piriformis and glutes; Comfortable supine position allows relaxation; Relieves sciatic tension; Improves hip external rotation; No equipment needed; Gentle enough for daily use
Muscles Worked (Raw): Piriformis; Gluteus maximus; Deep hip external rotators; Gluteus medius

Description: Lie flat on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Extend both arms out to your sides at shoulder height in a T-shape. Slowly lower both knees together to the right side, letting them rest on the floor. Keep both shoulders pressed flat to the floor — your hips will rotate but your shoulders should stay grounded. Turn your head to the left for a deeper twist (optional). Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply. Slowly bring your knees back to center, then drop to the left side. Repeat 2 to 3 times per side.
Benefits: Mobilizes the spine through rotation; Stretches the obliques and lower back; Decompresses the spine; Calming and restorative; No equipment needed; Excellent before sleep
Muscles Worked (Raw): Obliques; Quadratus lumborum; Erector spinae; Gluteus medius; IT band (slight)

Description: Lie flat on your back with both legs extended on the floor. Bend your right knee and bring it toward your chest. Wrap both hands around your right shin or behind your right thigh. Gently pull your knee closer to your chest until you feel a comfortable stretch. Keep your left leg flat on the floor (or bend the left knee with foot flat for less intensity). Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply and relax. Release and switch to the left knee. For both knees together: pull both toward your chest simultaneously and rock gently side to side.
Benefits: Relieves lower-back tension; Stretches the glutes and hip extensors; Calming and restorative; Gentle enough for daily use and rehabilitation; No equipment needed; Useful before bed for back relaxation
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus maximus (stretched); Erector spinae (stretched); Hamstrings (secondary); Hip extensors

Exercise Name: Lying Leg Tuck Hip Back Stretch
Description: Lie on the back with the legs extended. Bend one knee and bring it toward the chest. Wrap both hands around the shin or thigh. Brace the core and keep the other leg flat on the floor. Pull the knee deeper into the chest. Feel the stretch in the glute and lower back. Hold the stretch for the desired duration. Release and repeat on the other side.
Benefits: Stretches the glute and lower back.; Decompresses the lumbar spine.; Useful for hip mobility.; Joint friendly stretch.; Improves recovery.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus maximus; Erector spinae; Hip flexors

Description: Lie face up on a bench with your hips positioned at the very edge. Pull your left knee toward your chest. Hold it with both hands. Allow your right leg to hang off the bench. Let gravity pull it down. Feel the stretch in the front of your right hip. Hold the position for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply and relax into the stretch. Switch legs and repeat the stretch. Perform 2 to 3 rounds per side.
Benefits: Passive hip flexor stretch — gentle and effective; Allows long holds without active effort; Gravity deepens the stretch over time; Improves hip extension for squats and running; Counteracts the effects of prolonged sitting; Excellent post-workout stretch
Muscles Worked (Raw): Iliopsoas (hip flexor); Rectus femoris (slight); Tensor fasciae latae; Sartorius

Description: Lie on your back near the edge of a bench with your right hip just at the edge. Pull your left knee toward your chest. Hold it with both hands. Let your right leg drop off the side of the bench, allowing gravity to lower it. Allow the right thigh to drop below the level of the bench. Feel the deep stretch through your right hip flexor. Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply and let gravity deepen the stretch. Switch sides and repeat. Use a sturdy bench or table that allows the leg to drop fully.
Benefits: Passive hip flexor stretch — gentle and effective; Allows long holds without active effort; Gravity deepens the stretch over time; Improves hip extension for squats and running; Counteracts prolonged sitting; Excellent post-workout stretch
Muscles Worked (Raw): Iliopsoas (hip flexor); Rectus femoris (slight); Tensor fasciae latae; Sartorius

Exercise Name: Lying Leg Tuck Hip Twist Stretch
Description: Lie on the back with the legs extended. Bend one knee and bring it toward the chest. Brace the core and keep the shoulders flat. Guide the bent knee across the body to the opposite side. Press the knee gently toward the floor. Reach the same side arm out to the side. Feel the stretch through the lower back and obliques. Hold for the desired duration then switch sides.
Benefits: Mobilizes the spine.; Stretches the glutes and obliques.; Decompresses the lower back.; Useful for hip mobility.; Improves recovery.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae; Obliques; Gluteus maximus

Exercise Name: Lying Leg Tuck Hip Twist to Left Stretch
Description: Lie on the back with the legs extended. Bend the right knee and bring it toward the chest. Brace the core and keep the shoulders flat. Guide the right knee across the body to the left. Press the knee gently toward the floor on the left side. Reach the right arm out to the side. Turn the head to the right. Hold for the desired duration then switch sides.
Benefits: Mobilizes the spine.; Stretches the obliques.; Opens the glute.; Decompresses the lower back.; Useful for recovery.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae; Obliques; Gluteus maximus

Description: Lie flat on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Bring both knees toward your chest. Wrap your arms around your shins. Gently pull your knees closer to your chest. Feel the stretch through your lower back. Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. For variation, gently rock side to side to massage the lower back. Release slowly. Lower one foot at a time back to the floor. Repeat two to three times.
Benefits: Decompresses the lumbar spine; Stretches the lower back and glutes; Relieves back tension and tightness; Gentle enough for daily use and rehabilitation; No equipment needed; Calming and restorative
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae (lower back); Gluteus maximus; Quadratus lumborum; Hip extensors

Description: Lie on the back with the knees bent and feet flat. Place the hands at the sides palms down. Brace your core and keep the shoulders relaxed. Lift the head slightly off the floor. Tilt the chin gently to one side. Hold the position briefly to activate the scalenes. Lower the head with control. Repeat to the other side.
Benefits: Trains the neck; Useful for neck health; Strong activation drill; Builds neck mobility; Useful for posture
Muscles Worked (Raw): Sternocleidomastoid; Trapezius; Levator scapulae

Description: Lie flat on your back on the floor. Extend the arms straight out to the sides on the floor. Set the palms facing up. Brace your core lightly. Sweep both arms along the floor up overhead. Reach the hands together overhead. Sweep the arms back down to the sides along the floor. Continue the smooth sweeping motion.
Benefits: Mobilizes the shoulders; Opens the chest; Useful warm-up drill; No equipment needed; Easy mobility move; Strong shoulder opener
Muscles Worked (Raw): Anterior deltoid; Pectoralis major; Latissimus dorsi

Description: Lie flat on your back. Extend both legs straight along the floor. Lift your right leg straight up toward the ceiling. Point your toes. Press your lower back into the floor. Brace your core hard. Trace small, controlled circles in the air with your right leg. Keep the rest of your body still. Perform 5 to 8 circles in one direction, then reverse for 5 to 8 circles. The non-working leg stays pressed flat on the floor throughout. Switch to the left leg and repeat. Start with small circles. Increase the size only if you can keep your hips and lower back stable.
Benefits: Improves hip mobility through full circular range; Builds core stability against limb movement; Foundational Pilates mat exercise; Trains hip dissociation from the lower back; No equipment needed; Excellent rehabilitation exercise
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hip flexors and extensors; Hip rotators (internal and external); Adductors and abductors; Rectus abdominis (anti-rotation); Transverse abdominis

Exercise Name: Lying Leg Tuck Hip Stretch with Overhead Hands
Description: Lie on the back with the legs extended. Bend one knee and bring it toward the chest. Hold the shin with the same side hand. Reach the opposite arm overhead along the floor. Brace the core and keep the shoulders flat. Pull the knee deep into the chest. Feel the stretch through the side body and glute. Hold for the desired duration then switch sides.
Benefits: Stretches the glute.; Lengthens the side body.; Decompresses the lumbar spine.; Useful for hip mobility.; Joint friendly stretch.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus maximus; Latissimus dorsi; Erector spinae

Description: Lie on your side with the knees stacked and bent at ninety degrees. Stretch both arms out in front of you in a stack. Brace the core and keep the knees pinned together.
