Rotate the top arm up and across the body to the other side. Follow the moving hand with your eyes. Open the chest as the arm reaches the floor on the opposite side. Pause briefly and feel the stretch through the upper back. Return to the start and repeat for all reps then switch sides.
Benefits: Improves thoracic spine rotational mobility.; Opens the chest and shoulders.; Reduces upper back stiffness.; Carryover to better squat and overhead positions.; Excellent warm up before lifting.; No equipment needed.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi; Pectoralis major; Posterior deltoid; Erector spinae

Description: Lie on the back with the legs together and bent. Drop the knees over to one side. Place the arms out to the sides palms up. Brace your core and keep the shoulders down. Rotate the upper torso to the opposite side of the knees. Try to keep both shoulders on the floor. Hold the stretch briefly. Switch the legs to the other side and repeat.
Benefits: Mobilizes the T spine; Stretches the obliques; Strong mobility drill; Useful warm-up; Builds spinal range
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae; Obliques; Latissimus dorsi

Description: Sit comfortably in a chair or cross-legged on the floor. Sit up tall with a straight spine. Rest your hands on your thighs or in your lap. Close your eyes or soften your gaze. Begin breathing naturally through your nose. Do not try to control the breath — just observe it. Notice the sensation of breath entering and leaving your nostrils. Notice the rise and fall of your belly with each breath. When your mind wanders to thoughts, gently bring your attention back to the breath. This is the practice — not to avoid thoughts but to return to the breath. Continue for 5 to 20 minutes. To end, take three deeper breaths, slowly open your eyes, and notice how you feel.
Benefits: Reduces stress and anxiety; Calms the nervous system; Improves focus and concentration; Enhances recovery between training; Improves sleep quality; No equipment needed
Muscles Worked (Raw): Diaphragm; Intercostal muscles; Deep core (transverse abdominis); Pelvic floor

Description: Stand tall in mountain pose with feet hip-width apart. Pull your shoulders down and back, chest open. Bring your palms together in front of your heart in a prayer position. Press the bases of the palms together firmly. Pull the elbows out to the sides at heart level. Press the fingertips up toward the ceiling. Hold the pose with steady deep breathing. Maintain a tall spine and relaxed shoulders throughout the hold.
Benefits: Centering and grounding pose; Stretches the wrists and forearms; Opens the chest; Improves posture; Calms the mind through breath focus; Foundation for many yoga sequences
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Wrist flexors; Trapezius

Description: Stand with your feet together (or hip-width apart for more stability). Distribute your weight evenly across both feet. Ground through the four corners of each foot: big toe, little toe, inner heel, outer heel. Straighten your legs without locking your knees. Engage your quadriceps gently. Tuck your tailbone slightly. Draw your lower belly in. Lift your chest. Roll your shoulders back and down, away from your ears. Let your arms hang naturally with palms facing forward. Lengthen through the crown of your head. Tuck your chin slightly so the back of your neck is long. Gaze straight ahead with soft eyes. Breathe deeply and evenly. Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Feel the alignment of your entire body.
Benefits: Teaches foundational postural alignment; Builds body awareness and proprioception; Improves posture for daily life; Starting position for all standing yoga poses; Calming and grounding; Strengthens the feet, ankles, and legs isometrically
Muscles Worked (Raw): Quadriceps (isometric engagement); Core (transverse abdominis, gentle engagement); Erector spinae (postural alignment); Feet and ankle stabilizers; Gluteus medius (balance)

Description: Sit or stand tall with shoulders pulled back and down. Slowly drop your chin toward your chest. Begin to slowly roll your head in a clockwise circle: chin to right shoulder, then back of head behind, then to left shoulder, and back to chin down. Make the circle as large and slow as comfortable. Each circle should take 5 to 8 seconds. Complete 3 to 5 circles in the clockwise direction. Reverse and complete 3 to 5 circles counter-clockwise. Stop immediately if you feel any pinching or sharp pain. Move slowly throughout. Never force the rotation.
Benefits: Mobilizes the cervical spine in all directions; Stretches neck muscles in 360 degrees; Quick and accessible; Useful for desk workers; No equipment needed; Easy warm-up for upper body training
Muscles Worked (Raw): Sternocleidomastoid; Upper trapezius; Levator scapulae; Splenius capitis and cervicis; Scalenes; Suboccipitals

Description: Sit or stand tall with shoulders pulled back and down. Slowly tilt your head backward, looking up toward the ceiling. Allow your jaw to relax and your mouth to open slightly. Feel the stretch through the front of your neck and throat. Hold for 15 to 20 seconds. Breathe normally. Slowly return your head to neutral position. Repeat 2 to 3 times. Move slowly and never force the stretch — protect your cervical spine.
Benefits: Stretches the front of the neck; Counteracts forward head posture; Quick and accessible; No equipment needed; Useful for desk workers; Improves cervical spine mobility
Muscles Worked (Raw): Sternocleidomastoid; Scalenes (anterior, middle, posterior); Platysma; Sternohyoid

Description: Stand or sit tall. Interlace your fingers in front of you with palms facing your body. Rotate your wrists outward so your palms now face forward. Extend your arms forward at chest height, pushing your hands away from your body. Round your upper back, like you are hugging a large beach ball. Tuck your chin slightly toward your chest. Feel the stretch through your upper back, rhomboids, and rear shoulders. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Release and shake out your shoulders. Repeat 2 to 3 times.
Benefits: Opens the thoracic spine and rhomboids; Stretches the mid-back and rear shoulders; Counteracts hunched posture; Quick and accessible; No equipment needed; Excellent between-sets stretch
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rhomboids; Trapezius (middle fibers); Posterior deltoid; Latissimus dorsi (slight)

Description: Sit or stand tall with shoulders pulled back and down. Slowly drop your chin toward your chest. Place both hands on the back of your head and apply gentle downward pressure to deepen the stretch. Feel the stretch through the back of your neck and upper traps. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Slowly release and return your head to neutral. Repeat 2 to 3 times. Apply only gentle pressure with the hands — protect the cervical spine.
Benefits: Stretches the back of the neck; Relieves upper-trap tension; Quick and accessible; Counteracts hunched posture; Useful for desk workers; No equipment needed
Muscles Worked (Raw): Suboccipitals; Splenius capitis and cervicis; Upper trapezius; Levator scapulae; Erector spinae (cervical)

Description: Sit or stand tall with the shoulders relaxed. Place one hand on the opposite side of the head. Let the other arm hang at your side. Gently pull the head sideways toward the shoulder. Stop when you feel a stretch on the side of the neck. Keep the shoulders down and avoid shrugging. Hold the stretch for the desired duration. Release and repeat on the other side.
Benefits: Lengthens the upper traps and side of the neck.; Reduces tension from desk work.; No equipment needed.; Easy to perform anywhere.; Improves neck mobility.; Excellent recovery between training sessions.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Trapezius; Levator scapulae; Sternocleidomastoid; Scalene

Description: Stand next to a wall with one side of your body facing it. Place your palm flat on the wall, arm extended straight and at shoulder height. Keep your hand in place and slowly rotate your torso away from the wall. Continue rotating until you feel a stretch across your chest and bicep. Hold the stretch for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily. Release gently by rotating your body back toward the wall. Switch sides and repeat with the other arm. Perform 2 to 3 rounds per side.
Benefits: Opens tight chest muscles; Stretches the biceps and front shoulder; Great recovery stretch after pressing; Requires no equipment; Easy to perform anywhere with a wall; Improves upper body mobility
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Biceps brachii; Anterior deltoid

Description: Sit or stand tall. Pull both shoulders back and down. Tilt your head to the right, bringing your right ear toward your right shoulder. Place your right hand gently on the left side of your head and apply light pressure to deepen the stretch. Keep your left shoulder pulled down and back — do not let it shrug up. Feel the stretch through the left side of your neck and upper trap. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Release and switch sides. Apply only gentle pressure with the hand — never force the stretch.
Benefits: Relieves neck and upper-trap tightness; Counteracts stress and screen-related tension; Quick and accessible; No equipment needed; Excellent for desk workers; Improves head and neck posture
Muscles Worked (Raw): Upper trapezius; Sternocleidomastoid; Levator scapulae; Splenius capitis; Scalenes

Description: Stand to the right of a sturdy doorframe, pole, or pull-up bar. Reach up and grip the anchor with your right hand at roughly head height. Use a thumbless grip if comfortable. Step away from the anchor with your right hand still gripping. Lean your hips and torso to the left, away from the anchor. Drop your right shoulder toward the floor to deepen the stretch. Feel the deep stretch through your right lat and right side body. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Release and switch sides.
Benefits: Isolates each lat individually; Reveals left-right tightness asymmetries; Deep stretch through the lat and side body; Improves overhead mobility; No equipment needed beyond a sturdy anchor; Excellent post-workout stretch
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi; Teres major; Obliques (stretched side); Quadratus lumborum; Triceps brachii

Description: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Arms at your sides. Quickly raise both arms straight out to the sides and continue lifting them overhead. Clap your hands together overhead. Lower your arms back down to your sides under control. Repeat for 15 to 25 reps. Move at a moderate pace. The point is to mobilize and warm up the shoulders. Keep your core braced and torso upright throughout. Excellent warm-up before any upper-body training.
Benefits: Mobilizes the shoulders dynamically; Activates the lower traps and serratus anterior; Improves shoulder warm-up before pressing; No equipment needed; Builds shoulder endurance; Easy to scale by adjusting tempo
Muscles Worked (Raw): Anterior, lateral, and posterior deltoid; Lower trapezius; Serratus anterior; Upper trapezius

Description: Lie on your right side with knees bent at 90 degrees, stacked on top of each other. Extend both arms straight out in front of you at shoulder height, palms together. Keep your knees stacked and pinned to the floor throughout the movement. Inhale and slowly rotate your top (left) arm up and over toward the opposite side. Continue rotating until your left hand reaches the floor on your left side (or as close as possible). Look at your top hand throughout the rotation. Your head and chest follow the arm. Hold the open position for 2 to 3 breaths. Feel the stretch through your chest and thoracic spine. Slowly return to start. Repeat 5 to 8 times per side.
Benefits: Targets thoracic spine rotation specifically; Keeps the lower back stable while mobilizing the upper back; Stretches the chest, lats, and obliques; Excellent warm-up for rotational sports; No equipment needed; One of the best thoracic mobility drills
Muscles Worked (Raw): Thoracic spine rotators; Pectoralis major (stretched); Latissimus dorsi (stretched); Obliques; Anterior deltoid (stretched)

Description: Stand or sit tall. Reach your right arm straight up overhead. Bend your right elbow to drop your right hand down behind your head, between your shoulder blades. Reach your left hand up and grasp your right elbow. Gently pull your right elbow toward the left and slightly down, deepening the stretch. Feel the stretch through the back of your right upper arm (tricep) and the right side of your back (lat). Keep your chest lifted. Avoid arching your lower back. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch sides and repeat.
Benefits: Stretches the triceps and lats; Improves overhead mobility; Quick and accessible; No equipment needed; Excellent post-workout stretch for arm and pressing days; Counteracts forward shoulder posture
Muscles Worked (Raw): Triceps brachii (especially long head); Latissimus dorsi; Posterior deltoid; Teres major

Description: Lie flat on your back. Extend both legs straight. Bend your right knee and bring it toward your chest. Clasp both hands around your right shin. Gently pull your knee closer to your chest. Keep your left leg extended flat on the floor. Press your lower back into the floor. Relax your shoulders and neck. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply into your belly. Release and switch to the left knee. For the full pose: pull both knees to your chest simultaneously and rock gently side to side. This pose is calming and restorative — no effort or strain should be involved.
Benefits: Relieves lower-back tension and tightness; Stretches the glutes and hip extensors; Gently massages the abdominal organs; Aids digestion and relieves gas (hence the name); Calming and restorative; Suitable for all levels including complete beginners
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus maximus (stretched); Erector spinae (lower back, stretched); Hip extensors; Hamstrings (secondary stretch)

Exercise Name: One Legged Upward Bow Pose Eka Pada Urdhva Dhanurasana
Description: Lie on the back with the knees bent and feet flat. Place the hands by the ears with fingers pointing toward the shoulders. Press the hips up and lift into upward bow. Press the chest open and straighten the arms. Brace the core and squeeze the glutes. Lift one leg straight up toward the ceiling. Hold the pose with the leg lifted. Lower with control then switch sides.
Benefits: Stretches the chest deeply.; Opens the hip flexors.; Builds shoulder strength.; Trains balance.; Advanced backbend progression.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Hip flexors; Quadriceps; Anterior deltoid

Description: Start in a tabletop (hands and knees) or downward-facing dog position. Bring your right knee forward and place it on the floor behind your right wrist. Your right shin angles toward your left hip (beginners) or is parallel to the front of the mat (advanced). Extend your left leg straight behind you with the top of the left foot on the floor. Square your hips toward the front of the mat as much as possible. Walk your hands forward and lower your torso over your right leg for a deeper stretch. Rest your forehead on the floor or on your stacked hands. Feel the deep stretch in your right glute and outer hip. You should also feel a stretch in your left hip flexor. Hold for 30 to 90 seconds. Breathe deeply and let gravity deepen the stretch. Press back up to tabletop and repeat on the other side.
Benefits: One of the deepest hip and glute stretches in any discipline; Stretches the piriformis and deep hip rotators; Opens the hip flexors of the back leg; Relieves sciatic tension for many people; Improves hip mobility for squats and deadlifts; Calming and restorative — excellent for cool-downs
Muscles Worked (Raw): Piriformis (front leg); Gluteus maximus (front leg); Deep hip external rotators (front leg); Hip flexors (back leg, stretched); Erector spinae (when folded forward)

Description: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor. Place your hands on your hip bones or at your sides. Gently tilt your pelvis so your lower back presses flat into the floor. Imagine pulling your belly button toward your spine. Hold for 5 to 10 seconds. Release and allow your natural arch to return. Repeat 10 to 15 times. The movement is subtle — focus on the pelvic rotation, not ab crunching.
Benefits: Foundational core activation exercise; Widely used for lower back pain management; Activates the transverse abdominis; Teaches pelvic awareness and control; No equipment needed; Gentle and accessible for all levels
Muscles Worked (Raw): Transverse abdominis; Rectus abdominis (slight); Gluteus maximus (slight); Multifidus (learning to control)

Description: Sit on the floor with your right leg extended. Cross your left ankle over your right thigh. Use your right hand to grip the top of your left foot. Gently roll your left foot inward — bring the sole of your foot to face the ceiling. You should feel a stretch along the outer side of your left lower leg and ankle. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Release and shake out your foot. Switch sides. For a standing version: cross one foot over the other and roll the top foot inward. Repeat two to three times per side.
Benefits: Stretches the peroneal muscles on the outer calf; Improves ankle inversion mobility; Relieves tightness from lateral movement and running; Helps prevent ankle injuries; Useful for athletes in court sports; No equipment needed
Muscles Worked (Raw): Peroneus longus and brevis; Lateral ankle muscles; Lateral foot fascia

Description: Start in a high plank position. Push your hips up and back into a pike (downward dog) position — an inverted V shape. Feel the stretch in your hamstrings and calves. Press your heels toward the floor. Shift your weight forward, lowering your hips toward the floor while lifting your chest. Roll forward into a cobra position. In cobra: hips near the floor, chest lifted, arms straight or slightly bent, shoulders pulled back. Hold briefly, then push your hips back up and back into the pike position. Continue flowing between pike and cobra for the desired number of reps. Move with your breath: exhale into pike, inhale into cobra. Perform 8 to 12 reps as a warm-up or mobility drill.
Benefits: Improves full spinal flexion and extension mobility; Stretches the hamstrings, calves, chest, and shoulders; Warms up the entire body dynamically; Builds shoulder and core endurance; Excellent pre-workout mobility drill; No equipment needed
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae (cobra phase); Hamstrings and calves (pike phase); Pectoralis major (cobra phase, stretched); Anterior deltoid (pike phase, loaded); Core (transition control)

Description: Kneel down and place the hands flat on the floor with fingers pointing back. Bend the elbows and bring them together. Press the elbows into your abdomen below the ribs. Lean the chest forward over the hands. Brace your core hard. Shift the weight forward and lift the legs off the floor. Hold the body horizontal in a straight line. Lower the legs back down with control.
Benefits: Advanced arm balance; Builds wrist strength; Trains core balance; No equipment needed; Strong yoga pose; Builds forearm strength
Muscles Worked (Raw): Core; Wrist flexors; Forearms; Anterior deltoid

Description: Lie flat on your back with knees bent at 90 degrees and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Begin with a posterior pelvic tilt: press your lower back firmly into the floor and tilt your pelvis up toward your ribs. From the pelvic tilt, sequentially roll your spine off the floor — tailbone, lower back, mid-back — until you reach a glute bridge position. At the top, your body forms a straight line from knees to shoulders. Squeeze your glutes. Reverse the motion: roll your spine back down sequentially — mid-back, lower back, tailbone. End with the posterior pelvic tilt before releasing. Move slowly and with control. Each vertebra should leave and return to the floor sequentially. Repeat for 8 to 12 reps as a warm-up or core activation.
Benefits: Teaches segmental spinal articulation; Builds glute activation; Improves lumbar control; Excellent warm-up for lower-body training; Useful for rehabilitation and posture work; No equipment needed
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus maximus; Hamstrings; Erector spinae (control); Rectus abdominis (pelvic tilt); Transverse abdominis

Description: Start in a high plank position. Press the hips up and back into a downward dog pike. Hold the pike position briefly stretching the hamstrings. Lower the hips and slide the body forward through plank. Continue forward as the body lowers toward the floor. Lift the chest up into a low cobra position. Press the chest tall opening the front body. Hold the cobra briefly. Reverse the flow back to pike.
Benefits: Strong full body yoga flow; Stretches the hamstrings; Opens the chest; Builds shoulder mobility; Useful cool down; Strong yoga flow
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings; Pectoralis major; Spinal erectors

Description: Lie on your back with arms at your sides, palms down. Press your palms into the floor and use your core to lift your legs straight up to vertical. Continue lifting your hips off the floor and bring your legs overhead. Lower your toes toward the floor behind your head. If they reach the floor, rest them gently. If your toes do not reach, support your hips with your hands or use a chair behind you. Keep your weight on your shoulders, not your neck. Your chin should be tucked toward your chest. Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe slowly and deeply. To exit, bring your hands to your lower back for support and slowly lower your legs back to the start.
Benefits: Deeply stretches the hamstrings, calves, and lower back; Decompresses the spine; Calms the nervous system; Stimulates the thyroid (claimed); Foundation for shoulder stand; No equipment needed
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings (deep stretch); Erector spinae (decompressed); Gastrocnemius and soleus; Trapezius (loaded); Core (lifting and lowering)

Description: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out. Squat down as deep as possible — ideally with your hips below your knees. Keep your heels on the floor. If your heels rise, widen your stance or angle your toes out more. Hold the deep position. Arms can be in front for counterbalance. Breathe deeply and relax into the position. Hold for 30 to 120 seconds. Build up hold time progressively. Use a door frame or pole for balance assistance if needed.
Benefits: Develops deep squat mobility; Improves hip, ankle, and thoracic flexibility; Builds comfort in the bottom squat position; No equipment needed; Used as a daily mobility practice; Foundational human resting position
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hip flexors and adductors (stretched); Calves and ankles (dorsiflexion); Quadriceps (isometric); Erector spinae; Gluteus maximus

Description: Sit on your heels in a kneeling position with the tops of both feet pressing into the floor. Sit back on your heels until you feel a stretch through the front of your ankles, shins, and tops of your feet. Place your hands on your knees or thighs for balance. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. For a deeper stretch, lift your knees slightly off the floor by leaning back. For a single-leg version, sit cross-legged and place one foot on top of the opposite knee, pointing the toes. Release and shake out your feet. Repeat as needed for shin and foot tension relief.
Benefits: Stretches the tibialis anterior (front of shin); Opens the top of the foot and front of the ankle; Relieves shin splint discomfort; Counteracts tightness from running and sprinting; No equipment needed; Quick and accessible
Muscles Worked (Raw): Tibialis anterior; Extensor digitorum longus; Top of foot fascia; Anterior ankle ligaments

Description: Sit on the floor with your right leg extended. Cross your left ankle over your right thigh. Use your right hand to grip the top of your left foot. Gently pull your left toes back toward your shin while turning the sole outward (eversion). You should feel a stretch through the inner side of your left lower leg, behind your shin. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Release and shake out your foot. Switch sides. For a standing version: place one foot on a curb or step with the inside edge slightly elevated. Repeat two to three times per side.
Benefits: Stretches the posterior tibialis (deep inner calf); Helps relieve plantar fasciitis and shin splints; Improves ankle eversion mobility; Supports better arch function; Useful for runners with foot pain; No equipment needed
Muscles Worked (Raw): Posterior tibialis; Flexor digitorum longus; Deep posterior compartment of the lower leg; Plantar fascia (secondary)

Description: Lie on your right side. Bend your right knee to 90 degrees in front of you, with your right foot pointing forward. Bend your left knee behind you, bringing your left heel toward your left glute. Reach back with your left hand and grab your left foot. Pull it gently toward your glute for a quad stretch. Keep your right side body pressed into the floor for support. Feel the stretch through your right hip rotators (in front) and your left quad and hip flexor (behind). Use your right hand to support yourself if needed. Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply. Roll over and switch sides.
Benefits: Combines hip rotation with quad stretch; Opens multiple muscle groups simultaneously; Excellent for tight hips from sitting or running; Time-efficient combined stretch; No equipment needed; Calming when held for longer durations
Muscles Worked (Raw): Piriformis (front leg); Gluteus maximus and medius (front leg); Quadriceps (back leg); Hip flexors (back leg); IT band

Description: Lie face down on the floor. Interlock the hands behind the lower back. Brace your core and squeeze the glutes. Lift the chest off the floor. Pull the interlocked hands down toward the feet. Squeeze the upper back and rear delts. Hold the cobra position briefly. Lower with control to the start.
Benefits: Opens the chest; Builds the upper back; Strong cobra variation; Useful for posture; Builds back extension
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae; Posterior deltoid; Trapezius

Description: Stand tall. Hold a PVC pipe or stick with both hands in front of you, elbows at 90 degrees by your sides. Use your left hand to push the stick to the right, rotating your right forearm outward (external rotation). Go as far as comfortable. Hold for 5 to 10 seconds. Return to center. Use your right hand to push left, rotating your left forearm outward. Continue alternating for 10 to 15 reps per side. The stick provides gentle assisted stretching. Use as a warm-up before pressing or overhead work.
Benefits: Gentle rotator cuff warm-up and mobility; Stick provides assisted stretching; Improves external rotation range; Prevents shoulder impingement; Minimal equipment needed; Widely used in physical therapy
Muscles Worked (Raw): Infraspinatus; Teres minor; Posterior deltoid (slight)

Description: Stand with feet slightly wider than hip-width, toes turned out 30 to 45 degrees. Squat down deep, lowering your hips toward your heels. Bring your hands together in prayer position at your heart center. Press your elbows against the inside of your knees, pushing them outward. Sit up tall with chest lifted and back as straight as possible. Keep your heels pressed into the floor. If they lift, place a folded blanket or yoga block under them. Hold for 30 seconds to 2 minutes. Breathe deeply. To exit, place your hands on the floor and slowly stand up.
Benefits: Deep hip opener — one of the most effective hip stretches; Improves squat depth and mobility; Stretches the inner thighs and groin; Strengthens the legs and feet; Foundational yoga pose; Calming when held for longer durations
Muscles Worked (Raw): Adductors; Hip external rotators; Gluteus maximus; Quadriceps; Calves and ankle stabilizers; Erector spinae (postural)

Description: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Bring your palms together in front of your chest in a prayer position. Press the bases of the palms together firmly. Pull the elbows out to the sides at chest level. Press the palms together hard, engaging the chest. Hold the maximum chest contraction. Maintain steady deep breathing through the hold. Release the press, rest briefly, and repeat for desired sets.
Benefits: Isometric chest activation; Stretches the wrists; No equipment required; Strong inner chest engagement; Useful for warmups; Builds mind-muscle connection
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Wrist flexors; Anterior deltoid

Description: Stand facing a sturdy pole, doorframe, or squat rack. Position your feet wider than shoulder-width with toes pointed slightly out. Reach forward and grip the support with both hands. Brace your core and keep your chest up. Squat down by sitting your hips back and lowering between your feet. Continue down until your hips are below your knees. Use the support to stay balanced and pull yourself deeper. Hold the deep squat and breathe, then stand back up using the support.
Benefits: Opens the hips and ankles; Loosens the groin and adductors; Improves squat depth; Useful for mobility and warm-up; Easy to scale with support
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hips; Adductors; Quadriceps; Calves

Description: Start in a tabletop position on your hands and knees. Hips directly above knees, shoulders above wrists. Walk your hands forward as far as you can while keeping your hips stacked above your knees. Lower your chest toward the floor. Let your forehead or chin rest on the mat. Keep your arms active — press your palms into the floor and reach forward. Feel the stretch through your chest, shoulders, armpits, and upper back. Keep your hips high — directly above your knees. Do not let them drift forward. Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply into the stretch. To release, walk your hands back toward your knees.
Benefits: Deeply stretches the chest, shoulders, and upper back; Opens the armpits and lats; Extends the spine gently; More active than Child’s Pose, deeper than Downward Dog; Calming and restorative; No equipment needed
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major (stretched); Latissimus dorsi (stretched); Anterior deltoid (stretched); Erector spinae (gently extended); Triceps brachii (extended arms)

Description: Lie on your side with your bottom leg extended straight. Bend the top knee and reach back to grab the top ankle. Pull the top heel toward the same-side glute. Keep your hips stacked and squared. Push the top hip forward slightly to deepen the stretch. Hold the position and breathe deeply. Release the leg slowly. Roll to the other side and repeat.
Benefits: Stretches the quadriceps; Lengthens the hip flexors; No balance required; Easier than standing version; Useful for tight quads
Muscles Worked (Raw): Quadriceps; Hip flexors; Rectus femoris

Description: Stand tall on one leg. Hold a wall or pole for balance if needed. Bend your right knee and grab your right ankle behind you with your right hand. Pull your right heel toward your right glute. Keep your knees together. Squeeze your right glute and tuck your tailbone slightly to deepen the stretch. Stand tall — do not lean forward. Feel the stretch through the front of your right thigh. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch to the left leg and repeat.
Benefits: Stretches all four quadriceps muscles; Improves quad flexibility for squat depth; Quick and accessible — works anywhere; No equipment needed; Trains balance simultaneously; Useful warm-up or cool-down stretch
Muscles Worked (Raw): Quadriceps (rectus femoris, vastus medialis, lateralis, intermedius); Hip flexors (rectus femoris crosses the hip)

Description: Hold a PVC pipe, broomstick, or band with a very wide overhand grip in front of your thighs. Keep your arms straight throughout. Raise the stick up overhead and continue the arc behind your back. The stick should travel from front → overhead → behind in one smooth motion. Reverse the motion back to the front. Start with a very wide grip. Narrow over time as mobility improves. If any point feels painful, widen your grip. Perform 10 to 15 pass-throughs as a warm-up.
Benefits: Gold-standard shoulder mobility exercise; Improves shoulder flexion and extension range; Warms up the entire shoulder complex; Easy to track progress by grip width; Minimal equipment needed; Used by Olympic lifters worldwide
Muscles Worked (Raw): Deltoids (all heads through range); Rotator cuff; Pectoralis major (stretched); Latissimus dorsi (stretched); Trapezius

Description: Stand or sit tall. Interlace your fingers in front of you with palms facing your body. Rotate your wrists outward so your palms now face forward. Extend your arms forward at chest height, pushing your hands away from your body. Round your upper back, like you are hugging a large beach ball. Tuck your chin slightly toward your chest. Feel the stretch through your upper back, rhomboids, and rear shoulders. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Release and shake out your shoulders. Repeat two to three times.
Benefits: Opens the rhomboids and mid-back; Stretches the rear shoulders; Counteracts hunched posture from lifting and sitting; Quick and accessible; No equipment needed; Excellent between-sets stretch
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rhomboids; Trapezius (middle fibers); Posterior deltoid; Latissimus dorsi (slight)

Exercise Name: Resistance Band Assisted Front Rack Stretch
Description: Anchor a resistance band overhead. Stand under the band facing away. Place the band over the hands and behind the elbows. Bring the elbows up to the front rack position. Brace your core and keep the chest up. Let the band assist in pulling the elbows higher. Hold the deepened front rack stretch. Release with control.
Benefits: Improves front rack mobility; Stretches the triceps; Useful warm-up; Strong shoulder mobility move; Builds shoulder range
Muscles Worked (Raw): Triceps brachii; Latissimus dorsi; Posterior deltoid

Description: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Reach your right arm straight up overhead. Extend as high as you can. Feel the stretch through your right shoulder, lat, and side body. For a deeper stretch, grab your right wrist with your left hand and gently pull to the left, adding a side lean. Hold for 15 to 20 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch sides and repeat. Can also be done with both arms reaching overhead simultaneously. Keep your ribs down — do not flare them or arch your back excessively.
Benefits: Opens the shoulders and stretches the lats; Counteracts hunched posture from sitting; Stretches the intercostals and obliques with a side lean; Quick and accessible — works anywhere; Excellent between-sets stretch; No equipment needed
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi (stretched); Deltoids (stretched); Obliques (with side lean); Intercostals; Triceps brachii (overhead position)

Description: Sit on the floor with both legs extended in front of you. Hold a resistance band or yoga strap. Loop the band around the ball of your right foot. Hold both ends with your hands. Sit up tall with chest lifted. Gently pull both ends of the band toward your body, flexing your right ankle. Keep your right knee straight throughout. Feel the deep stretch through your right calf and Achilles tendon. Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch legs and repeat. Apply only gentle pulling pressure.
Benefits: Safe and controlled calf stretch; Band allows precise depth control; Excellent for tight calves; Comfortable seated position; Easy on the lower back; Useful for runners
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gastrocnemius and soleus; Achilles tendon; Plantar fascia (slight); Hamstrings (secondary)

Description: Stand with feet about three feet apart in a split stance. Right foot forward, left foot back and angled slightly outward. Square your hips forward as much as possible. Both legs straight. Inhale and lift your chest. Place your hands on your hips or clasp them behind your back. Exhale and fold forward from the hips over your right leg. Lead with your chest, not your head. Lower your torso as far as your flexibility allows. Place your hands on the floor, blocks, or your shin. Keep both legs straight. Press through the heel of your front foot. Hold for 5 to 10 breaths. Breathe deeply and let gravity deepen the fold. Inhale to rise up. Switch sides.
Benefits: Intensely stretches the hamstrings and calves of the front leg; Stretches the hip flexors of the back leg; Improves balance and proprioception; Builds spinal flexibility; Strengthens the legs isometrically; Calming forward fold
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings (front leg); Gastrocnemius and soleus (front leg); Hip flexors (back leg, stretched); Erector spinae (stretched); Quadriceps (isometric)

Exercise Name: Resistance Band Serratus Wall Slide with Foam Roll
Description: Loop a small resistance band around both wrists. Stand facing a wall with a foam roller pressed against it. Place both forearms on the roller with the band stretched. Brace the core and press the arms forward into the roller. Roll the foam roller up the wall while reaching overhead. Keep the band taut throughout to engage the serratus. Lower with control to the start. Continue for the working set.
Benefits: Activates the serratus anterior.; Band trains scapular control.; Improves overhead mobility.; Builds shoulder health.; Useful warm-up.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Serratus anterior; Trapezius; Anterior deltoid

Exercise Name: Resistance Band Shoulder Stretch Behind the Back
Description: Hold a resistance band behind the back with both hands. Set the hands at shoulder width apart. Stand tall with the chest up. Brace the core and keep the shoulders down. Pull the hands wider apart against the band. Feel the stretch across the front of the shoulders and chest. Hold the stretched position. Release and repeat for the desired time.
Benefits: Stretches the front shoulders.; Opens the chest.; Loads the biceps gently.; Useful warm-up.; Improves shoulder mobility.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Anterior deltoid; Pectoralis major; Biceps brachii

Exercise Name: Resistance Band Squatting Front Warming Up
Description: Hold a light resistance band with both hands in front of you. Stand with feet at shoulder-width. Pull lightly on the band to engage the upper back. Brace your core and keep your chest up. Squat down as deep as feels comfortable. Use the band tension to keep the upper back tall. Pause briefly in the deep squat to feel the hip stretch. Drive up through the heels to stand back up.
Benefits: Mobilizes the hips; Warms up the legs; Trains squat depth; No equipment needed beyond band; Useful pre-training drill; Easy to add to any warm-up
Muscles Worked (Raw): Quadriceps; Gluteus maximus; Hip flexors; Adductors

Exercise Name: Resistance Band Standing Forward Achilles Stretch
Description: Loop a resistance band around the ball of the working foot. Hold the band ends with both hands. Step the working foot back into a forward lunge stance. Keep the back heel on the floor. Brace your core and keep the chest up. Pull the band gently to deepen the stretch. Lean the front knee forward over the toes. Hold the stretch then switch sides.
Benefits: Stretches the calves; Improves dorsiflexion; Useful warm-up; Strong Achilles stretch; Trains ankle mobility
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gastrocnemius; Soleus; Calves

Exercise Name: Resistance Band Standing Back Warming Up
Description: Stand tall with the feet shoulder width apart. Hold a resistance band at chest height with both hands. Set the hands shoulder width apart. Brace the core and keep the chest up. Pull the hands apart against the band. Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the end range. Pause briefly at the squeezed position. Return to the start and continue for the working set.
Benefits: Warms up the upper back.; Activates the rear delts.; Improves posture.; Useful pre-workout.; Builds shoulder health.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Posterior deltoid; Trapezius; Rhomboids

Exercise Name: Resistance Band Standing Down Warming Up
Description: Anchor a resistance band overhead. Stand under the anchor and grab the band with both hands. Hold the band straight overhead. Brace the core and keep the chest up. Pull the hands straight down past the hips. Squeeze the lats hard at the bottom. Pause briefly at full extension. Return to the start and continue for the working set.
Benefits: Warms up the lats.; Activates the triceps.; Useful pre-workout.; Improves shoulder health.; Builds the upper back.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi; Triceps brachii; Trapezius

Description: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Bring both arms behind your back. Clasp your hands together with palms facing each other or with fingers interlaced. Pull your shoulders back and down. Lift your chest. Slowly straighten your arms and lift your clasped hands away from your body, behind you. Continue lifting until you feel a deep stretch across your chest and front shoulders. Keep your chest lifted. Avoid hunching forward or arching your lower back. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Release slowly. Repeat two to three times.
Benefits: Deeply opens the chest, shoulders, and biceps; Counteracts forward-rounded shoulders; Quick and accessible — works anywhere; No equipment needed; Improves shoulder mobility; Excellent between-sets stretch
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major (stretched); Anterior deltoid (stretched); Biceps brachii (stretched); Subscapularis

Exercise Name: Resistance Band Standing Overhead Warming Up
Description: Stand on a resistance band with both feet. Grab the handles and bring them to shoulder height. Brace the core and keep the chest up. Set the elbows in front of the body. Press both hands overhead to lockout. Squeeze the delts and triceps at the top. Lower the hands back to shoulder height. Continue for the working set.
Benefits: Warms up the shoulders.; Activates the triceps.; Useful pre-workout.; Improves shoulder health.; Builds overhead readiness.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Anterior deltoid; Lateral deltoid; Triceps brachii

Description: Stand or sit tall with feet hip-width apart. Reach both arms behind your back. Clasp your hands together with palms facing inward or fingers interlaced. Pull your shoulders back and down. Slowly lift your clasped hands up and away from your body, behind you. Continue lifting until you feel a deep stretch across your chest, front shoulders, and biceps. Keep your chest lifted and core braced. Avoid arching your lower back. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Release slowly and repeat two to three times.
Benefits: Opens the chest, front shoulders, and biceps; Counteracts rounded shoulder posture; Quick and accessible; No equipment needed; Excellent for desk workers; Improves shoulder mobility
Muscles Worked (Raw): Anterior deltoid; Pectoralis major and minor; Biceps brachii; Subscapularis

Exercise Name: Resistance Band Standing Front Warming Up

Muscles Worked (Raw): Biceps brachii; Brachialis; Brachioradialis

Description: Stand with the back to a wall. Place a massage ball between the upper trap and the wall. Brace the core and keep the body tall. Press into the ball with controlled pressure. Tip the head gently away from the ball to deepen pressure. Roll slowly across the trap area. Pause on tender spots for several breaths. Continue for the working time then switch sides.
Benefits: Releases the upper trap.; Reduces neck tension.; Improves shoulder mobility.; Useful for desk workers.; Joint friendly release.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Trapezius; Levator scapulae; Sternocleidomastoid

Exercise Name: Roll Chest Opener Lying on Floor
Description: Place a foam roller on the floor lengthwise. Sit at the end of the roller and lie back so the spine rests along the length. Bend the knees with feet flat for stability. Allow the head to rest on the roller. Open the arms out to the sides at shoulder height. Allow the hands to relax toward the floor. Breathe slowly and deeply into the stretch. Hold for the desired duration.
Benefits: Opens the chest.; Stretches the front shoulders.; Mobilizes the thoracic spine.; Useful for posture.; Joint friendly stretch.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Anterior deltoid; Erector spinae

Exercise Name: Roll Erector Spinae Lying on Floor
Description: Lie on the back with the knees bent and feet flat. Place a foam roller along the side of the spine. Brace the core and keep the head supported. Lift the hips slightly to load the roller. Shift the body slowly along the length of the erector. Pause on tender spots for several breaths. Avoid pressing directly on the spine. Continue for the working time then switch sides.
Benefits: Releases the back muscles.; Improves spinal mobility.; Reduces lower back tightness.; Useful after heavy lifting.; Joint friendly release.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae; Quadratus lumborum; Trapezius

Description: Lie on the back with the knees bent and feet flat. Place a massage ball below the shoulder blade in the mid back. Brace the core and keep the head supported. Lift the hips slightly to load the ball. Roll slowly through the lower trap area. Pause on tender spots for several breaths. Adjust angle to find the muscle. Continue for the working time then switch sides.
Benefits: Releases the lower trap.; Improves shoulder mechanics.; Reduces upper back tightness.; Useful for pressing.; Joint friendly release.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Trapezius; Rhomboids; Erector spinae

Exercise Name: Roll Front Shoulder and Chest Lying on Floor
Description: Lie face down on the floor. Place a foam roller diagonally under the chest and front shoulder. Extend the working arm out to the side. Brace the body on the other forearm. Keep the working chest and shoulder relaxed over the roller. Roll slowly across the chest and front delt. Pause on tender spots for several breaths. Continue for the working time then switch sides.
Benefits: Releases the chest and front shoulder.; Improves shoulder posture.; Reduces front body tightness.; Useful after pressing work.; Joint friendly release.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Anterior deltoid; Pectoralis minor

Exercise Name: Roll Glute Twist Lying on Floor
Description: Sit on the floor with a foam roller under one glute. Cross the working leg ankle over the opposite knee. Lean back onto the hands for support. Brace the core and shift the weight onto the roller. Roll the glute slowly back and forth. Twist the hips to one side over the roller. Twist back through to the other side. Continue for the working time then switch sides.
Benefits: Releases the glutes through multiple angles.; Hits the glute max and medius.; Useful for hip mobility.; Reduces sitting tightness.; Joint friendly release.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus maximus; Gluteus medius; Piriformis

Description: Place a small firm ball (lacrosse ball, tennis ball, or massage ball) on the floor. Stand with your right foot on top of the ball. Place your hands on a wall or chair for balance. Apply moderate pressure by transferring some of your bodyweight onto the ball. Slowly roll your foot back and forth across the ball — from heel to toes. Roll slowly. Pause on tender spots and apply gentle sustained pressure. Roll the inner and outer parts of your foot as well. Continue for 1 to 2 minutes per foot. For less intensity, sit in a chair instead of standing.
Benefits: Releases plantar fascia tightness; Most effective intervention for plantar fasciitis; Improves foot mobility and circulation; Helps reduce arch pain; Inexpensive — needs only a small ball; Easy to do anywhere
Muscles Worked (Raw): Plantar fascia; Foot intrinsic muscles; Achilles tendon (secondary); Calves (referred)

Description: Stand facing a wall with a foam roller pinned vertically against it. Place one forearm flat against the roller. Press the arm into the roller with the body weight. Brace the core and keep the chest up. Slide the forearm slowly up and down the roller. Rotate the wrist to cover all sides of the forearm. Pause on tender spots for several breaths. Continue for the working time then switch sides.
Benefits: Releases the forearms.; Reduces grip fatigue.; Improves wrist mobility.; Useful for climbers and lifters.; Joint friendly release.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Forearm flexors; Forearm extensors; Brachioradialis

Description: Sit on the floor with a foam roller under one glute. Cross the working leg ankle over the opposite knee. Lean back onto the hands for support. Brace the core and shift the weight onto the roller. Roll the glute slowly back and forth over the roller. Pause on tender spots for several breaths. Adjust angle to cover the full glute. Continue for the working time then switch sides.
Benefits: Releases the glutes.; Improves hip mobility.; Reduces sitting tightness.; Useful for runners.; Joint friendly release.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus maximus; Gluteus medius; Piriformis

Description: Lie face down on the floor. Place a foam roller under one side of the chest near the shoulder. Extend the working arm out to the side. Brace the body on the other forearm. Keep the working chest relaxed over the roller. Roll the chest slowly over the roller. Pause on tender spots for several breaths. Cover the upper inner and outer chest then switch sides.
Benefits: Releases the chest.; Improves shoulder posture.; Reduces front body tightness.; Useful after pressing work.; Joint friendly release.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Pectoralis minor; Anterior deltoid

Description: Kneel on the floor in front of a foam roller. Place one elbow on the roller with the palm up. Set the other hand on the floor for support. Brace the core and keep the back flat. Rotate the torso toward the supported elbow. Reach the chest open with the rotation. Hold the rotated position briefly. Return to start and continue for all reps then switch.
Benefits: Mobilizes the thoracic spine.; Releases the upper back.; Opens the chest.; Useful warm-up.; Improves rotational mobility.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Latissimus dorsi; Trapezius; Rhomboids

Description: Place a small foam roller or massage ball on the floor. Lie face down with the roller just inside your right hip bone. Position the roller below the rib cage and to the inside of the hip. Support yourself on your forearms. Brace your core and breathe slowly. Slowly shift your weight onto the roller in this position. Allow the roller to sink into the iliopsoas tissue. Hold tender spots for 20 to 30 seconds. Switch sides.
Benefits: Releases hip flexor tension; Improves hip mobility; Useful for desk worker tightness; Helps with lower back tension; Recovery drill for lifters and runners; Easy to do at home
Muscles Worked (Raw): Iliopsoas; Hip flexors; Quadriceps (rectus femoris)

Exercise Name: Roll Hamstrings and Glute Sitting on Floor
Description: Sit on the floor with a foam roller under one hamstring. Set the other foot flat on the floor for stability. Lean back onto the hands for support. Brace the core and shift the weight onto the roller. Roll from the back of the knee up the hamstring. Continue rolling up onto the glute. Pause on tender spots for several breaths. Continue for the working time then switch sides.
Benefits: Releases the hamstrings and glute.; Improves hip mobility.; Reduces posterior chain tightness.; Useful for runners.; Joint friendly release.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings; Gluteus maximus; Piriformis

Description: Sit on the floor with a foam roller under one hamstring. Set the other foot flat on the floor for stability. Lean back onto the hands for support. Brace the core and shift the weight onto the roller. Roll the hamstring slowly along the back of the thigh. Pause on tender spots for several breaths. Cover from glute to behind the knee. Continue for the working time then switch sides.
Benefits: Releases the hamstrings.; Improves hip mobility.; Reduces hamstring tightness.; Useful for runners.; Joint friendly release.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings; Gluteus maximus; Calves

Exercise Name: Roll Neck Rotation Lying on Floor
Description: Lie on the back on the floor. Place a foam roller or massage stick under the neck. Bend the knees with feet flat on the floor. Brace the core and keep the body relaxed. Allow the head to settle onto the roller. Slowly rotate the head to one side. Pause briefly at the end range. Rotate slowly through center to the other side.
Benefits: Releases the neck muscles.; Improves cervical rotation.; Reduces neck stiffness.; Useful for desk workers.; Joint friendly release.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Sternocleidomastoid; Trapezius; Levator scapulae

Exercise Name: Roll Posterior Shoulder Lying on Floor
Description: Lie on one side with a foam roller under the back of the shoulder. Set the bottom arm extended overhead. Stack the legs for balance. Brace the core and keep the body relaxed. Roll the back of the shoulder slowly over the roller. Pause on tender spots for several breaths. Adjust angle to cover the rear delt and infraspinatus. Continue for the working time then switch sides.
Benefits: Releases the rear shoulder.; Improves shoulder mobility.; Reduces rotator cuff tightness.; Useful for desk workers.; Joint friendly release.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Posterior deltoid; Infraspinatus; Trapezius

Exercise Name: Roll Peroneal Side Lying on Floor
Description: Lie on one side on the floor. Place a foam roller under the outer lower leg. Stack the legs or stagger them for balance. Brace the body on the bottom forearm. Keep the upper body relaxed. Roll the outer lower leg slowly along the roller. Pause on tender spots for several breaths. Cover from knee to ankle then switch sides.
Benefits: Releases the peroneals.; Improves ankle stability.; Reduces lower leg tightness.; Useful for runners.; Joint friendly release.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Calves; Tibialis anterior; Soleus

Exercise Name: Roll Middle Back Lying on Floor
Description: Lie on the back with the knees bent and feet flat. Place a foam roller across the mid back. Cross the arms over the chest or place hands behind the head. Brace the core and keep the hips lifted. Roll the mid back slowly along the roller. Pause on tender spots for several breaths. Allow the upper body to fall back over the roller for extension. Continue for the working time.
Benefits: Releases the mid back.; Improves thoracic mobility.; Useful for posture.; Reduces upper back tightness.; Joint friendly release.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Trapezius; Rhomboids; Erector spinae

Exercise Name: Roll Neck Decompress Lying on Floor
Description: Lie on the back on the floor. Place a foam roller or massage stick under the base of the skull. Bend the knees with feet flat on the floor. Brace the core and keep the body relaxed. Allow the head to settle onto the roller. Tip the head gently from side to side. Pause on tender spots for several breaths. Continue for the working time.
Benefits: Decompresses the cervical spine.; Releases neck tension.; Reduces headache risk.; Useful for desk workers.; Joint friendly release.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Sternocleidomastoid; Trapezius; Levator scapulae

Description: Place a foam roller on the floor. Lie face down with one thigh on top of the roller. Support the upper body on the forearms. Brace your core and keep the back flat. Roll the front of the thigh slowly over the roller. Stop on tight spots and hold for several seconds. Continue rolling from the hip down to the knee. Switch legs and repeat on the other thigh.
Benefits: Releases quad tightness; Useful warm-up drill; Strong recovery move; Easy to add to any session; Builds quad mobility; Releases hip flexor tension
Muscles Worked (Raw): Quadriceps; Hip flexors; Adductors

Description: Sit on the floor with both legs extended in front. Place a foam roller under your right calf. Cross your left leg over the right ankle to add downward pressure (or keep it on the floor for less intensity). Place your hands flat on the floor behind you. Press into them to lift your hips off the floor. Roll your right calf along the foam roller from just above the ankle to just below the knee. Roll slowly — about 1 inch per second. If you find a tender spot, pause and hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Rotate your foot to roll the inner and outer calf as well. Switch legs and repeat. Roll each leg for 1 to 2 minutes.
Benefits: Releases calf tightness; Improves ankle mobility; Reduces post-workout soreness; Useful for runners and lifters; Easy to do at home with a foam roller; Inexpensive equipment
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gastrocnemius; Soleus; Achilles tendon; Plantaris

Description: Place a foam roller on the floor. Lie on the side with the hip placed on the roller. Stack the hips and shoulders. Press the bottom forearm into the floor for support. Brace your core and keep the body straight. Roll slowly across the TFL on the side of the hip. Pause on tight spots and breathe. Switch to the other side and repeat.
Benefits: Releases the TFL; Improves hip mobility; Strong recovery move; Useful warm-up; Improves IT band tissue
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hip Flexors; Gluteus medius; Gluteus maximus

Description: Place a foam roller on the floor. Lie on your back with the roller positioned between your shoulder blades. Support your head with your hands behind it. Bend your knees with feet flat on the floor. Lift your hips slightly off the floor. Brace your core and breathe slowly. Slowly roll up and down through the upper back area. Hold tender spots for 20 to 30 seconds.
Benefits: Releases upper back tension; Improves thoracic mobility; Helps with desk-induced tightness; Recovery drill for upper body lifters; Improves posture; Easy to do at home
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rhomboids; Trapezius (middle); Erector spinae

Description: Place a foam roller on the floor. Get into a quadruped position with one shin over the roller. Set the front of the lower leg on top of the roller. Support the upper body on the hands. Brace your core and keep the back flat. Roll the shin slowly over the roller from below the knee to the ankle. Stop on tight spots and hold for several seconds. Switch legs and repeat on the other shin.
Benefits: Releases shin tightness; Useful for runners; Strong recovery move; Easy to add to any session; Builds lower leg mobility; Helps with shin splints
Muscles Worked (Raw): Tibialis anterior; Calves; Forearms

Description: Lie on your back. Place a foam roller horizontally under your upper back, just below your shoulder blades. Cross your arms over your chest or place hands behind your head with elbows pointing forward. Lift your hips off the floor. Slowly roll back and forth, moving the roller along your upper back from below the shoulder blades to the top of the neck. Pause on tight spots and apply sustained pressure. To extend over the roller: keep your hips down, lean back over the roller, and gently arch your upper back over it. Hold the extension for 10 to 20 seconds. Roll for 1 to 2 minutes total.
Benefits: Releases thoracic spine tightness; Improves T-spine mobility; Counteracts hunched posture; Excellent before pressing or pulling exercises; Improves breathing capacity; Inexpensive equipment
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae (thoracic); Trapezius (middle and lower); Rhomboids; Latissimus dorsi (upper); Thoracic spine joints

Exercise Name: Roll Shoulder Back Rotation Lying on Floor
Description: Lie on the back with the knees bent and feet flat. Place a foam roller under one shoulder blade at an angle. Cross the arms over the chest. Brace the core and lift the hips slightly. Rotate the torso slowly toward the working side. Reach the top arm across the body. Hold the rotated position briefly. Return to start and continue for all reps then switch.
Benefits: Mobilizes the thoracic spine.; Releases the shoulder blade.; Improves rotational mobility.; Useful warm-up.; Joint friendly drill.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Trapezius; Rhomboids; Posterior deltoid

Exercise Name: Roll Shoulder Blade Reach Lying on Floor
Description: Lie on the back with the knees bent and feet flat. Place a foam roller under the upper back at an angle. Brace the core and lift the hips slightly. Reach one arm straight overhead along the floor. Allow the shoulder blade to slide across the roller. Hold the reached position briefly. Return the arm to the side. Continue for all reps then switch sides.
Benefits: Releases the shoulder blade.; Mobilizes the lats.; Improves overhead mobility.; Useful warm-up.; Joint friendly release.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rhomboids; Latissimus dorsi; Trapezius

Description: Lie on your right side with your right arm extended forward, perpendicular to your torso. Bend your right elbow to 90 degrees so your right forearm points up toward the ceiling. Place your left hand on top of your right wrist or fingertips. Gently press your right hand toward the floor in front of you, internally rotating your right shoulder. Stop when you feel a deep stretch in the back of your right shoulder. Do not force. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch to the left side and repeat. If you feel any sharp pain, stop immediately — only a gentle stretch should be felt.
Benefits: Stretches the posterior shoulder capsule; Improves internal rotation; Helps prevent shoulder impingement; Useful for athletes in overhead sports; Counteracts pressing-dominant training imbalances; No equipment needed
Muscles Worked (Raw): Posterior shoulder capsule; Infraspinatus; Teres minor; Posterior deltoid

Description: Lie on your back with arms at your sides, palms down. Legs extended straight up toward the ceiling. Brace your core. Press your palms into the floor for support. Exhale and lift your hips off the floor, rolling your legs overhead toward the floor behind your head. If your flexibility allows, touch your toes to the floor behind your head. Do not force this. Open your legs to shoulder-width at the end position. Slowly roll back down one vertebra at a time, controlling the descent with your abdominals. Lower your legs back to the starting vertical position. Close your legs together. Repeat for 3 to 5 reps. Do not perform this exercise if you have neck issues.
Benefits: Builds spinal flexibility through full range; Develops core control during the roll-up and roll-down; Stretches the hamstrings and entire posterior chain; Teaches sequential spinal articulation; Foundational intermediate Pilates exercise; Decompresses the spine at the end range
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis (rolling control); Erector spinae (stretched); Hamstrings (stretched); Hip flexors (lifting legs overhead)

Description: Sit on the floor with knees bent and feet flat. Lean back slightly and lift your feet off the floor. Balance on your sit bones with shins parallel to the floor. Extend your arms forward at shoulder height. Brace your core hard to maintain balance. Pull your arms back as if rowing, drawing your elbows behind you. Reach your arms forward again to begin the next row. Continue the rowing motion while maintaining the boat pose throughout.
Benefits: Dynamic boat pose variation; Trains core endurance; Strong hip flexor engagement; Builds balance and stability; No equipment required; Useful for yoga and pilates flow
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis; Hip flexors; Obliques; Hamstrings

Description: Sit or stand tall with shoulders relaxed. Look straight ahead. Pull your shoulders back and down. Slowly rotate your head to the right, looking over your right shoulder. Hold for 5 to 10 seconds. Feel the stretch on the left side of your neck. Slowly return to center. Rotate to the left, looking over your left shoulder. Hold for 5 to 10 seconds. Return to center. Repeat 5 to 8 times per side. Move slowly — never force the rotation.
Benefits: Improves cervical spine rotational mobility; Relieves neck tension; Quick and accessible — works anywhere; Excellent for desk workers; No equipment needed; Counteracts screen-time stiffness
Muscles Worked (Raw): Sternocleidomastoid; Splenius capitis; Splenius cervicis; Levator scapulae; Upper trapezius

Description: Step your right foot forward into a deep lunge stance. Lower your left knee to the floor behind. Place both hands on the floor on either side of your right foot. Square your hips forward. Press your hips down and forward to feel the stretch in your left hip flexor. Keep your right knee directly above your right ankle (do not let it travel forward over the toes). For a deeper stretch, lift your left knee off the floor and straighten your right leg slightly. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch sides and repeat with the left foot forward. For variation, you can straighten the front leg and fold over it for a hamstring stretch.
Benefits: Stretches the hip flexors and hamstrings; Excellent pre-run or pre-workout warm-up; Improves hip mobility for running; No equipment needed; Quick and accessible; Practical functional stretch
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hip flexors (back leg, iliopsoas); Hamstrings (front leg, with extended variation); Quadriceps (back leg); Calves (front leg)

Description: Lie face down on the floor with hands placed beside your shoulders. Press your hands into the floor and lift your chest into a cobra position. Keep hips on the floor. From the cobra position, rotate your torso to the right, looking over your right shoulder toward your right heel. Hold the rotation for 5 to 10 seconds. Feel the deeper stretch through your left abdominal and side. Return to center cobra. Rotate to the left, looking over your left shoulder. Hold and return to center. Repeat 3 to 5 rotations per side. Move slowly with breath control.
Benefits: Stretches the abs, obliques, and chest; Mobilizes the thoracic spine through rotation; Counteracts hunched posture from sitting; Combines extension with rotation in one stretch; No equipment needed; Excellent ab counter-stretch after core training
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rectus abdominis (stretched); Obliques; Pectoralis major (stretched); Hip flexors; Thoracic spine rotators

Description: Stand or sit tall with arms at your sides. Look straight ahead. Slowly elevate (shrug) both shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as possible. Hold the elevated position for 1 to 2 seconds. Then slowly depress (pull down) both shoulders as far away from your ears as possible. Hold the depressed position for 1 to 2 seconds. Continue alternating elevation and depression for the desired reps. Move slowly with control — this is a mobility drill, not an explosive exercise. Perform 10 to 15 reps as a warm-up or shoulder mobility drill.
Benefits: Builds awareness and control of the scapulae; Mobilizes the shoulder blades; Improves shoulder positioning for pressing and pulling; Excellent shoulder warm-up; No equipment needed; Useful for rehabilitation
Muscles Worked (Raw): Upper trapezius (elevation); Lower trapezius (depression); Levator scapulae; Latissimus dorsi (depression)

Description: Lie face down on the floor with arms extended out to the sides at shoulder height (T-position). Lift your right leg slightly off the floor. Bend your right knee and bring it across your body, reaching toward your left hand. Allow your hips to rotate as your right foot crosses over to the left side. Keep your shoulders and chest pressed firmly into the floor. Continue rotating until your right foot reaches toward your left hand or as far as comfortable. Hold briefly, then return to start. Switch sides. Perform 5 to 8 reps per side.
Benefits: Improves hip rotation mobility; Develops thoracic spine rotation; Stretches the hip flexors and quads; Excellent dynamic warm-up drill; Builds body awareness; No equipment needed
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hip rotators; Quadriceps (stretched); Hip flexors (stretched); Thoracic spine rotators; Obliques

Description: Stand or sit tall with arms extended forward at shoulder height, hands clasped or palms together. Begin with neutral shoulder blades. Retract: pull your shoulder blades together by squeezing them toward your spine. Your arms will draw slightly back. Hold the retracted position for 1 to 2 seconds. Squeeze hard. Protract: push your hands forward, rounding your upper back and pushing your shoulder blades apart. Hold the protracted position for 1 to 2 seconds. Continue alternating retraction and protraction for the desired reps. Perform 10 to 15 reps as a warm-up or shoulder mobility drill.
Benefits: Builds awareness and control of the scapulae; Improves shoulder positioning for pressing and pulling; Strengthens the rhomboids and serratus anterior; Excellent shoulder warm-up; No equipment needed; Foundational shoulder rehabilitation drill
Muscles Worked (Raw): Rhomboids (retraction); Trapezius (middle fibers); Serratus anterior (protraction); Posterior deltoid

Description: Sit in a chair with both feet flat on the floor. Lift your right foot off the floor. Slowly rotate your right ankle in clockwise circles for 10 reps. Reverse and rotate counterclockwise for 10 reps. Then point your right toes forward (plantarflexion). Hold 2 seconds. Pull your right toes back toward your shin (dorsiflexion). Hold 2 seconds. Repeat the point-and-flex 8 to 10 times. Add ankle inversion (sole rolls inward) and eversion (sole rolls outward) — 5 each direction. Switch to the left foot and repeat.
Benefits: Improves ankle mobility; Stretches the calves and shins; Maintains foot and ankle health; Excellent for desk workers; Useful warm-up before running; No equipment needed
Muscles Worked (Raw): Calves (gastrocnemius, soleus); Tibialis anterior; Peroneals; Ankle stabilizers

Description: Sit on the floor with both legs extended in front. Bend one knee and place the foot flat on the floor close to the same side hip. Reach the arm on the bent knee side forward and around the bent knee. Bring the other arm behind the back and clasp the hands together. Keep the extended leg flexed and active. Inhale to lengthen the spine. Exhale and fold forward over the extended leg. Hold the pose for the desired duration then switch sides.
Benefits: Stretches the hamstrings and lower back.; Opens the shoulders and chest through the bind.; Improves seated forward fold mobility.; Calms the mind in classical yoga practice.; No equipment needed.; Excellent recovery posture.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings; Erector spinae; Posterior deltoid; Gluteus maximus

Description: Sit on the floor with both legs extended straight in front of you. Loop a towel or resistance band around the ball of your right foot. Hold both ends with your hands. Sit tall with a straight back. Brace your core gently. Pull your toes toward your shin by gently pulling on the towel. Keep your knee straight. Feel the stretch through your right calf — both the upper calf (gastrocnemius) and deep calf (soleus). Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply and relax into the stretch. Switch to the left foot and repeat. For a deeper soleus stretch, slightly bend your knee while pulling your toes toward you.
Benefits: Stretches the gastrocnemius and soleus effectively; Improves ankle dorsiflexion for better squat depth; Relieves calf tightness from running, walking, or heels; No equipment needed (towel optional); Gentle enough for daily use and rehabilitation; Useful cool-down after lower-body training
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gastrocnemius (medial and lateral heads); Soleus; Achilles tendon; Plantar fascia (secondary)

Exercise Name: Roll Thoracic Spine Lying on Floor
Description: Lie on the back with the knees bent and feet flat. Place a foam roller across the mid back. Cross the arms over the chest or place hands behind the head. Brace the core lightly and keep the hips lifted. Allow the upper body to fall back over the roller. Press the chest open into thoracic extension. Hold the extended position briefly. Roll the spine slowly along the roller.
Benefits: Mobilizes the thoracic spine.; Improves overhead mobility.; Useful for posture.; Reduces upper back tightness.; Joint friendly drill.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Trapezius; Rhomboids; Erector spinae

Description: Sit upright in a chair. Look straight ahead. Pull your chin straight back without tilting your head. Imagine making a double chin. Hold for 5 to 10 seconds. Release and relax. Repeat 10 to 15 times. Perform throughout the workday every 30 to 60 minutes. This is the most accessible posture exercise for desk workers.
Benefits: Corrects forward head posture at a desk; Can be done while sitting at work; Strengthens deep cervical flexors; No equipment needed; Quick and accessible; Prevents neck pain from desk work
Muscles Worked (Raw): Deep cervical flexors; Suboccipitals (stretched)

Description: Sit tall on the floor with the legs extended forward. Bend one leg and place the foot on the outside of the opposite knee. Set the opposite elbow on the outside of the bent knee. Brace your core lightly and keep the chest up. Rotate the torso toward the bent knee side. Use the elbow to deepen the twist. Hold the position and breathe deeply. Release back to center then switch sides.
Benefits: Mobilizes the spine; Stretches the obliques; No equipment needed; Useful warm-up stretch; Easy to add anywhere; Strong basic stretch
Muscles Worked (Raw): Obliques; Spinal erectors; Latissimus dorsi

Exercise Name: Roll Triceps Side Lying on Floor
Description: Lie on one side with a foam roller under the back of the upper arm. Set the bottom arm extended overhead. Stack the legs for balance. Brace the body on the bottom forearm. Keep the upper body relaxed over the roller. Roll the triceps slowly along the roller. Pause on tender spots for several breaths. Cover the full upper arm then switch sides.
Benefits: Releases the triceps.; Reduces upper arm tightness.; Improves elbow mobility.; Useful after pressing work.; Joint friendly release.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Triceps brachii; Anconeus; Latissimus dorsi

Description: Sit tall on a bench or chair with feet flat on the floor. Place both hands behind your head with fingers interlaced. Brace your core lightly. Pull the elbows out wide to the sides. Open the chest fully as the elbows go wide. Feel the stretch through the chest and front shoulders. Hold the open position and breathe deeply. Release back to the start.
Benefits: Stretches the chest; Opens the front shoulders; No equipment needed; Useful posture stretch; Easy to add anywhere; Strong basic chest opener
Muscles Worked (Raw): Pectoralis major; Anterior deltoid; Biceps brachii

Description: Sit on a chair or bench with the back tall. Cross one ankle over the opposite knee. Place the hand of the lifted leg on its knee. Brace your core and keep the chest up. Press the lifted knee gently down toward the floor. Lean forward at the hips for a deeper stretch. Hold the stretch in the glute and hip. Release with control. Finish then switch sides.
Benefits: Stretches the glutes; Mobilizes the hips; Strong figure four stretch; Useful for desk workers; Builds hip range
Muscles Worked (Raw): Gluteus maximus; Hip Flexors; Gluteus medius

Description: Sit tall on a chair or the floor with the shoulders relaxed. Place the hands on the lap. Inhale and slowly tip the chin down toward the chest. Feel a stretch along the back of the neck. Hold for a moment then return to neutral. Exhale and tilt the head back to look up at the ceiling. Feel a stretch along the front of the neck. Return to neutral and repeat for the desired duration.
Benefits: Mobilizes the neck through flexion and extension.; Reduces tension from desk work.; No equipment needed.; Easy to perform anywhere.; Improves overall neck range of motion.; Excellent recovery between training sessions.
Muscles Worked (Raw): Trapezius; Sternocleidomastoid; Levator scapulae; Scalene

Description: Sit on a chair with feet flat on the floor. Keep the back upright and chest up. Brace your core lightly. Slide one foot forward keeping the heel down. Drive the knee forward over the toes as the foot slides. Feel the stretch through the back of the ankle. Slide the foot back to the start. Continue the slide pattern then switch feet.
Benefits: Mobilizes the ankle; Builds dorsiflexion range; No equipment needed; Useful warm-up drill; Easy to add anywhere; Strong basic mobility move
Muscles Worked (Raw): Calves; Tibialis anterior; Soleus

Description: Sit on the floor with both legs extended in front of you. Bend your left knee and bring the sole of your left foot against the inside of your right thigh. Sit up tall. Reach both arms overhead. Hinge forward at the hips over your right (extended) leg, keeping your back flat. Reach for your right foot, ankle, or shin — wherever you can comfortably reach. Feel the deep stretch through your right hamstring and calf. Keep your right foot flexed (toes pointing up). Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch sides.
Benefits: Deeply stretches the hamstring of the extended leg; Stretches the calf and lower back; Calming and restorative; No equipment needed; Single-leg approach reveals asymmetries; Foundational hamstring stretch
Muscles Worked (Raw): Hamstrings (extended leg); Gastrocnemius and soleus; Erector spinae; Adductors (bent leg)

Description: Sit upright on a chair with both feet flat on the floor. Cross your right ankle over your left knee, just above the kneecap. Flex your right foot. Sit tall with chest lifted. Lean forward from the hips with a flat back. Place your hands on your right shin or thigh. Gently press your right knee down for a deeper stretch in the glute and outer hip. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply. Switch sides and repeat. The stretch should be in the glute, not the knee — reduce depth if you feel knee pain.
Benefits: Practical office and desk-friendly glute stretch; Stretches the piriformis and gluteus maximus; Relieves sciatic tension; No equipment needed beyond a chair; Improves hip external rotation; Gentle enough for daily use
Muscles Worked (Raw): Piriformis; Gluteus maximus and medius; Deep hip external rotators

Description: Sit on the edge of a chair with feet flat on the floor, slightly wider than shoulder-width. Sit up tall with chest lifted. Slowly fold forward at the hips, letting your torso drop between your knees. Let your arms hang toward the floor or rest on your shins. Let your head hang heavy. Allow gravity to decompress your spine. Feel the gentle stretch through your lower back and posterior chain. Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply. Slowly roll up to seated, vertebra by vertebra.
Benefits: Decompresses the lower back gently; Stretches the entire spine; Practical for office settings; No equipment needed beyond a chair; Relieves daily back tension; Calming and grounding
Muscles Worked (Raw): Erector spinae (lower back); Hamstrings (slight); Gluteus maximus; Quadratus lumborum

Description: Sit on the floor with legs extended. Bend both knees and bring the soles of your feet together. Let your knees drop out to the sides toward the floor. Pull your heels as close to your groin as comfortable. Hold your feet with both hands. Sit up tall with chest lifted. Feel the stretch through your inner thighs and groin. To deepen the stretch, gently press your knees toward the floor with your elbows. For an even deeper stretch, fold forward from the hips with a flat back. Reach your forehead toward your feet. Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply. Avoid forcing your knees down — let gravity do the work over time.
Benefits: Stretches the adductors and groin; Opens the hips for squats and wide-stance lifts; Improves hip flexibility over time; Calming and restorative pose; No equipment needed; Useful for athletes in sports with lateral movement
Muscles Worked (Raw): Adductor magnus, longus, brevis; Gracilis; Pectineus; Hip rotators; Lower back (with forward fold)
